title: GP
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic Salaried GP to join our friendly, community-focused practice. The role involves delivering high-quality, patient-centred care, including routine consultations, management of acute and chronic conditions, and preventative healthcare.

You will work as part of a supportive multidisciplinary team and contribute to the continued development of practice services. Opportunities to develop clinical interests, participate in teaching, and engage in quality improvement are encouraged.

We offer a positive working environment with a strong emphasis on teamwork, professional development, and work-life balance, with flexibility considered..

  • Provide General Medical Services in accordance with the GMS contract

  • Undertake surgery consultations, telephone and online consultations

  • Diagnose and manage patients presenting with acute and chronic conditions

  • Prescribe safely and appropriately in line with practice and national guidelines

  • Process and action laboratory results, clinical correspondence, and referrals

  • Maintain accurate, contemporaneous clinical records

  • Participate in practice meetings, clinical governance, audit, and quality improvement activities

  • Work collaboratively as part of the multidisciplinary team

  • Contribute to the training and supervision of medical and allied health professionals where appropriate

Borth Surgery is a purpose-built Health Centre, established in 1995, located on the main street of Borth, a charming coastal village nestled in the heart of Cardigan Bay. We are a highly community-focused practice, committed to delivering compassionate, patient-centred care while fostering strong relationships with our local population.

Our modern premises offer excellent facilities, including two large rear car parks with designated disabled spaces, ensuring easy access for patients and staff. The practice serves a wide and diverse area, from Penparcau in the south to Furnace in the north, and across to Ponterwyd in the east.

We have a friendly and experienced multidisciplinary team comprising a GP Partner, a Salaried GP, two Practice Nurses, a Healthcare Assistant, and a District Nursing team, supported by a proactive Practice Manager and skilled administrative staff. We pride ourselves on a supportive and collaborative working environment.

In addition to providing a full range of general practice services, we run specialist clinics in Respiratory Care, Diabetes, and Cardiovascular Disease. We are also an established training practice, supporting a range of learners, and host a Coding Hub delivering services to practices across Wales.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist General Adult (ADHD) - Substantive
descriptionHtml:
Atrom Mindcare RTC is seeking an experienced Consultant Psychiatrist in General Adult Psychiatry to join our expanding Adult ADHD Service.

The post-holder will play a key role in delivering high-quality diagnostic assessments, formulation, and management plans for adults presenting with ADHD and related comorbidities. This is a flexible, hybrid role suited to a motivated clinician with a strong interest in neurodevelopmental disorders and modern, patient-centred models of care.

About Atrom Mindcare RTC Adult ADHD Service

Atrom Mindcare is a Private Holistic Psychiatric Clinic located in Epping on the border of North East London and Essex. Atrom Mindcare deliver a range of Adult Psychiatric treatments including Deep TMS and Psychological therapies and Psychiatric Assessments. This post is to recruit for the growing demand for its Adult ADHD pathway under NHS Right to Choose to deliver evidence-based care to adults with ADHD. Our vision is to ensure timely, high-quality assessments and person-centred treatment pathways for all service users.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist Inpatient & Community Forensics
descriptionHtml:
Your expertise can change lives.At Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, we believe in care that goes beyond treatment--it's about compassion, respect, and trust. If you're ready to make a real difference, we'd love you to join us as a Consultant Forensic Psychiatrist in ourLow Secure and Community Forensic Directorate.

This is an opportunity to work at the heart of our community, supporting people through their recovery journey and helping them build brighter futures. You'll be part of a team that values collaboration, innovation, and inclusion, delivering care across a range of specialist services:

  • Community Forensic Service
  • Inpatient services at Wells Road Centre

Why You'll Love Working With Us

  • Our Values in Action: We put people first--patients and colleagues alike. Compassion and respect aren't just words; they're how we work every day.
  • Support That Matters: From structured mentoring for new consultants to a strong peer network, you'll never feel alone in your role.
  • Flexibility: Full-time is ideal, but we're open to conversations about flexible working.
  • Growth Opportunities: Access our academic programme, CPD sessions, and annual appraisals to keep your skills sharp and your career moving forward.

For an informal chat or visit, contact:

Dr Abdul Shaikh, Clinical Director? abdul.shaikh@nottshc.nhs.uk | ? 0115 969 1300

Apply now and help us shape the future of forensic mental health care in Nottinghamshire.

What Your Role Looks Like

The post-holder will have consultant responsibilities for a caseload of up to 14 in inpatient and 8 community-based patients. Some of these patients will be subject to Mental Health Act (MHA) provisions (conditionally discharged, guardianship or CTO). Care co-ordination is provided by community psychiatric nurses, occupational therapists or mental health practitioners. You will have specific consultant responsibility predominantly for patients across Nottinghamshire.

Day-to-day, you'll:

  • Provide high-quality, evidence-based care to patients in the community and in an inpatient setting.
  • Work closely with multidisciplinary teams to ensure safe, effective treatment.
  • Take part in service development and academic programmes.
  • Uphold professional standards and contribute to the efficient running of services.

#TeamNottsHC comprises over 11,000 dedicated colleagues who #MakeADifference every day. We deliver intellectual disability, mental health, community health, forensic, and offender healthcare services across Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire, Lincolnshire, and South Yorkshire. Our care is provided from over 200 sites, spanning community locations, acute settings, and secure environments, including prisons.

We are one of the largest mental health and community Trusts in the East Midlands and one of Nottinghamshire's biggest employers. We also host national and regional services, such as the National High Secure Deaf Service and the Nottingham Centre for Transgender Health.

We offer a variety of employee-led staff networks, including Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) groups, the Green Champions network, the Freedom to Speak Up network, the Health and Wellbeing Champions network, and the Menopause Champions network.

The health and wellbeing of our colleagues is a top priority. We invest significantly in this through our in-house occupational health and staff counselling services, supported by a dedicated Health and Wellbeing team.

The Trust is committed to reducing its carbon emissions, with a specialised Energy and Environmental team working to ensure compliance with environmental legislation, enhance our environmental performance, and achieve our net-zero commitment.

title: General Practitioner (GP)
descriptionHtml:
The primary focus for this role is to help deliver safe and effective patient care to registered patients across DMC Primary care. You will be responsible for the provision of medical services to the practice population, delivering an excellent standard of clinical care whilst complying with the [GMS/PMS] contract. Furthermore, the post-holder will adhere to the GMC standards for good medical practice, contributing to the effective management of the practice, leading by example, maintaining a positive, collaborative working relationship with the multidisciplinary team.

The delivery of effective medical care to the entitled population. Provision of services in line with the GMS contract. Generic prescribing in accordance with local and national guidance. Effective management of long-term conditions using CESEL guidelines. Timely processing of administration, including referrals, repeat prescriptions and related tasks. On a rotational basis, undertake telephone triage and duty doctor responsibilities. Maintain accurate clinical records in line with best practice, policy and guidance. Work collaboratively, sharing an equal proportion of the practice workload. Adhere to clinical guidelines and participate in audit processes. Contribute to continuous improvement and quality initiatives within the practice. Accept delegated responsibility for specific areas, including QOF. Attend and contribute effectively to practice meetings. Support the development and maintenance of the practice, including clinical governance, training, financial management and HR. Ensure compliance with appraisal and revalidation. Commit to ongoing professional development and promote learning across the practice team. Support the training of medical students. Assist partners in achieving strategic objectives, making recommendations to improve income and reduce costs. Adhere to practice protocols and policies. Promote collaborative working and a culture of continuous improvement. Participate in practice audits, local initiatives to enhance service delivery.

DMC Healthcare is a leading independent provider of primary care, consultant-led dermatology, radiology reporting, in-sourced routine endoscopy services and MSK community services to the NHS.We believe that everyone should have the opportunity to achieve healthier outcomes.Firmly rooted in the NHS and dedicated to excellent patient care for nearly 55 years, DMC Healthcare currently works with 30+ NHS organisations and other partners, treating over 100,000* patients each year.With NHS waiting list pressures, workforce shortages and unprecedented demand, we want to help. We support capacity deficits with a firm eye on quality and robust clinical governance.Find out more:https://dmchealthcare.co.uk

employer: Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist, CYPS, Aldershot (attracts £25K RRP)
descriptionHtml:
Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust is a General Medical Council (GMC) Sponsor Employer.

This job attracts a Recruitment and Retention payment of £25,000 in addition to £8000 relocation allowance. The RRP is pro rata for part time employees.

We are looking for a Consultant Psychiatrist to join our Community Children and Young People's (CYPS) Mental Health Team in North East Hampshire, based at the Aldershot Centre for Health.

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a well-established, welcoming, and multi-skilled team that supports the mental health and wellbeing of children and young people aged 5 to 18. Our service provides specialist assessments, evidence-based treatments and ongoing support for young people with a range of emotional, behavioural, and complex mental health needs.

You'll provide clinical leadership and direct psychiatric input as part of a multidisciplinary team that includes psychologists, nurses, therapists, and support workers. You'll work with schools, GPs, local authorities and other partners to ensure coordinated and person-centred care. The team also has strong links to our Eating Disorder Service, Crisis Intervention and Early Intervention in Psychosis teams.

You'll be joining a Trust committed to early intervention, prevention, and supporting young people to thrive. If you're passionate about improving outcomes for children and families, we'd love to hear from you!

You'll have the opportunity of working within a well-established and friendly team of highly skilled professionals who are passionate and committed to the care needs of our children and young people.

You would be responsible for providing a diagnostic, assessment and treatment service for children and adolescents with mental health problems within a multi-disciplinary approach to care, promoting high-quality multidisciplinary working and relationships. On average, a full-time consultant would complete 2-3 monthly assessments. Patients have a consultant review after 6 weeks of treatment in the team and then every 2-3 months.

You will participate in an emergency out-of-hours rota, providing back-up for junior doctors and professionals in assessing young people seen in A&E.

You'll have opportunities to support, supervise and train our Junior Medical Staff within the team.

Our Offer:

  • NHS Consultant grade £113,565 - £150,569 per annum + £149 fringe + on- call requirement
  • GMC Sponsorship
  • Recruitment premia £25,000 *subject to policy requirements
  • Relocation allowance: up to £8000 *subject to policy requirement
  • Sponsorship for International candidates
  • Up to £2000/year CPD allowance *subject to policy requirements
  • NHS pension employers contribution 23.7% from day one
  • Company Car Lease Scheme
  • Discounted Nuffield Gym Membership and many more.

Please check our benefits here:Medical : Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust for other benefits.

Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust is the leading provider of health and social care services for people of all ages with mental ill-health and learning disabilities in Surrey and North East Hampshire. We also provide social care services for people with a learning disability in Croydon and ASD and ADHD assessment services in Hampshire.

We actively seek to engage people who use our services and our communities in improving the mental wellbeing of the local population. We work closely with other NHS and voluntary sector organisations who provide services and support people who use services and carers.

Surrey is a beautiful county lying just 30 minutes away from Central London and from the South Coast.

Our historic market towns and bustling districts are enveloped in wonderful countryside, and our excellent road and rail networks bring the rest of the country within easy reach.

For international travel, both Gatwick and Heathrow airports are nearby.

Please note that we reserve the right to close posts as soon as sufficient applications are received.

We look forward to receiving your application!

title: Salaried GP - UCN
descriptionHtml:
At DHU Healthcare, every role matters. Were a not-for-profit team driven by compassion and respect, where your voice is heard and your growth truly matters. Join us and be part of something bigger. For you, for them, with us.

Shaping the future of care.

At DHU Healthcare, our Urgent and Emergency Care teams work on the frontline of the NHS, delivering expert, compassionate care 24/7, 365 days a year. From Emergency Departments and Urgent Treatment Centres to GP surgeries and communities across the East Midlands and beyond, were there when people need us most.

Our teams of skilled medical, nursing, allied health, and support professionals all work together to respond quickly and effectively to every patient. We deliver a wide range of services including community nursing, urgent treatment, primary care streaming, urgent on-day primary care, GP home visiting, phlebotomy, community hospital medical cover, telephone consultation support, and palliative care home visiting. With us, youll be supported to succeed - in your role, your development, and your career.

Every patient journey relies on skilled clinicians delivering safe, high quality care. Your expertise helps us meet urgent needs and improve outcomes.

As a Salaried GP you will:

  • Assess, diagnose and manage patients presenting with urgent undifferentiated illness and minor injury presentations in line with UTC scope, competence and local pathways.
  • Undertake clinical history taking, physical examination and clinical decision making using evidence based practice.
  • Request, interpret and act on appropriate investigations available within the UTC setting, including point of care tests, ECGs and imaging where available and authorised.
  • Maintain full GMC registration, licence to practise and inclusion on the Performers List.
  • Maintain appraisal, revalidation, mandatory training and professional development requirements.

We offer a benefits package with your health, happiness and future in mind. You'll have access to the NHS pension scheme (and well honour your existing NHS pension pot and holiday entitlement if transferring), free parking at most sites, birthday leave, and our Health Cash Plan for you and your family covering dental, optical, therapy costs, and 24/7 GP access after six months.

Plus, wellbeing perks, flexible working, a salary sacrifice Car Lease Scheme with low-emission options, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, and a rewarding referral programme. It's our way of saying thank you.

Learning, leading, shaping healthcare

At DHU Healthcare, we support your growth at every stage of your career. With career paths, tailored training, and the DHU Academy, you'll have the tools and encouragement to explore skills and opportunities, take the next step, and make an impact. From leadership programmes and apprenticeships to essential role-specific training, development is part of how we work and shape healthcare together.

A culture where differences matter.

We believe that when everyone feels valued respected and supported, they can do their best work. We're proud to reflect the rich diversity of the communities we serve, welcoming colleagues from all backgrounds. We are committed to supporting the Armed Forces community and, as a Disability Confident Employer, we welcome candidates to share any support or reasonable adjustments they may need during the recruitment process.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist in Older Adults
descriptionHtml:
Priory Hospital Dewsbury is looking for a Consultant Psychiatrist in Older Adults (or General Adult Psychiatrist with experience in managing Older Adults).

Flexible hours up to 37.5 hours per week.

Competitive Salary and package.

Service rated Good CQC.

Based in the residential area of Earlsheaton, Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, Priory Hospital Dewsbury provides 32 beds, divided into two 16-bed wards for males who have mental health disorders. Hartley Ward is a level 2 Rehabilitation and Recovery Ward (Higher Support Needs). Jubilee Ward is an Older Adult service. Each service has a dedicated Consultant Psychiatrist who performs the duties of Responsible Clinician.

The available post is for Jubilee Ward (10 bedded Specialist Dementia Service, and 6 bedded Functional Disorders).

An excellent opportunity for somebody looking to join an established team caring for individuals with Dementia. Jubilee Ward is a 16 bedded male unit which provides a therapeutic environment for men with dementia (10 beds) and Functional Disorders (6 beds). Most patients are under MHA. The Consultant will work closely with other experienced members of the MDT. The post would be suitable for an Older Adult Consultant Psychiatrist or a General Adult Psychiatrist, with experience of older adults.

Physical health input is provided by the on-site Specialist Physical Health Nurse and visiting GP.

We want you to succeed at Priory and thrive in your role. You will be well supported with regular career conversations. We also offer full training and numerous pathways into leadership and qualified clinical positions to help you shape your career with us. 

-        Negotiable, flexible hours.

-        Competitive Independent Sector salary and package.

-        Peer Group of Doctors that are supportive.

-        Generous study leave (including funding).

-        Generous annual leave and birthday leave.

-        Supplemented meals.

-        Car parking

-        Dedicated office with full admin support, and laptop and mobile phone for remote working.

-        Priory Benefit Package (including private health insurance, salary sacrifice car scheme plus other benefits and discounts).

-        Employee Assistance Program.

-        Pension Scheme.

-        Support for CPD and a mentorship programme for medical staff new to the independent sector or to Priory.

Due to the large size of the company there are excellent career progression opportunities.

Shortlisting may begin upon receipt of applications, and the Recruiting Manager may close the vacancy early if enough suitable candidates are identified.

Priory is the UKs leading independent provider of mental health and adult social care. With 12,000 colleagues and a network of 270 services, we support over 24,000 people each year to live their lives as fully and independently as possible. We treat more than 70 conditions including depression, anxiety, eating disorders and childrens mental health and provide residential and supported living care for autistic adults, people with a learning disability, PraderWilli Syndrome, brain injuries and older people.

We are an equal opportunities employer committed to providing an inclusive, accessible recruitment process. Learn more about the accessibility support we offer here.

For agency enquiries and applications, please view our legal statement here.

All roles are subject to a successful disclosure at an appropriate level from the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS), Access NI or Disclosure Scotland. Priory will cover the cost of a DBS check.

title: Consultant in GA Psych - Broxtowe & Hucknall LMHT & EIP + Golden Hello
descriptionHtml:

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Hilltop Medical Practice is seeking an enthusiastic and committed Salaried GP (4 sessions per week) to join our progressive, patient-centred team in Brent. This is an exciting opportunity for a motivated clinician who is passionate about delivering high-quality primary care and working within a supportive, forward-thinking environment.

The role is funded through the NHS GP Reimbursement Scheme and offers the opportunity to work with a vibrant and culturally diverse patient population. You will become part of a collaborative multidisciplinary team that is dedicated to improving health outcomes, reducing inequalities, and delivering accessible healthcare services tailored to the needs of our community.

We are committed to supporting our clinicians through effective administrative systems, a strong team ethos, and opportunities for ongoing professional development. Whether you are looking to broaden your experience in general practice, develop specialist interests, or contribute to service improvement initiatives, this role provides an excellent platform to do so.

The post is available on a fixed-term basis until 31 March 2027, subject to current NHS funding arrangements. However, extension may be possible by mutual agreement. We welcome applications from GPs who share our commitment to clinical excellence, compassion, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

The successful candidate will provide comprehensive primary care services to registered patients through a combination of face-to-face, telephone, and digital consultations. You will assess, diagnose, and manage a wide range of acute and long-term conditions while supporting patients to make informed decisions about their health and wellbeing.

You will work closely with our multidisciplinary team, including nurses, pharmacists, social prescribers, care coordinators, and administrative colleagues, to ensure patients receive coordinated and effective care. The role also involves reviewing clinical correspondence, laboratory results, medication management, and maintaining accurate clinical records using EMIS Web.

As part of the practice team, you will contribute to safeguarding responsibilities, clinical governance activities, quality improvement projects, and service development initiatives. There will be opportunities to participate in practice meetings, educational activities, and the ongoing development of services that support the needs of our local population.We are committed to supporting professional development and actively encourage candidates to develop additional skills and areas of expertise that will enhance both their career progression and the services we provide to our patients.

The role requires excellent communication, sound clinical judgement, and a commitment to delivering safe, efficient, and patient-centred care.

Hilltop Medical Practice is a well-established, friendly, and welcoming GP practice serving a diverse and growing community in Brent. We pride ourselves on providing high-quality, compassionate healthcare while maintaining a strong focus on accessibility, inclusion, and patient experience. Practice has recently been rated as 'Good' by CQC.

Our multidisciplinary team includes experienced GPs, nurses, pharmacists, social prescribers, care coordinators, and dedicated administrative staff who work collaboratively to support patients and one another. We have created a positive working environment where teamwork, mutual respect, and open communication are highly valued.

We are committed to the professional development and wellbeing of our staff and encourage continuous learning, innovation, and service improvement. Team members benefit from flexible working arrangements, supportive leadership, modern clinical systems, and opportunities to develop clinical or non-clinical interests.

At Hilltop Medical Practice, we recognise that our people are our greatest asset. We strive to create a workplace where individuals feel valued, supported, and empowered to provide the very best care to the communities we serve.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and committed Salaried GP to join our team in an exciting and varied role working across several practices within the Primary Care Network (PCN), alongside sessions at a related practice in Scunthorpe. This is a dynamic opportunity for a GP who enjoys collaborative working, portfolio variety, and delivering high-quality patient care across multiple settings. The role will also include participation in Extended Access GP cover and provision of PCN GP cover during training afternoons, supporting service resilience and continuity across the network. This post offers the opportunity to work as part of a supportive multidisciplinary team while contributing to innovative, patient-centred primary care delivery.

The Salaried GP will provide high-quality, patient-centred primary care across several practices within the PCN and a related practice in Scunthorpe. Duties include undertaking routine and urgent consultations, managing acute and chronic conditions, prescribing, and maintaining accurate clinical records. The role will contribute to Extended Access services, provide GP cover during PCN training afternoons, support multidisciplinary team working, participate in clinical meetings and quality improvement activity, and work collaboratively to deliver safe, effective, and responsive care to the practice populations.

Apollo PCN is a collaborative Primary Care Network bringing together member practices to deliver joined-up, high-quality primary care for the local population. Working in partnership with practices and wider health and care services, Apollo PCN supports innovative, patient-centred care through shared workforce models, multidisciplinary working, extended access services, and the development of services that improve access, resilience, and outcomes for patients. The PCN is committed to collaboration, continuous improvement, and supporting the delivery of sustainable general practice across the network.

title: Full Time GP
descriptionHtml:
Join Our Forward-Thinking GP Practice in London. Were looking for an exceptional General Practitioner to become an integral part of our thriving NHS practice. This role offers the perfect blend of clinical excellence and career growth in a supportive, collaborative environment. As a valued member of our team, you will shape patient care, mentor future healthcare professionals, and develop special clinical interests. With structured career progression, leadership opportunities, and a strong focus on work-life balance, this is a role that allows you to thrive while making a meaningful impact.

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis and suitable candidates may be invited to interview before the advertised closing date. The organisation reserves the right to close this vacancy early should sufficient suitable applications be received.

You will also oversee chronic disease management, and maintain high standards in patient care. The role includes mentorship of junior staff, involvement in clinical teaching, and opportunities to lead quality improvement initiatives. Administrative excellence and adherence to clinical governance frameworks are vital to ensure high-quality service delivery.

Our modern and innovative GP practice in London combines the best aspects of traditional general practice with cutting-edge approaches to healthcare delivery. We are a dynamic team committed to clinical excellence and continuous improvement. Our collaborative culture fosters professional growth, with opportunities to mentor junior doctors, develop special interests, and take on leadership roles. We prioritise work-life balance, offer structured career progression, and provide robust professional support, including protected CPD time and mentorship programs. Join us to advance your career in a practice that values excellence and innovation.

title: PCN GP
descriptionHtml:
Are you looking for more than just a salaried GP role?

Would you like to join a friendly, forward-thinking practice where you can develop your career, enjoy genuine work-life balance, and potentially progress to a future GP Partnership?

Guildhall Surgery is seeking an enthusiastic and motivated GP to join our supportive clinical team for 6 sessions per week. This is an exciting opportunity to become part of a well-established practice with an excellent reputation for patient care, education and staff wellbeing.

Why Join Us?

At Guildhall Surgery, we believe that providing excellent patient care starts with looking after our team. We have built a collaborative, supportive culture where GPs enjoy working together, sharing knowledge and supporting one another.

We offer:

  • A competitive salary with a strong commitment to work-life balance.
  • A welcoming, experienced and highly supportive multidisciplinary team.
  • Daily opportunities to meet informally with colleagues over coffee to discuss cases, share ideas and support one another.
  • Regular peer support meetings to review complex cases and promote continuous learning.
  • An established teaching practice, training GP Registrars and medical students from the University of Cambridge and the University of East Anglia.

  • Strong relationships with community services, including monthly multidisciplinary meetings with community providers, mental health services, social care and voluntary organisations.
  • A commitment to continuing professional development, with training and personal development actively encouraged and supported.

West Rural Suffolk Primary Care Network, based in West Suffolk, is comprised of Wickhambrook Surgery, Guildhall Clare Surgery and Glemsford surgery. We are a small, rural primary care network, with a combined patient population of around 16,000. All practices work on SystmOne.

title: Salaried General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
All Saints Surgery is a friendly, single site practice in Burton On Trent, caring for around 11,000 patients as part of East Staffordshire Primary Care. We are looking for an enthusiastic salaried GP to join our team and help us strengthen capacity for patients, with a particular focus on supporting timely same-day urgent care alongside good continuity for those who need it most.

This is a genuinely additional post created to expand our clinical capacity, so you would be adding to the team rather than replacing a colleague. You will work alongside 2 GP partners, 1 salaried GPs, our nursing team and a wider multidisciplinary team that includes clinical pharmacists, first contact physiotherapists, social prescribers and care coordinators. We use EMIS Web and offer a supportive environment with protected time, regular clinical meetings and a real commitment to a manageable, sustainable workload.

We would be happy to talk to GPs at any stage of their career, including those recently qualified, those returning to practice, and experienced GPs looking for a settled salaried role. We can be flexible on sessions and working pattern for the right person, and we welcome an informal chat or visit before you apply.

Provide consultations to patients attending the surgery, by telephone and online clinically appropriate.

Take a share of duty doctor and same-day urgent access sessions, triaging and managing acute presentations safely.

Assess, diagnose and treat patients across the full range of general practice, making appropriate referrals to secondary care and other services.

Prescribe safely and cost effectively in line with practice and ICB formulary guidance, and contribute to medicines optimisation and repeat prescribing.

Review and action investigation results, clinical correspondence and documents in a timely way.

Contribute to the ongoing management of patients with long term conditions and to delivery of the Quality and Outcomes Framework and local and enhanced services.

Maintain accurate, contemporaneous and coded records using EMIS Web

Recognise and act on safeguarding concerns for children and adults at risk in line with practice policy and statutory duties.

At All Saints Surgery you will join a close, supportive team where people genuinely look out for one another. Our GPs, nurses, pharmacists and wider clinical and administrative colleagues work side by side, share knowledge openly and help each other through the busy days. New starters tell us they feel welcome from day one.

The atmosphere is calm, friendly and grounded. We protect time for a proper coffee and a chat as well as for clinical meetings, and we take workload and wellbeing seriously, so you can do good work without feeling stretched too thin. Decisions are made together and your ideas will be heard, whatever your stage of career.

You will have a manageable, well-organised list, protected administrative time and generous study leave to support your development, appraisal and revalidation, plus the NHS Pension Scheme and the day-to-day backing of experienced colleagues and a strong multidisciplinary team. We are happy to be flexible on sessions and working patterns to fit life outside work. WE offer free parking.

Above all, this is a place that values kindness, continuity and good medicine. If you want to work somewhere you are trusted, supported and able to build real relationships with patients and colleagues, we would love to hear from you.

employer: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Radiologist
descriptionHtml:
The Royal Devon is seeking to appoint a Consultant in Radiology to our services based at the Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital.

With the development of the Community Diagnostics Centre and a range of one-stop clinics, alongside an increase in demand across Medical Imaging services, we are looking to appoint Consultant Radiologists to join our friendly, successful and ambitious team.

Specialist interests are strongly encouraged. Participation in multidisciplinary team meetings is expected and the successful applicants will be part of the registrar supported on-call for general radiology (currently 1 in 16).

We are based in the South West of England, in a county renowned for its natural beauty, sc

For more detail about the main duties of this role, please see the job description section below. As a key member of the Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, you will be joining an exceptional team working together to help our patients to stay healthy, when they need it most.

Stretching across Northern, Eastern and Mid Devon, we have a workforce of over 15,000 staff, making us the largest employer in Devon. Our core services, which we provide to more than 615,000 people, cover more than 2,000 square miles across Devon, while some of our specialist services cover the whole of the peninsula, extending our reach as far as Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly.

We deliver a wide range of emergency, specialist and general medical services through North Devon District Hospital and the Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital (Wonford).

Alongside our two acute hospitals, we provide integrated health and social care services across a variety of settings, including community inpatient hospitals, outpatient clinics, and within peoples own homes. We also offer primary care services, a range of specialist community services, and Sexual Assault Referral Centres (SARC).

Our state-of-the-art equipment, leading technologies and strong links to local universities put us at the forefront of research and innovations, enabling us to provide world-class care to our local communities.

Its never been a more exciting time to join the Royal Devon, as youll help to shape our services as we continue along our integration journey.

title: Ambulance Care Assistant (bank)
descriptionHtml:
Join our dedicated emergency CQC registered response team as an Ambulance Care Assistant/Driver, where you'll play a vital role in delivering compassionate patient care and ensuring safe transportation to healthcare facilities. This dynamic position combines the responsibilities of providing essential support to paramedics, first responders and patients with the crucial task of driving ambulance vehicles efficiently and safely. Your energetic approach and commitment to safety will help us deliver timely, professional medical assistance in diverse situations, making a real difference in people's lives every day.

We are looking for people to join our bank and are ideally able to commit to one shift per week (min 4 hours). You must be able to start work from the Ambulance Station at Malton, and be prepared to travel anywhere in the UK.

Duties

  • Safely operate ambulance vehicles, adhering to all traffic laws and safety protocols, while maintaining a high standard of driving professionalism.
  • Assist paramedics with patient handling, including lifting, transferring, and securing patients on stretchers or wheelchairs.
  • Provide compassionate support to patients during transit, ensuring their comfort and dignity are maintained at all times.
  • Conduct routine vehicle maintenance checks, including fluid levels, tire pressure, and safety equipment, reporting any issues promptly.
  • Communicate clearly and effectively with team members, emergency services, and patients to coordinate smooth operations.
  • Support the loading and unloading of medical equipment and supplies necessary for patient care.
  • Maintain accurate records of journeys, patient details, and vehicle inspections in compliance with organisational policies.

YorMed Limited is an independent ambulance, patient transport and event medical services provider based in North Yorkshire, delivering professional, reliable and patient-focused services across the UK.

Why Work With YorMed?

At YorMed, we believe that the quality of our service starts with the people who deliver it. We are committed to building a professional, supportive and dependable team of ambulance and event medical personnel who share our focus on excellent patient care.

Varied opportunities including patient transport, ambulance work and medical cover at a wide range of events.

Flexible working our bank and casual opportunities can work well alongside other employment and existing commitments.

Professional standards our patient transport services operate within a CQC-regulated environment, with a strong emphasis on governance, safeguarding, infection prevention, patient dignity and safety.

A supportive team environment as an independent provider, we value good communication and develop positive working relationships with our crews.

Opportunities to use your skills whether you are working in patient transport or providing medical support at an event, you will have the opportunity to put your training and experience into practice.

Clear compliance standards we take recruitment and compliance seriously and require appropriate qualifications, competencies, DBS checks and supporting documentation before personnel are approved for deployment.

title: Salaried General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a salaried GP to join our established team working between 4 and 8 sessions per week.

In general the post-holder will be expected to undertake all the normal duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care namely:

  • In person consultations.
  • Telephone consultations.
  • Visiting patients at home and in nursing homes.
  • Checking and signing repeat prescriptions.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - EDU
descriptionHtml:
Priory Hospital Cheadle Royal

Full Time | 37.5 hours | Site Based

£170,000

Applicants must hold MRCPsych (or an equivalent qualification), a CCT (or equivalent) and be included on the GMC Specialist Register, along with Section 12(2) approval and Approved Clinician status. Candidates should also have evidence of ongoing continuous professional development.

We have an opportunity for a Consultant Psychiatrist to join our team at Priory Hospital Cheadle. Working on our EDU ward, this is an excellent role for a Psychiatrist.

The primary purpose of this role is to deliver outstanding clinical care to patients referred to the hospital, ensuring they receive compassionate, evidence-based treatment tailored to their individual needs. Working closely with multidisciplinary teams, you will help provide holistic, person-centred care that supports recovery, wellbeing, and positive long-term outcomes.

You will take clinical responsibility for a defined patient caseload, leading key aspects of care delivery, including multidisciplinary ward rounds, risk assessments and reviews, strategic care planning, and the development of a safe, therapeutic, and recovery-focused environment.

As part of your responsibilities, you will also fulfil the role of Responsible Clinician for patients detained under the Mental Health Act 1983, providing clinical leadership and ensuring the highest standards of care, governance, and legal compliance.

You can find additional information in the attached job description.

Set within picturesque landscaped gardens in Stockport, Priory Hospital Cheadle Royal offers a range of comprehensive inpatient mental health services for young people and adults. The focus of our service is to help people to live their best life in a safe and supportive environment. 

Priory Hospital Cheadle Royal is accessible by public transport, with local bus routes along Wilmslow Road and Cheadle Hulme and East Didsbury railway stations approximately 12 miles from the service.

employer: University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay NHS Trust
title: Consultant (Stroke) Physician
descriptionHtml:
This post has received Royal College Approval

Application for thissubstantivepost will only be accepted if you hold full GMC registration with a license to practice and entry on the Specialist Register or anticipating being in receipt of CCT/Professional Portfolio (formally CESR) within six months of interview.

We are delighted to be able to offer an opportunity for a highly motivated, ambitious, dynamic individual to join our committed and well integrated multidisciplinary team, providing high standard care to the local community. This will be a full-time, substantive post (potentially >10 Programmed Activities by negotiation).

Those with sub-specialty training in stroke medicine will be encouraged to apply.Applicants are encouraged to clearly exhibit how they meet our criteria in their applications.

The Royal Lancaster Infirmary provides an active acute thrombolysis service (with thrombectomy provided at Royal Preston Hospital) and also makes use of the specialist Telestroke On-Call Service out of hours and at weekends. There is an expectation that the successful candidate will join the regional Telestroke On-Call rota.

The post supports continued development of the Stroke Service and you will work alongside existing Stroke Consultants, as well as a wider Care of the Elderly Team and General Medicine colleagues. You will also liaise with Neuroradiology, Neurosurgery and Vascular Surgery Teams, as well as Stroke Advanced Nurse Practitioners, Matrons, Ward Managers, Nurses, Therapists and Secretaries, to assist in providing excellent care to our patients at all stages of the patient's hospital journey. You will provide clinical leadership to a dedicated team.

The Trust's Hospitals are situated on the edge of the Lake District National Park, surrounded by an area of outstanding natural beauty offering superb outdoor and recreational activities, particularly related to the sea, lakes, fells and countryside. Cities such as Liverpool and Manchester are merely a short train or car journey away.

We can offer you a commitment to teaching, education and audit. The University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay NHS Foundation Trust has a keen interest and deep involvement in medical and dental education at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels, so you could play an active role in progressing the knowledge and skills of these junior colleagues. Medical Students from Lancaster Medical School receive the whole of their education, academic and clinical, in Cumbria and North Lancashire. UHMBFT is the lead NHS organisation and takes responsibility throughout the five years of the degree for the provision of acute practice placements.

title: Consultant Medical Virologist
descriptionHtml:
This is a full-time post for virology services at UKHSA Clinical Network Laboratory, Birmingham, providing Consultant level input into the laboratory, clinical virology and public health service. The post is based at the Lead Public Health Laboratory for the Midlands which is situated at the Birmingham Heartlands Hospital in the University Hospital Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust (Teaching). However, it is a requirement of employment that the post holder be prepared to work at any additional or different location owned or served by the trust, either on an on-going or temporary basis according to the demands of the service. The provision of clinical virology services at Good Hope, Solihull, Birmingham Heartlands Hospitals and Queen Elizabeth Hospital will be by rotation and in partnership with other infection service consultants. In addition to the clinical virology service, the post holder will be providing public health functions for the Midlands Region.

The University Hospital Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust is one of 96 Foundation Trusts in England. The Trust was established in the first of April 2018 by the merger of Heart of England and Queen Elizabeth Hospital Foundation Trusts. The new organisation includes Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, Good Hope Hospital, Solihull District General Hospital, Queen Elizabeth Hospital and Birmingham Chest Clinic. It is a dynamic organisation that represents one of the largest trusts in the UK.

See attached Job Description.

1. Work with colleagues for the provision of a comprehensive clinical medical virology service including: advice regarding appropriate specimens, involvement in specimen analysis, validation and interpretation of results for transmission to service users. Appropriate involvement in policies guidelines and standard operating procedures preparation, relevant to consultant virologist duties. On-call duty will be shared equitably with the other consultants in virology and will involve supervision and support of the on-call Specialist Trainees on front-line duty and provision for cover for consultant colleagues' periods of leave. The on-call support is generally through telephone consultation and only on rare occasions is attendance necessary.

2. In conjunction with the other infection (microbiology, virology, infectious diseases, and immunology) consultants, provide ward-based and telephone advice on the prevention, diagnosis and management of infection in individual patients and outbreaks of infection. This will involve ad hoc clinical consults arising from referrals or significant laboratory results, attending multi-disciplinary clinical meetings and regular ward rounds.

3. Collaborate with colleagues in UKHSABPHL and Infectious Disease Unit in delivering a joint infection service for the host Trust and other users of the service

For further details, please refer to the attached Job Description & Person Specification.

We pride ourselves as being an employer of choice, where Everyone Matters promoting equality of opportunity to actively encourage applications from everyone, including groups currently underrepresented in our workforce.

UKHSA ethos is to be an inclusive organisation for all our staff and stakeholders. To create, nurture and sustain an inclusive culture, where differences drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our workforce and wider communities. We do this through celebrating and protecting differences by removing barriers and promoting equity and equality of opportunity for all.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Are you a motivated GP looking to develop your career within an innovative primary care network (PCN) setting?

Beauchamp House Surgery isseeking a dynamic salaried GP to join our multi-disciplinary team as part of a wider PCN, focusing on improving outcomes for our most vulnerable patients through managing frailty and preventing unnecessary hospital admissions.

Theposition is for 6 sessions per week,looking after patients from our Beauchamp House and Baddow Village Surgeries. You will be required to work on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Fridays each week.

This role offers the opportunity to work across two practices, delivering proactive, holistic care for patients with complex needs, particularly those living with frailty. You will be a key player in a growing ARRS team, collaborating closely with multidisciplinary colleagues including GPs, nurses, pharmacists, paramedics, a digital and transformation manager, social prescribers, general practice assistants and care coordinators.

This is an excellent opportunity to grow your clinical skills while making a tangible difference in your local community. If you want to be part of a forward-thinking PCN delivering improved care for vulnerable patients, we would love to hear from you.

  • Undertaking a variety of duties including surgery consultations, telephone consultations and queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork, reports and correspondence in a timely fashion;
  • Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting medical problems, whether self-referred or referred from other healthcare workers within the organisation;
  • Assessing the healthcare needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems;
  • Screening patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness;
  • Developing care plans for health in consultation with patients and in line with current practice disease management protocols;

  • Recording clear consultation notes to agreed standards;
  • Collecting data for audit purposes and complying with QOF requirements;
  • Delivering enhanced services;
  • Compiling and issuing computer-generated acute and repeat prescriptions;
  • All general duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care.

The four surgeries which make up Chelmsford City Health PCN Limited are separate practices that formed a network to benefit from shared resources and to be able to offer healthcare services at scale to its population of 43,000+ patients. Two of the practices are dispensing practices and all four are training practices.

This is an excellent opportunity to work alongside experienced colleagues as part of a friendly, progressive PCN committed to improving community health and to provide collaborative and patient-centred care.

We offer the following benefits:

  • Competitive salary based on experience and aligned with the current ARRS GP pay scales
  • Fixed term with possibility of extension
  • NHS Pension
  • Mentorship & support: Comprehensive induction and mentoring offered, ideal for newly qualified GPs or those new to ARRS roles.
  • Training & development: Access to ongoing professional development, peer support, and PCN-led educational events
  • Supportive and friendly environment
  • Flexible working hours: all flexible offers and working arrangements will be considered
  • Peer support - Work alongside experienced colleagues to provide collaborative and patient-centred care
  • Positive working culture: Join a friendly, progressive PCN committed to improving community health outcomes

employer: North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Stroke Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The Trust's Stroke Department in the Directorate of Elderly Care, Stroke and Rehabilitation falls under the remit of the Speciality Medicine Collaborative.

There are currently approximately 700 patients for North Cumbria each year with a discharge diagnosis of stroke. Approximately 20 patients per week are seen in the Neurovascular clinic at Cumberland Infirmary, Carlisle (CIC).

The Trust has a Hyper-Acute Stroke Unit (HASU) at the Cumberland Infirmary site, which comprises of a 10 bedded HAS unit at CIC, with 25 acute and rehabilitation beds and a further 15 acute and rehabilitation beds at WCH. A 7 day service model allows the delivery of 7 day stroke/TIA clinics which will rapidly speed up diagnosis and therapeutic intervention, and will provide an integrated pathway into community services.'

We are looking to appoint dynamic and forward-thinking Consultant Physicians with a special interest in Stroke Medicine to complete a team of six (including new appointments) within the Trust covering North Cumbria. This is an opportunity to join an organisation in which Clinicians are at the forefront of management.

Appraisal and Job Planning is carried out at regular intervals, and forwarded to the specialty lead.

Our CEO, Trudie Davies, and Executive Medical Director, Adrian Clements, would love to hear from you to discuss your future career in North Cumbria. To arrange an informal chat, please contact Sally Rushton on Sally.Rushton1@ncic.nhs.uk for Trudie and Julia McClune on Julia.mcclune@ncic.nhs.uk for Adrian.

At NCIC, we have an ambition to deliver outstanding hospital and health services to half a million people. We're responsible for delivering over 70 services across 15 main locations and we employ more than 6,500 members of staff.

Our 5 key principles demonstrate our belief in the delivery of 'safe, high quality care every time'.

title: Maternity GP Locum

GP maternity cover role at New Addington Group Practice, joining a friendly, well-supported team. Bourne Health is a leading Primary Care NHS (National Health Service) GP (General Practitioner) Partnership. title: Consultant Dermatologist
descriptionHtml:
Join 18 Week Support as a Consultant Dermatologist and make a direct contribution to improving patient access to NHS care. We are seeking experienced Dermatologists to deliver both Two-Week Wait (2WW) and General Dermatology clinics across our NHS services.

You will work alongside experienced clinical teams, helping to reduce waiting times while delivering high-quality, patient-centred care. This is an opportunity to use your expertise in a supportive environment, with flexible opportunities available across a range of NHS sites.

If you are an experienced Consultant Dermatologist looking for additional clinical work alongside your existing commitments, we would be pleased to hear from you.

  • As a Consultant Dermatologist, you will be responsible for delivering high-quality dermatology clinics, including:

    • Assessing, diagnosing and managing patients across 2WW and General Dermatology pathways.
    • Undertaking comprehensive dermatological examinations and clinical assessments.
    • Assessing and managing patients with suspected skin cancer where appropriate.
    • Developing and communicating appropriate treatment and management plans.
    • Providing specialist clinical advice and guidance to patients and colleagues.
    • Maintaining accurate and timely clinical documentation and communicating outcomes appropriately.
    • Working collaboratively with the wider clinical team to ensure safe and effective patient care.
About 18 Week Support

18 Week Support is a leading NHS insourcing provider, working in partnership with NHS Trusts across the UK to increase clinical capacity, reduce waiting times and improve patient access to care.

Our clinical teams work alongside NHS services to deliver additional outpatient and surgical capacity, supported by experienced Clinical Leads and Nurse Leads. Patient safety, clinical governance and quality of care are central to everything we do.

title: GP - Salaried
descriptionHtml:
Come and join our exceptional and thriving practice in the heart of Somerset in the historic and lively town of Glastonbury.

We are a six partner team and have a vacancy for a 4 - 6 session salaried GP. Working days will include a Thursday & Friday (4 sessions).

It's a great place to perform the demanding and yet highly satisfying role of a GP, with supportive colleagues and a wonderful practice team which altogether means we are well placed to navigate the ever changing world of primary care with autonomy and a sense of well being.

We are a training practice for both GP registrars and medical students, and regularly receive excellent feedback from these posts, and several of our ex-trainees are now partners.

Interested? Please take the time to read the information pack attached to this advert to learn more about the exciting opportunity to work as part of our team.

To informally discuss the opportunity, learn more about how we work, or to apply, please email or call Adam Hann, somicb.glastonburysurgery.recruitment@nhs.net or 01458 836 109.

This is an open advert and we reserve the right to shortlist and interview ahead of the published closing date for this advert.

The post-holder will provide high quality general medical services to a personalised list of patients and work as part of the practice team to manage a range of health needs in a purpose built and modern primary care setting, ensuring the continuous delivery of the highest standards of care.

Your working day will follow the BMA guidance on safe daily contacts, with an established blend of pre-booked and same day face to face and telephone appointments.

The experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians collectively manage same day patient demand, removing the requirement for limitless duty doctor sessions.

We are a stable, supportive and very friendly training practice that has retained its family and patient-first ethos. We work from purpose-built premises that has been recently extended, in a colourful market town offering semi-rural primary care.

The practice is very successful and has a good reputation amongst the GP community both externally and internally as evidenced by strong staff retention.

We care for a registered population size of 14,000 served by 11 GPs, GP Registrars, Nurse Practitioners, and a team of Practice Nurses and HCAs, physiotherapists, administrative, secretarial and reception.

Caring for the population of Glastonbury, Street and the surrounding villages offers a unique opportunity to connect with a diverse population that is passionate for the town and its rich history and culture. By offering a person centred and continuity of care approach, we can demonstrate quality outcomes, as defined by QOF, whilst also respecting the views and beliefs of the local community.

We undertake a formal and regular business planning cycle to ensure that we effectively manage the rapidly changing environment we are in, optimising opportunities for the practice and have a track record of innovation.

The information pack offers insight into our structure, achievements, and the respective opportunities available to the right person.

title: ENT Doctor
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a skilled and dedicated ENT Clinician to join our dynamic healthcare team at CHEC. This sessional position offers a flexible opportunity to make a real impact on patient care and support the growth of our community ENT service.

At CHEC, we care deeply about our people and the future of healthcare. We are committed to innovation and the delivery of high-quality patient care, and we are looking for clinicians who share our values and wish to play an active role in shaping the future of health services.CHEC is looking to recruit an experienced ENT GP to join our team and support the continued growth of our community ENT services. About CHEC

Since 2012, CHEC has been working with the NHS to increase patient choice and provide better access to exceptional, timely, locally-based ophthalmology and gastroenterology care  free at the point of care.

CHEC has a nationwide portfolio of community hospitals and clinics  operating in a unique hub-and-spoke model. We are proud to have a role alongside colleagues in the NHS, offering patients the choice of access to essential procedures and help achieve the best possible clinical outcomes.
