CHEC is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all employees to share this commitment, this includes being aware of and adhering to all CHEC Safeguarding policies.  Recruitment checks are undertaken in accordance with the NHS Employment Check Standards and successful applicants may be required to undertake an Enhanced Disclosure via the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS).

title: Healthcare Assistant (HCA) / Phlebotomist
descriptionHtml:
Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group is looking for an experienced Healthcare Assistant (HCA) / Phlebotomist to join our team across GP practice sites in Barking and Dagenham.

This is a full-time, permanent role for 37.5 hours per week. The successful candidate will work across different practice sites according to the rota, but will normally remain at one site for the full working day.

We are looking for an experienced primary care HCA who is confident in phlebotomy and a broad range of routine HCA duties. Formal phlebotomy training/competency certification and recent practical phlebotomy experience are essential.

The role will include supporting long-term condition reviews, NHS Health Checks and other routine clinical activity. Early starts are essential due to morning phlebotomy clinics.

You will join an experienced clinical team, with nursing support available for ongoing development and competency updates where appropriate.

We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if a sufficient number of suitable applications are received. Early application is therefore encouraged.

The Healthcare Assistant / Phlebotomist will support the clinical team by delivering a range of routine patient care and monitoring activities within general practice.

Main duties will include:

  • Phlebotomy and specimen collection.
  • Blood pressure, height, weight and BMI checks.
  • NHS Health Checks.
  • Supporting long-term condition reviews, including diabetes checks and foot assessments.
  • Performing ECGs and urinalysis.
  • Administering B12 injections in line with practice protocols and appropriate authorisation.
  • Smoking and alcohol screening and brief health-promotion advice.
  • Recording observations and clinical information accurately in the patient record.
  • Maintaining infection prevention and control standards and safe clinical environments.
  • Working closely with GPs, nurses and the wider practice team to support safe and efficient patient care.

The postholder will work within their level of competence and follow agreed practice protocols, with experienced nursing support available where required.

Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group provides GP services across Barking and Dagenham, East London.

We are a busy and developing multi-site organisation with a strong focus on patient care, teamwork, safe clinical practice and continuous improvement.

You will work as part of an experienced clinical and administrative team, with support from GPs, nurses and other healthcare professionals. The role offers variety across our practice sites, ongoing learning opportunities and the chance to contribute to high-quality patient care.

We offer a permanent full-time position, NHS Pension access subject to eligibility, annual leave entitlement and support with ongoing training and development.

employer: Avon & Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Acute Inpatient, North Somerset
descriptionHtml:
Are you looking for your next role as a dynamic clinical leader in Acute Inpatient Psychiatry?

Join a dynamic and supportive medical community as the Inpatient Consultant on Juniper Ward -- an 18-bed mixed-gender unit within the Long Fox Unit at Weston General Hospital. You'll provide clinical leadership to a dedicated multi-disciplinary team, ensuring high-quality care and fostering a culture of collaboration and innovation.

Professional Development

North Somerset Mental Health is proud of its inclusive and forward-thinking ethos. We actively support consultants in shaping services and driving improvements. You'll be encouraged to:

  • Take on leadership and management roles
  • Pursue career development opportunities
  • Contribute to service transformation initiatives

This is more than a clinical post -- it's a chance to lead, grow, and make a lasting impact.

As the ward consultant you will deliver direct interventions and weekly review to inpatients including those patients who require use of the Mental Health Act who are difficult to engage. This will include on-going assessment, diagnoses (including review and clarification) and treatment of mental and physical health needs.

You will lead the ward rounds and will provide advice and support to members of the ward team including junior medical staff.

You will be responsible for MHA related work, including reports and attendance at tribunals.

You will be an integral part of psychoeducation, crisis, relapse prevention and care planning for inpatients and will liaise with other parts of the service, including community MH teams; GPs and non NHS organisations wherever applicable. You will liaise with the Intensive and recovery services as appropriate to facilitate the smooth handover of clients between services.

We are AWP (Avon and Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust) a diverse organisation with over 5,000 dedicated staff providing inpatient and community-based mental health care. We provide services from a range of locations to approximately 1.8 million people living in Bath and North East Somerset (B&NES), Bristol, North Somerset, South Gloucestershire, Swindon, across the county of Wiltshire and in parts of Dorset. Our outstanding people promote mental health and wellbeing. The expertise and resources within AWP are dedicated to a person-centred approach for those who use our services and for all employees. We recognise that happy and fulfilled employees give better care.

Please note that Avon & Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust is not currently a sponsor under the GMC Sponsorship Scheme.

As a result, we regret to inform you that we are unable to consider applications from individuals who require GMC sponsorship

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are a unique dispensing practice in a picturesque Cotswold town with excellent railway connections to both Oxford and London. Attractive Cotswold Stone single site premises with good on-site parking. Easy access to Charlbury Station, which is only a 15 minute journey from Oxford Station. We use EMIS Web, AccuRx and Docman 10 and are a dispensing practice. We are a forward thinking practice with a strong cohesive, happy team.

We are seeking a Salaried GP for 4 sessions per week, likely to involve a Monday and a Thursday with 2 sessions on call per week.

  • 25 x 15 minute appointments and 2.5 hours admin per day.
  • Minimal home visits due to the support of Early Visiting Service.
  • No Nursing Home.
  • This post is offered as a permanent position with 6 weeks annual leave and 1 week study leave pro rata.
  • Salary dependent on experience.
  • Monthly afternoon practice meetings.
  • Well supported by our existing team of clinicans and administrative staff.
  • We are a Research Active Practice.

Our team currently consists of GP partner, Paramedic/Managing Partner, Salaried GPs, Practice Nurses, Nurse Associate, Health Care Assistants and we also have a physiotherapist, pharmacist team and mental health practitioner working at our practice.

Main Duties and Responsibilities

Clinical Duties

Provide face to face and telephone for undifferentiated and un-diagnosed conditions.

Manage a personal patient caseload and ensure continuity of care.

Conduct clinical assessments, develop management plans, and provide health education.

Identify risk factors and early signs of illness.

Prescribe medications in line with national and practice guidelines.

Request, interpret, and act on diagnostic tests and results.

Make appropriate referrals to secondary care and community services.

Administrative and Governance Duties

Complete clinical administration including correspondence, reports, and accurate record keeping.

Maintain highquality clinical notes using EMIS Web, AccuRx, and Docman 10.

Participate in clinical audits, quality improvement activities, and achievement of QOF and contract targets.

Attend practice meetings and contribute to service development.

Team and Practice Involvement

Work collaboratively with partners, salaried GPs, nurses, HCAs, paramedics, pharmacists, physiotherapists, social prescribers, and mental health practitioners.

Support teaching, training, and development activities where appropriate.

Adhere to safeguarding, confidentiality, and all practice policies.

Practice Context

4 sessions per week, including Fridays, with 25 x 15 minute appointments plus admin time.

Opportunities to contribute to research and take on lead roles.

The Charlbury Medical Centre provides GP services to 5,489 patients in a rural area of the Cotswolds, in the small picturesque market town of Charlbury. The practice serves an area with an overall low level of deprivation, although there are pockets of rural poverty, with related issues of geographical isolation, including ease of access to medical care.

The practice has two partners and 3 salaried GPs There are 2 practice nurses, a nurse associate and 2 healthcare assistants. We are a very friendly, strong, cohesive, happy team The surgery building was built in the late 1990s. There is an onsite dispensary which can provide pharmaceutical services to patients who live more than one mile (1.6km) from their nearest pharmacy premises. Two dispensers currently provide the services to approximately one third of the practices patients. The practice is fully open from 8am to 6.30pm Monday to Friday. The out of hours service is provided by Oxford Health and is accessed by calling NHS 111.

employer: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Stroke Medicine and HfOP
descriptionHtml:
The Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to appoint a Consultant to join the department of Stroke Medicine & Healthcare for the Older Person for its Eastern services, based at Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital (Wonford).

These roles form part of a wider integrated department that includes our Northern services based in Barnstaple.

Our combined Stroke Medicine department is friendly, successful and ambitious. The Royal Devon is a Trust which encourages and supports innovation, diversity, digital development and research.

Successful candidates will be given a high degree of autonomy and time to undertake supporting professional activities. This includes training and teaching or to pursue sub-specialty interests. This is a fantastic opportunity to design a consultant post to suit your professional aspirations.

For more detail about the main duties of this role, please see the job description section below. As a key member of the Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, you will be joining an exceptional team working together to help our patients to stay healthy, when they need it most.

Stretching across Northern, Eastern and Mid Devon, we have a workforce of over 15,000 staff, making us the largest employer in Devon. Our core services, which we provide to more than 615,000 people, cover more than 2,000 square miles across Devon, while some of our specialist services cover the whole of the peninsula, extending our reach as far as Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly.

We deliver a wide range of emergency, specialist and general medical services through North Devon District Hospital and the Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital (Wonford).

Alongside our two acute hospitals, we provide integrated health and social care services across a variety of settings, including community inpatient hospitals, outpatient clinics, and within peoples own homes. We also offer primary care services, a range of specialist community services, and Sexual Assault Referral Centres (SARC).

Our state-of-the-art equipment, leading technologies and strong links to local universities put us at the forefront of research and innovations, enabling us to provide world-class care to our local communities.

Its never been a more exciting time to join the Royal Devon, as youll help to shape our services as we continue along our integration journey.

employer: County Durham & Darlington NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Anaesthesia and Intensive Care
descriptionHtml:
This is a full time post for a Consultant in Anaesthesia and Intensive Care Medicine based at Darlington Memorial Hospital (DMH), County Durham and Darlington NHS Foundation Trust. A fantastic opportunity to continue your career in Anaesthetics and Intensive Care in a supportive and enthusiastic district general hospital with a focus on multidisciplinery contiuity of care and a team based approach.

The main duties of the role are to provide consultant led care in anaesthetis and intensive care medicine within a District General Hospital with a variety of elective and emergecny specialities.

In hours anaesthetic job planned sessions have the opportunty to work within a variety of specialites and the intensive care rota includes fixed 1 in 8 continuity week comprising of morning sessions with additional long day job planned sessions.

On call commitment will cover intensive care medicine and paediatric stabilisations. This is a frequency of 1:12 and are based on weekday out of hours cover from 18:00 to 08:00 and split day weekend 12 hour sessions from 08:00 to 20:00 plus additional weekend morning cover to allow support the unit ward round.

Paediatric stabilisations are covered by both theatre and intensive care consultants to provide robust support, with the first responder responsibility being shared on alternative weekly rota.

Progress to non clinical department development including teaching, governance, research and management.

If you are being interviewed you must accept an interview slot in the system to continue, even if you have arranged with the manager.

You must be able to produce ALL certificates stated essential in the person specification or you will not be able to complete pre-employment checks.

We provide hospital services from two acute sites - Darlington Memorial Hospital and University Hospital of North Durham. We have a centre for planned care in Bishop Auckland and provide care from community hospitals in Chester-le-Street, Shotley Bridge, Barnard Castle, Sedgefield and Weardale as well as over 80 other community based settings and providing care in patients' homes.

We particularly welcome applications from disabled and Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic (BAME) candidates as BAME and disabled people are currently under-represented.

Full Job Descriptions can be found in the adverts supporting documents.

Over reliance on AI-generated content is discouraged and may diminish the applicant's chances of success.

For the most up-to-date information on visa requirements and eligibility, please check online to determine whether you can apply.

title: Locum Consultant in Elective Gynaecology
descriptionHtml:
Join Optimised Care as a Locum Consultant in Elective Gynaecology and play a key role in delivering outstanding patient-centred care within a modern, growing elective healthcare service.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Consultant to focus on high-quality elective gynaecology, undertaking outpatient clinics, post-operative reviews, and elective procedures including laparoscopic surgery, hysteroscopy, endometrial assessment, and Mirena coil insertion. With no routine on-call commitments, you'll have the opportunity to concentrate on achieving excellent clinical outcomes while working within a supportive multidisciplinary team.

You'll work alongside experienced healthcare professionals who share a passion for clinical excellence, patient safety, and innovation in elective care.

We offer competitive locum rates, well-organised theatre lists, dedicated operational support, and the opportunity to contribute to the development of a growing elective service. Whether you're looking for additional sessions or a longer-term locum opportunity, this role provides flexibility, professional autonomy, and the chance to make a meaningful impact on patients' lives.

If you're a GMC-registered Consultant Gynaecologist with expertise in elective procedures and a commitment to delivering the highest standards of care, we'd love to hear from you.

As a Locum Consultant in Elective Gynaecology, you will provide specialist care to patients throughout their elective treatment journey, from initial consultation through to post-operative follow-up. Working within a modern elective healthcare environment, you will undertake outpatient clinics, perform a range of planned gynaecological procedures, and support the delivery of safe, efficient, and high-quality patient care.

You will collaborate closely with a multidisciplinary team to ensure excellent clinical outcomes, positive patient experiences, and smooth patient pathways. The role offers the opportunity to work in a dedicated elective setting with well-structured theatre lists and clinics, allowing you to focus on delivering expert care without the pressures often associated with acute and emergency services.

In addition to your clinical responsibilities, you will contribute to maintaining high standards of governance, patient safety, and service quality, while supporting continuous improvement initiatives within the organisation. This is an ideal opportunity for an experienced Consultant Gynaecologist seeking a flexible role where they can utilise their specialist skills, enjoy professional autonomy, and make a meaningful impact within a growing elective care service.

At Optimised Care, we are committed to delivering outstanding healthcare services through innovation, clinical excellence, and a patient-first approach. Our focus is on providing high-quality elective care in a professional, efficient, and supportive environment where both patients and staff can thrive.

We pride ourselves on creating a collaborative culture where experienced clinicians, healthcare professionals, and operational teams work together to achieve the very best outcomes. Our organisation values integrity, compassion, accountability, and continuous improvement, ensuring that every patient receives safe, personalised, and high-quality care throughout their journey.

As a growing healthcare provider, we are passionate about investing in our people and creating an environment where expertise is recognised and valued.

You will benefit from working within modern facilities, alongside highly skilled colleagues, with access to dedicated operational support and well-managed clinical pathways that allow you to focus on delivering exceptional patient care.

Our team is driven by a shared commitment to excellence, innovation, and making a positive difference to the lives of the patients we serve. If you are looking to join an organisation where your expertise will be valued and your contribution will have a meaningful impact, Optimised Care is an excellent place to build your next opportunity.

title: Elective ENT Locum Consultant
descriptionHtml:
Optimised Care is seeking an experienced and motivated Locum Consultant ENT Surgeon to join our growing elective healthcare service. This is an excellent opportunity to work within a patient-focused organisation dedicated to reducing waiting times and delivering outstanding clinical outcomes through high-quality planned care.

As a Locum Consultant ENT, you will play a key role in providing specialist outpatient consultations, post-operative follow-up care, and elective surgical procedures including Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery (FESS), Septoplasty, and Tonsillectomy. Working alongside a highly skilled multidisciplinary team, you will help deliver efficient patient pathways while maintaining the highest standards of safety, governance, and patient experience.

This role offers flexibility, competitive locum rates, and the opportunity to focus on elective care without the pressures typically associated with emergency or on-call commitments.

We are looking for a GMC Specialist Registered ENT Consultant with a strong track record in elective surgery, excellent communication skills, and a commitment to patient-centred care. Experience within independent healthcare or elective recovery programmes is highly desirable.

If you are passionate about delivering high-quality ENT services and want to be part of an organisation committed to improving patient access to care, we would welcome your application.

The successful candidate will provide consultant-led ENT care across elective outpatient and surgical services, supporting patients throughout their treatment journey. You will assess, diagnose, and manage patients presenting with a wide range of ENT conditions, ensuring high standards of clinical care and patient experience at all times.

Working closely with multidisciplinary colleagues, you will contribute to the delivery of efficient and effective elective services, helping to improve access to care and reduce waiting times. The role involves undertaking planned surgical procedures, reviewing patient outcomes, and supporting the continuous development of clinical pathways and service quality.

You will be expected to maintain excellent clinical governance standards, ensure accurate record keeping, and actively promote patient safety within all aspects of practice. This is an opportunity to work within a collaborative and forward-thinking healthcare environment focused on delivering outstanding outcomes for patients through high-quality elective care.

Optimised Care is a patient-focused healthcare provider dedicated to delivering high-quality elective services with efficiency, compassion, and clinical excellence. Our approach is centred on improving patient access to care, reducing waiting times, and ensuring every individual receives safe, timely, and personalised treatment.

We are proud of our collaborative and supportive environment, where clinicians, nurses, theatre teams, and administrative staff work closely together to achieve outstanding patient outcomes. Our teams are proactive, solutions-focused, and committed to maintaining the highest standards of clinical governance and patient safety.

The culture at Optimised Care is built on respect, accountability, and continuous improvement. We value open communication, shared learning, and a strong team ethic, ensuring every member of staff feels supported and empowered in their role. There is a genuine focus on quality care delivered through streamlined pathways and well-organised elective services.

Working with us offers the opportunity to be part of a forward-thinking organisation that prioritises both patient experience and professional satisfaction. We provide well-structured clinical environments, modern facilities, and efficient administrative support to enable clinicians to focus on delivering excellent care. Flexible working arrangements and competitive locum rates further support a positive and balanced working experience.

title: Bank Consultant Dermatologist
descriptionHtml:
Bank Consultant Dermatologist Private Hospital Gloucester

Optimised Care is looking to welcome an experienced Consultant Dermatologist to our growing consultant-led private healthcare service in Gloucester.

This is an opportunity to build or complement your private practice with flexible bank clinics, arranged around your existing NHS, private or professional commitments.

We provide a supportive, professionally managed environment where consultants can focus on what matters most delivering exceptional clinical care and an outstanding patient experience. You will have access to an experienced hospital and administrative team, with efficient support around your clinics.

We are particularly interested in hearing from Consultants with specialist interests or procedural expertise who would like the opportunity to develop their clinical offering within a growing private healthcare setting.

At Optimised Care, we are committed to creating strong, long-term relationships with our consultants and providing the environment, support and flexibility to help you deliver the highest standards of patient care.

If you are an experienced Consultant Dermatologist looking for a flexible private practice opportunity, we would welcome a confidential conversation about how you could become part of the Optimised Care consultant team.

Flexible sessions. Consultant-led care. A growing private healthcare service.

As a Bank Consultant Dermatologist, you will provide specialist dermatology consultations to private patients within a professional, patient-focused healthcare environment in Gloucester.

You will assess patients, establish diagnoses and develop appropriate treatment and management plans, ensuring each patient receives a high standard of personalised care.

The role will include:

  • Conducting consultant-led dermatology clinics and patient assessments.

  • Reviewing medical histories, symptoms and previous investigations.

  • Providing expert advice, diagnosis and treatment recommendations.

  • Discussing treatment options clearly with patients and supporting informed decision-making.

  • Providing appropriate follow-up and ongoing management where required.

  • Maintaining accurate, comprehensive and timely clinical documentation.

  • Communicating effectively with referring clinicians and the wider healthcare team.

  • Working collaboratively with the hospital's clinical and administrative teams to provide a seamless patient journey.

  • Maintaining the highest standards of clinical governance, patient safety and professional practice.

The role offers flexibility around your existing commitments, with clinic sessions agreed according to your availability and the needs of the service.

We are particularly interested in Consultants who have specialist interests or procedural expertise that could complement and help develop the dermatology service.

Optimised Care is a growing, consultant-led private healthcare provider built around one simple principle: exceptional clinical care with a genuinely personal approach.

Our consultant team brings together experienced specialists, many of whom combine senior NHS positions with private practice. Working from a modern hospital environment, our clinicians have access to professional facilities and a supportive multidisciplinary team, allowing them to focus on delivering excellent patient care.

We pride ourselves on being approachable, responsive and commercially progressive, while maintaining the highest standards of clinical governance and patient safety. Our focus is on providing patients with timely access to experienced consultants, clear treatment pathways and a high-quality experience from their first enquiry through to follow-up.

For our consultants, we aim to create a professional, collaborative and supportive environment where clinical expertise is valued and there is scope to develop services and specialist interests.

Joining Optimised Care means becoming part of a growing team with a strong work ethic, a commitment to clinical excellence and an ambition to continually improve the way private healthcare is delivered.

employer: Maidstone and Tunbridge Wells NHS Trust
title: Consultant in Palliative Medicine
descriptionHtml:
This is a post for Maidstone and Tunbridge Wells NHS Trust. The successful candidate will work with the existing palliative medicine consultant and support the Specialist Palliative Care (SPC) and Enhanced supportive Care (ESC) services on both sites of the Trust. The post is part of the Oncology directorate and the post will be based at Maidstone hospital, the main site for Kent Oncology services.

1. To provide a high standard of care to any patient for whom you have clinical responsibility. This will include any patients referred to you and cared for by you personally or by members of your team, and, in addition, any patients of consultant colleagues when you are covering on-call or for annual leave.

2. To participate in clinical and other service activities and development to ensure a high standard of patient care across the Trust.

3. To work in close co-operation with other medical, professional and managerial colleagues, both within and outside the speciality, to provide high-quality health care to the Trust's patients, and to contribute to future thinking about the Trust's strategic direction.

4. To participate fully in and share leadership of the clinical governance of the speciality covering its Trust-wide activities. To attend clinical governance half-days as detailed in the Trust's Guide to job planning, unless on agreed leave or while attending emergencies.

5. To participate actively in departmental audits, sharing co-ordination of audit activities within the department and implementation of change.

Maidstone and Tunbridge Wells NHS Trust ranks among the top 10 NHS Trusts nationwide and was named the second-best Trust to work for in the South East in the 2023 and 2024 NHS Staff Survey.

We are a large acute hospital trust in south-east England, providing general hospital services and specialist care to around 600,000 residents in West Kent and East Sussex. With a dedicated and diverse team of over 8,000 staff we are proud to offer specialised cancer services to over two million people through the Kent Oncology Centre.

Fordcombe Hospital, near Tunbridge Wells, became part of the Trust in October 2024. Specialising in planned care, it offers two operating theatres, 28 inpatient and day-care beds, diagnostic services (X-ray, MRI, CT, and endoscopy), and consultation/treatment rooms.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a motivated and enthusiastic qualified GP to join our friendly, supportive and proactive practice, in a Salaried Position.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic and motivated Salaried GP to join our friendly, supportive, and forward-thinking team at William Fisher Medical Centre.

We are a well-established dispensing practice serving a growing patient population in the beautiful semi-rural Dengie Peninsula. We pride ourselves on delivering high-quality patient care while maintaining a positive work-life balance for our clinicians. This is an excellent opportunity for a GP seeking a welcoming practice environment with strong multidisciplinary support and opportunities to develop special interests.

  • Provide comprehensive medical care to patients presenting with a wide range of acute and chronic health conditions.
  • Access, diagnose, treat and appropriately manage patients in accordance with current clinical guidelines and best practice.
  • Conduct face -to -face consultations, Accurx and telephone consultations.
  • Undertake home visits when clinically necessary and in accordance with practice arrangements.
  • Prescribe safely and appropriately in accordance with local and national guidelines.
  • Review test results, correspondence and other clinical information requiring GP action.

Salaried GP - 6-8 sessions

Sussex Primary Care (SPC) is an established, at-scale primary care provider committed to developing innovative approaches to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care.

We're looking for GPs to join Wadhurst Medical Group, our friendly, growing practice on the East Sussex/Kent border.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
4 - 8 Sessions per week

Esher Green Surgery, a part of Bourne Health, are looking for a proactive and enthusiastic GP to join our Practice, ideally working 4-8 sessions, to work closely with our nurses and GPs to manage a busy and interesting clinical caseload.

The postholder will provide high-quality patient care across both clinical sessions and telephone triage. They will have the opportunity to contribute to the leadership of key disease areas, monitoring Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF) trends, supporting staff training and development, and ensuring safe and effective prescribing. They will also play an active role in developing and improving healthcare services for a diverse patient population, including practice-based commissioning, patient participation and health promotion initiatives.

The postholder will be closely supported by both the clinical and management teams within the practice and will be part of a wider multi-site clinical team. While the main base will be at Esher Green Surgery, there may be opportunities to deliver triage and on-site clinical sessions at other Bourne Health GP Practices.

We appreciate the interest of all applicants in this opportunity. Please note that we may close this vacancy early if we identify a suitable candidate before the advertised closing date. We encourage interested applicants to submit their applications as soon as possible.

In accordance with the practice timetable, as agreed, the post-holder will make themselves available to undertake clinical sessions. A clinical session is normally composed of face-to-face appointments together with telephone appointments, followed by a variety of duties including queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions, actioning test results, medical reports, and examinations (e.g. Insurance Companies) on behalf of the Practice. The above duties should be performed in a timely manner. Appointments will be 10 minutes duration.

Bourne Health is the largest primary care provider in South West London, serving diverse communities across multiple GP surgeries. We are committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care, underpinned by innovation, community engagement, and operational excellence.

title: Salaried General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a friendly enthusiastic salaried GP to join our friendly practice. This position is available due to the reduction in sessions of our long standing senior partner in July 2027 and we wish to give ourselves plenty of time to find the right candidate.

We have a patient list size of 8100 in rural Oxfordshire, Main site at Bloxham with branch surgery at Hook Norton.

We have a full compliment of clinical staff who work closely together to support the practice needs.

We do not operate total triage at the practice. Our focus is to accommodate our patients on a daily basis with the options of either a face to face appointment or a telephone consultation depending on which option a patient has chosen.

We have open sessions in the morning with pre-booked appointments in the afternoon.

We have 15 slots in the morning and 12 slots in the afternoon.

You will be supported by a full compliment of nursing to support GP's over both sites. The team consists of 3 nurses, 2 health care assistants and 1 phlebotomist who is trained to do paediatric bloods.

You will be required to work at our branch surgery which is approximately 5 miles away from our main surgery site.

We have 1 private nursing home situated at the end of our driveway for which we cover 1 clinic session per week for their registered clients.

Your contract will be based on the BMA standard contract.

We are a traditional practice with a strong team work ethic to provide a highest possible standard of care for our patients.

title: Salaried GP

title: Consultant Gastroenterologist
descriptionHtml:
North Cumbria Integrated Care is looking for a dynamic and motivated Consultant gastroenterologist to join our team of consultant gastroenterologists and gastrointestinal surgeons to provide an integrated digestive diseases service across north Cumbria. The North Cumbria GI Service is a new, cohesive and integrated department, combining the services of gastroenterology and endoscopy, upper gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary, colorectal, emergency GI surgery.

The successful candidate will join a team of gastroenterologists supported by nurse specialists in IBD & hepatology across the Trust. Associated with the transformation of all our services across the Trust, and in conjunction with the introduction of our model for acute medical care, it is envisaged that future configurations will focus complex in patient work at the Carlisle site, and elective outpatient services (endoscopy and outpatient clinics) will be provided by all of the team across the Trust. Sub specialty interest will be encouraged where this contributes to and complements the department and Trusts' service needs.

Please note: You must be on the Specialist Register in order to be eligible for appointment to this level of post.

The department has two dedicated GI wards within the Cumberland Infirmary at Carlisle for the treatment of inpatients. The plan in the near future is to have all GI areas co-located. There is a dedicated 4-room endoscopy unit at The Cumberland Infirmary and the new endoscopy unit at West Cumberland Hospital, Whitehaven has 2 dedicated rooms in a new, state of the art facility. There is a specialist GI physiology lab on both sites.

We currently provide a consultant of the week service for our in patients, a 24/7 GI bleed rota as well as specialist services in IBD, Hepatology, HPB, Bowel Cancer screening and complex polypectomy. Endoscopy services, are provided across our two acute sites in Carlisle and Whitehaven. A full range of diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, including ERCP, are available. Our new £15M, 5 room, State of the Art, JAG accredited Endoscopy Suite opened in March 2025.

At NCIC, we have an ambition to deliver outstanding healthcare services to the population of North Cumbria. The Trust is committed to creating a centre of excellence in providing rural and remote healthcare and provides a wide range of community and acute services throughout our county.

Our 5 key principles demonstrate our belief in the delivery of 'safe, high quality care every time':

Being a clinically led organisation

Quality and safety at the heart of our Trust

A positive patient experience every time

A great place to work

Managing our money well

As an organisation we are serious about supporting a diverse workforce that reflects our local community and are very much focused on being an inclusive and compassionate place to work.

Across the North East and North Cumbria we are working together to deliver our ambition to be the greenest region in England by 2030. All staff are expected to support sustainability.

title: Consultant in Rehabilitation Medicine (Neuro & Spinal Rehab)
descriptionHtml:
Akessa Healthcare is seeking to appoint a Consultant Neurologist to lead the development of outpatient Neurological services, as well as support the ongoing treatment and rehabilitation of our neuro and spinal patients.

In this role the appointee is expected to provide comprehensive care for private patients. The appointment is based at two sites, The main base, with both outpatient and inpatient care, is based at the Royal Buckinghamshire Hospital in Aylesbury . Outpatient clinics will also be provided at The New Foscote Hospital in Banbury.

The appointee will be provided with luxurious facility, caring environment, ample time and administrative support to deliver world class care.

As a senior colleague, the post-holder will work in close co-operation with, and support, other clinical, medical professional and managerial colleagues in providing high quality healthcare to our patients.

The successful candidate will be assigned appropriate secretarial support to clinical work and diary management.

Duties and responsibilities:

  • Lead on the development of Neuro-Spinal services.
  • Deliver high-quality care for all patients and support the smooth running of the service.
  • Support efficient management of resources and maintenance of our short waiting lists for private and insured patients.
  • Take ownership in the successful performance against key performance indicators, ensuring zero compromise to the quality of care or clinical excellence for patients.
  • In collaboration with department leads, maintain and develop quality standards and improvement throughout the department and in line with any relevant accreditation requirements.
  • Provide on-site clinical expertise as and when needed, supporting MDTs as required.
  • Essential requirements:
  • CCT in Neurology or Rehabilitation Medicine
  • Full GMC Registration.
  • Inclusion in the GMC Specialist Register in Neurology or Rehabilitation Medicine.
  • Currently employed, or has previously held substantive NHS consultant post.
  • Eligible to register with private medical insurance companies (BUPA, AXA-PPP etc).
  • Able to take responsibility for delivering the service without direct supervision.

The Akessa Healthcare Group is managed and run by clinicians. We are proud to be part of a highly skilled, diverse team.

The New Foscote Hospital was established in Banbury over 40 years ago and has provided services and treatments to thousands of people from across the region. We have over 50 consultants, all of whom are leaders in their specialist fields and choose to hold their private practices here, working alongside our friendly, highly qualified and experienced nursing and support teams.

The Royal Buckinghamshire Hospital was established in Aylesbury in 1832 and has provided services and treatments to thousands of people from across the region. The ownership of the hospital was transferred to our new management team in January 2023. By joining our existing portfolio, the hospital is now run professionally and provides clinical care to private, insured and NHS patients, with a strong ethos on caring for our staff.

Significant ongoing investment into both hospitals includes complete refurbishment of the wards, the outpatient area, reception, staff facilities, radiology and the construction of additional state-of-the-art operating theatres and endoscopy suites.

With the expansion of the Group this is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Consultant Neurologist to join our growing team to provide clinical excellence for our patients at both hospitals.

title: Locum Consultant in Clinical Immunology and Allergy
descriptionHtml:
This advert is for a 1.0WTE Consultant in Allergy based at Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust (QMC Campus).

This appointment will be on the terms and conditions of the extant NHS Consultant contract. The contract is for a fixed 12 month period.

The successful candidate will be on the Full and Specialist Register of the GMC or be eligible for registration within six months of interview. It is expected that the appointee will hold Fellowship of the Royal College of Physicians (FRCP) or Pathologists (FRCPath).

The appointee, in collaboration with the other consultants, will be expected to fulfil the duties within the agreed Job Plan.

Summary of Duties:

  1. participation in the provision of a clinical service in the diagnosis and management of patients with allergic disease. This may occasionally require review of individual patients on the wards or discussion with colleagues outside NUH, for example in other Trusts or in primary care.
  2. cover for colleagues' annual leave and other authorised absences.
  3. professional supervision and management of junior medical staff, nursing staff, specialist pharmacist, dietitian, STPs and clinical scientists where required
  4. responsibility for carrying out teaching, examination and accreditation duties as required and for contributing to undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing medical education activity locally and nationally.
  5. participating in medical audit, the Trust's Clinical Governance processes and in CPD.
  6. involvement in research, as appropriate to job plan
  7. a willingness to undertake additional professional responsibilities at local, regional, or national levels.
  8. the post holder must at all times carry out their duties with due regard to the Trust's Equal Opportunities Policy.

Every day, our teams at Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust (NUH) make a difference. We save lives, we improve lives, and we usher in new life. We are proud to play a central role in supporting the health and wellbeing of people in Nottingham, Nottinghamshire and our surrounding communities.

With more than 20,000 colleagues, we are the largest employer in Nottinghamshire and one of the biggest and busiest NHS Trusts in the country, serving more than 2.5m residents of Nottingham and Nottinghamshire and a further four million people across the East Midlands and beyond. Our Trust spans over three sites including Queen's Medical Centre (QMC), Nottingham City Hospital and Ropewalk House.

We provide a range of national and internationally renowned specialist services, and we are at the forefront of new surgical procedures and research programmes.

We are home to the East Midlands Major Trauma Centre, the Nottingham Children's Hospital and in partnership with the University of Nottingham we host a Biomedical Research Centre carrying out vital research into hearing, digestive diseases, respiratory, musculoskeletal disease, mental health and imaging.

As a teaching hospital, we are instrumental in the education and training of doctors, nurses and other healthcare professionals. We are proud of our strong relationships with universities across the East Midlands, including the University of Nottingham, Nottingham Trent University and Loughborough University.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:

employer: Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board
title: Consultant Haematologist
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Consultant Haematologist to join a friendly and enthusiastic team at Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board. Whilst this appointment is a Health Board wide appointment, this post will be based at Prince Charles Hospital.

Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board is one of the largest Health Boards in Wales and was formed in 2019. It is situated near of the vibrant cities of Cardiff, Swansea and Bristol and is enriched with magnificent scenery including beautiful beaches and the stunning Brecon Beacons national park. Welsh history, culture, music and of course rugby lie at the heart of the Health Board.

Proposed Interview date: September 9th 2026

Welsh and/or English speakers are equally welcome to apply.

The post requires malignant and general haematological work. Candidates with any field of interest are encouraged to apply. However, it is desirable to have an interest and experience in haematological malignancy and chemotherapy. The work will be shared equally with the other consultants to provide clinical, laboratory, liaison haematology service and on call. The development of a special interest by the appointee is encouraged and would be in line with the clinical interest of the Health Board.

The haematology department at Cwm Taf Morgannwg UHB is also undergoing an exciting piece oftransformation work. This will lend itself to sub-specialisation and expansion and further development of all levels of the medical and nursing structure within the haematology service. Development and expansion of Advanced Nurse Practitioner, Clinical Nurse Specialist, Consultant Nurse, and Clinical Scientist posts are all being explored as a part of this on-going and dynamic work. Collaborative work with neighbouring health boards and trusts is also being explored.

The Cwm Taf Morgannwg UHB Haematology service, whilst performing BCSH level 2 Haematology, has close links with the regional Haematology and BMT centre based in the University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff,

Potential applicants are encouraged to visit and to meet the current team and consultants.

Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board is part of the NHS Wales family. Our Health Board provides primary, secondary and community health and wellbeing services to around 450,000 people living in three County Boroughs: Bridgend Merthyr Tydfil, and Rhondda Cynon Taf.

We live by our core values:

  • We listen, learn and improve
  • We treat everyone with respect
  • We all work together as one team

We are a proud local employer; around 80% of our 15000 workforce live within our region, making our staff not only our lifeblood of our organisation but of the diverse communities that we serve.

employer: The Hillingdon Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Neurological Rehabilitation
descriptionHtml:
This post consists of 10 Programmed Activities (PAs), annualized as 8.5 Direct Clinical Care (DCC) and 1.5 Supporting Clinical Activities (SPA). This is an appointment by the Hillingdon Hospital NHS Foundation Trust with license to attend at Imperial College NHS Trust. The post holder must hold full MRCP and a certificate of completion of training (CCT) in Rehabilitation Medicine. We welcome application from trainees in Rehabilitation Medicine who are approximately 6 months from CCT.

The appointee will join two consultants in Rehabilitation Medicine and a team of neurologists as part of a friendly and reputable service that works across Hillingdon Hospital and Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust to provide seamless transition for patients from tertiary care into secondary care and community services. This post provides an excellent opportunity to provide high quality neurological rehabilitation care for patients with spinal cord injury, in a busy District General Hospital or in a tertiary setting at Imperial. 6 of the DCC PA's will be based at the Hillingdon site and 4 PA's will be based primarily at Imperial.

The post holder will provide consultant input to the London Spinal Cord Injury Network and the Major Trauma Network in North West London. The post holder will be responsible for improving the care of spinal cord injury patients needing rehabilitation in the North West London sector. There is scope to develop integrated care across secondary and community services in partnership NW London ICB. This will involve linking with community teams and outreach visits to community settings.

The Hillingdon Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is the only acute Hospital in the London Borough of Hillingdon and offers a wide range of services including accident and emergency, inpatient care, day surgery, outpatient clinics and maternity services. The Trust's services at Mount Vernon Hospital include routine day surgery, delivered at a modern treatment centre, a minor injuries unit and outpatient clinics.

The safety and well-being of our patients and of our staff is paramount and we are making urgent improvements to address this - particularly in infection prevention and control. We are making progress and going forward by working in partnership with local GPs, charities,community services, academic partners, our local authority, neighbouring hospitals and the wider North West London Integrated care system, and ensuring that we listen and work in partnership with our local population. We are absolutely focused on ensuring that our hospitalsprovide high quality, safe and compassionate care, while drive forward the building of the new Hillingdon Hospital.

We have over 3,500 members of staff that are proud to care for nearly half a million people, with a vision to be an outstanding provider of healthcare through leading health and academic partnerships, transforming services, to provide the best care where needed.

title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:

Designed around you.

15-minute routine appointments: time to consult properly.

Non-duty clinical sessions: 12 appointments, plus 10 minutes for admin.

One paid admin session weekly, with the option to work from home.

Pro-rata duty rota managing online requests; infrequent home visits.

Mentoring, CPD and opportunities to develop clinical interests or contribute to education, service development and leadership.

Around 25,500 patients across three sites in Brighton, Hove and Portslade.

Pharmacy, paramedic and nursing colleagues support our work. Training is provided for working with neurodiverse, trans, non-binary and intersex patients.

WHO WERE LOOKING FOR

Full GMC registration; MRCGP or equivalent; general practice experience; safe clinical judgement; a collaborative, inclusive approach; and commitment to CPD, safeguarding and clinical governance. UK work eligibility and ability to work across all three sites are essential.

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and can discuss reasonable adjustments during recruitment.

As a GP, your clinical responsibilities include conducting surgery and telephone consultations, managing queries, home visits, repeat prescriptions, and timely correspondence. You will contribute to Enhanced Services, QOF/IIF initiatives, audits, and clinical standard setting. Additional duties include maintaining and developing patient records, summarising and Read-Coding data, and attending relevant training and events.

This role requires a commitment to quality care, continuous improvement, and teamwork in a dynamic and supportive environment.

Following the merger of two healthcare centres, we have become a diverse and innovative practice operating across three sites: Brunswick and Burwash in Hove, and Benfield in Portslade. With a patient population of 25,500, we pride ourselves on providing high-quality care to all, particularly focusing on disadvantaged populations. title: Consultant in Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Please note that candidates who interviewed unsuccessfully for this position within the last six months are currently ineligible to reapply. This policy allows time for meaningful professional development between applications.

An exciting opportunity has arisen to join United Lincolnshire Teaching Hospital NHS Trust (ULTH) as a Consultant in Accident and Emergency Department at Lincoln County Hospital.

We are looking for applicants with at least six months of experience within a Consultant capacity.

There is no better time to join our Trust as we have now been awarded Teaching Hospital Status.

We are currently recruiting for substantive consultant post in Pilgrim Hospital Boston in our Emergency Medicine at United Lincolnshire Hospitals. We are looking for consultants to provide the highest quality of care to each individual patient who attends the department. The appointee will be required to work in a 1:15 on call rota with a 1:5 weekend frequency. The job plan will be aligned to a 85% DCC and 15% SPA split.

Please note the job description has not been Royal College approved.

AAC panel interviews are being held on the 27th November 2026

The Appointee will be expected, in conjunction with his / her colleagues, to provide a comprehensive clinical, supervisory, educational and training support to the Emergency Department.

This is a substantive full time Consultant post in our Emergency Medicine department for the United Lincolnshire Teaching Hospital NHS Trust (ULTH). The purpose of this post is to ensure the highest quality of care is provided to each individual patient who attends the department. The on call supplement is currently category A and is classed as high frequency with an on call availability supplement of 8% currently payable. If the person appointed elects to undertake a part time contract, he / she will be required to devote substantially the whole of his / her professional time to the duties of the post and to give them priority at all times.

Any applicant who is unable for personal reasons to work full time will be eligible to be considered for the post. If such a person is appointed, modification of the content will be discussed on a personal basis with the Trust in consultation with consultant colleagues.

Apart from getting work within a talented team in a beautiful part of the country we offer an excellent relocation package.

Applicants must be on the GMC Specialist Register or within 6 months of their CCT. Applicants on the CESR/Portfolio pathway must have completed the process and be included on the Specialist Register.

You can expect a warm welcome at our United Lincolnshire Teaching Hospital NHS Trust (ULTH)our staff are friendly and welcoming. We listen to each other and work together to embed our Trusts values and behaviours. We appreciate our staff and reward them with an outstanding benefits package including a fantastic benefits package with competitive pay rates with annual increases, annual leave of 32 days plus Bank/Public holidays which normally is 8 days. Access to the NHS Pension Scheme to which you and the Trust contribute. Alongside this there are extensive training development opportunities. We promote a healthy work life balance, provide an Occupational Health Service to support you at work and have a number of NHS discounts available either directly through ourselves or online through NHS Discounts. As part of our recruitment process we can tell you more about our benefits package and you will see that we offer everything you would expect and more!

title: Group Work Facilitator
descriptionHtml:
Join our team as a Group Work Facilitator in Ludlow.

Our team in Ludlow is looking for a Group Work Facilitator to join them in providing high-quality support to people accessing our service. If you are enthusiastic, creative and passionate about helping others, wed love to hear from you.

Our South Shropshire Team offers a unique opportunity to work in one of the county's most rural communities, where no two days are ever the same. As a Group Work Facilitator, you'll enjoy the autonomy to work across towns and villages, building meaningful relationships with the people you support and becoming a valued part of the local community. This role will cover Ludlow, Bridgnorth and sites across the South of Shropshire.

Rural working allows for truly person-centred care, strong partnerships with local agencies and the chance to make a lasting difference where services can be harder to access. If you enjoy variety, independence, collaborative working and seeing the real impact of your work, our South Shropshire Team could be the perfect place for you to grow your career and change lives.

Please refer to the linked job description to support your application.

The closing date for this role is 8th November 2026; however, please note that this role may close early should sufficient applications be received, so early application is advised. All applicants should submit a CV and a covering letter on why youd like to be considered for this role.

As a Group Work Facilitator youll:

  • Provide a range of drug and alcohol-specific courses and psychosocial group-based activities in both 1:1 and group settings, using confidence-building and motivational techniques.
  • Deliver accredited training where required.
  • Work in partnership with people to evaluate their progress, identify their needs and develop realistic action plans, including ongoing reviews.
  • Use creative, innovative and evidence-based motivational interventions to support sustainable recovery and community reintegration.
  • Help people understand barriers to engagement and recognise the potential consequences of their behaviours.
  • Work collaboratively with colleagues and external partner agencies to provide effective group work interventions.
  • Involve the people we support in the design, development, delivery and evaluation of group work programmes.
  • Support colleagues, volunteers and Community Recovery Champions by providing advice and guidance where appropriate.
  • Work as part of the wider team to achieve targets, capture evidence and provide information for internal and external performance monitoring.

A driving licence and access to a vehicle are essential for this role, as youll be working across the South Shropshire area.

This role is full time and permanent, with a salary of £26,250 per annum. There will be some Saturday working on a rota basis to meet the needs of the service.

WithYou provides free and confidential support, without judgement, to more than 100,000 people every year experiencing challenges with drugs, alcohol and mental health across England and Scotland.

employer: York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Dermatologist
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Locum Consultant in Dermatology to join our friendly and supportive team on a 12-month contract. The department includes 11 consultants, a consultant/associate specialist, two specialist registrars on the Yorkshire rotation, hospital practitioners, a Physician Associate, GP trainees, Advanced Nurse Practitioners in skin cancer and specialist nursing teams.

The service has dedicated dermatology theatres and facilities for PDT, phototherapy and patch testing. Nurse-led services include dermatological surgery, leg ulcer and lymphoedema management, cryotherapy, drug monitoring, and skin cancer diagnosis and follow-up. We work closely with other specialties, including Maxillofacial Surgery, Plastic Surgery and Rheumatology.

The post is primarily based at York Hospital, with services also delivered at peripheral sites. An active teledermatology service supports advice and guidance and referral triage. Inpatient services are provided at York and Scarborough Hospitals through a weekday daytime on-call rota, supported by electronic referrals and remote review where appropriate.

The role includes general and specialist outpatient clinics, surgical lists and participation in the consultant on-call rota. Outpatient clinics will be held at York Hospital and one peripheral East Coast hospital.

This role provides general/specialist outpatient clinics and surgical lists plus contributing to the consultant on call rota. Outpatient clinics are at York Hospital and one peripheral East Coast hospital.You will join a well-established and collaborative department, focused on excellent, person-centred care. Within the Trust we are part of Clinical Support and Cancer Services Care Group, which includes most specialist medicine services. We have a Clinical Director responsible for all services.Individual job plans will be discussed with the post holder on appointment, with the Clinical Director to finalise the job plan which will become operational on commencement. All jobs' plans are agreed in line with the Trusts Job Planning Principles.

As a department we are committed to supporting flexible job plans and will work with you to mutually agree your activity commitment. We have opportunities to explore teaching, research and quality improvement projects to enhance our service.

We strive to support your leadership and development in role and would be keen to discuss development pathways and subspecialty interests; ensuring activity is allocated within your job plan to achieve this.

Our benefits

We offer a range of benefits to support our staff including:

  • Access to the NHS Pension Scheme, providing generous benefits upon retirement, as well as a lump sum and pension for dependants
  • 27 days holiday rising to 33 days (depending on NHS Trust service)
  • A variety of different types of paid and unpaid leave covering emergency and planned leave
  • Confidential advice and support on personal, work, family and relationship issues, 24/7, from our Employee Assistance Programme
  • NHS Car Lease scheme and Cycle to Work scheme
  • An extensive range of learning and development opportunities
  • Discounts on restaurants, getaways, shopping, motoring, cinema and finance from a range of providers

For further information on the fantastic range of benefits we offer please visit the Trust's dedicated Staff Benefits pages.

employer: Practice Plus Group - Health in Justice

title: Consultant Anaesthetics with an Interest in Peri-Operative Care & T&O
descriptionHtml:
It is an exciting time to join our welcoming and friendly team of 27 Anaesthetic Consultants based at Glangwili General Hospital. The successful candidate will support the current establishment of NHS and academic staff contributing to the on-call rota, and providing senior anaesthetic cover for elective, emergency and trauma surgery

There are opportunities for the successful candidate to deliver clinical care on emergency and trauma lists and gain further experience and expertise in a variety of specialities, including general surgery, ENT, and Ophthalmology.

The post is for a Consultant Anaesthetist with a specialist interest in Peri-operative medicine. The post holder will provide high quality care for patients within the anaesthetic Department and provide perioperative care for elective and emergency patients across the range of specialities available within Hywel Dda UHB. The candidate will join a team of consultants with an interest in Peri-operative medicine, doing High Risk pre-assessment, CPET clinics and assisting with our Pre-habilitation service.

Hywel Dda University Health Board plans and provides NHS healthcare services for people living in Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire, and bordering counties.

We have over 13,000 staff and together we provide primary, community, in-hospital, mental health and learning disabilities services.

We work in partnership with the three local authorities, as well as public, private and third sector colleagues, including our valued team of volunteers.

Our services are provided in:

  • Four main hospitals: Bronglais Hospital in Aberystwyth; Glangwili Hospital in Carmarthen; Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli; and Withybush Hospital in Haverfordwest
  • Five community hospitals: Amman Valley and Llandovery hospitals in Carmarthenshire; Tregaron Hospital in Ceredigion; and Tenby and South Pembrokeshire hospitals in Pembrokeshire
  • Two integrated care centres: Aberaeron and Cardigan in Ceredigion, and several other community settings
  • 47 general practices (six of which are health board managed practices); dental practices (including four orthodontic); 97 community pharmacies; 43 general ophthalmic practices; and 8 ophthalmic domiciliary providers
  • Numerous mental health and learning disabilities services

employer: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Consultant Respiratory Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The respiratory department operates a phased working job pattern. The appointee will be on ward duty (Respiratory Ward) for 1 week (7 days) at a time on a 1:5 rota. The respiratory consultants contribute equally to a 1:11 rota for respiratory in-reach to the AAU at HRI. 1 PA is allocated for respiratory inreach duties for week days. The workload for this will be variable as per respiratory admissions to the AAU; winter months see a higher number. Respiratory Consultants are helped by a SpR as well and work can be distributed as per requirements. There will be consideration of time off in lieu (such as for weekend working). Six new patients per clinic will be booked as standard. At the start of the post we do not anticipate follow up patients to be booked in to clinic. In due course when follow-up slots are required 1 new patient slot will equate to 2 follow up patients.

The new appointee will be allocated a consultant colleague to mentor and support them when they start.

The candidate will be supporting both the Asthma and Sleep/ NIV service. The successful candidate will also be expected to develop the CPET/Breathlessness Service

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.

Together we employ nearly 20,000 staff. Our five main hospital sites are Diana, Princess of Wales Hospital, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole and District Hospital, for NLAG and Hull Royal Infirmary and Castle Hill Hospital for HUTH.

As Teaching Hospitals working with the Hull York Medical School, we both lead and contribute to research in many areas - biomedical research, primary care, palliative medicine, cardiovascular and respiratory medicine, vascular surgery, cancer surgery and oncology.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

employer: NELFT North East London Foundation Trust
title: Community Adult Consultant Psychiatrist MHWT East
descriptionHtml:
Community Adult Consultant Psychiatrist

This post is for an Adult Consultant Psychiatrist position in the East Mental Health & Wellness Team (MHWT-E), based at Beam Park Health Centre, 2 Halewood Way, Rainham, RM13 8QZ.

This is a replacement, substantive, full-time post - 10 Programmed Activities (PAs) post with 7.5 Direct Clinical Contact activities (DCC) and 2.5 Supporting Professional Activities (SPAs).

On-call responsibility: The postholder will be part of the Senior Psychiatrist on-call rota covering out of hours and weekends for Mental Health Services in NELFT. The on call will cover service delivery for Adults and Older Adults presenting with mental health problems. This is currently a 1:50 rota with a 3% Category A salary supplement. The trust has also a daytime (9am - 5pm) Section 136 rota, with an approximate frequency of one day every three months.

The successful candidate will work as part of a multidisciplinary team providing care to adults with mental health needs who are registered with a GP Practice located in the eastern part of the London Borough of Barking & Dagenham (plus a small number of patients who reside in that part of the Borough but whose GP is elsewhere). This roughly equates to residents of the Electoral Wards named East Brook, Alibon, Goresbrook, River and Village on the borough map in Section 3.1 below.

The successful candidate will provide senior medical support to the team, and direct input on clinical cases. The consultant will be expected to provide guidance and supervision to the team, work directly with adult patients (and their families), and liaise as appropriate with other external mental health providers, and acute hospitals.

NELFT NHS Foundation Trust provides mental health and community services for over 4.9 million people living in the London Boroughs of Waltham Forest, Redbridge, Barking and Dagenham, Havering, and across Essex. We work to ensure our patients, their friends and family, feel confident that their health needs are well met. With an excellent reputation for research and development, our skilled health professionals are at the cutting edge of evidence-based innovation, opening up the possibilities for better ways of working and delivery of care.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team
descriptionHtml:
We are recruiting for a full-time Consultant Psychiatrist to join ourCrisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team (CRHTT) based at Saffron House in High Wycombe where you will have an active leadership role and medical responsibility for the diagnosis, management and treatment of adults of working age and older adults who are at risk of developing a mental health crisis.

With your expertise in Adult Psychiatry, you'll join our multi-disciplinary team (MDT) to deliver patient care through home treatment enabling early discharge from inpatient care. You'll work closely with inpatient wards and community teams, including the Inpatient Social Work service and the Patient Flow Transformation lead.

We offer rewarding career development with protected SPA time as part of your job plan, encouraging you to take leadership courses to enhance your skills. We also offer a relocation allowance of up to £8,000 for external applicants (subject to eligibility criteria).

Applicants must be fully registered with the General Medical Council (GMC) and on the Specialist Register or be within six months attaining their Certificate of Completion of Training (CCT) or an equivalent approved indicator of training.

Could this be the next step in your career? Come and join one of the UK's leading mental health Trusts at the forefront of research infrastructure and make a real difference to people's lives.

This role provides senior medical input and clinical leadership to the Buckinghamshire Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team (CRHTT). You will have responsibility for your own patients as well as those patients seen by medical staff under your supervision.

The key components of the CRHTT service are:

1. Crisis response (emergency assessments and reviews)

2. Intensive home treatment characterized by the availability of multiple visits each day which are of a length and content to allow for specialist psycho-social intervention to be delivered

3. Gate-keeping admissions to psychiatric beds

4. Enabling early discharge from psychiatric admission

The CRHTT provide crisis response and inpatient gate-keeping and a home treatment service to service users leaving inpatient care and living within South Bucks. There will be a phased approach to future expansion which will be dependent on further new investment. The nature and speed of phasing will also take account of CRHTT model fidelity and assessment of safety and quality in relation to existing service provision (i.e. whatever is developed will have good fit and add value to user / care experience).

title: Consultant Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust (CWPT) is seeking to recruit a Consultant Child & Adolescent Psychiatrist who will be responsible for treating children and young adults up to the age of 18 years at Parkview Clinic, Birmingham. The post holder will provide senior specialist psychiatric input and medical leadership within an established multidisciplinary inpatient team. They will have a central role in delivering psychiatric assessment and treatment for inpatients and their families, as well as contributing to providing psychiatric and medical risk management.

The post holder will behave consistently with the values and beliefs of the organization, act as a role model to colleagues, and use their initiative to take responsibility for the quality of their work and the service provided to patients. locations: Cambridge Bio Medical Campus, United Kingdom
descriptionHtml:
This is a Clinical Fellowship in Advanced Heart Failure, Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) and Heart Transplantation. The post is available for one year, with a possibility of extension by mutual agreement.

This Fellowship post in the Transplant Unit at Royal Papworth Hospital provides an opportunity for a Cardiologist to receive sub-specialty training in the management of advanced heart failure, mechanical circulatory support and heart transplantation.

The post-holder will work with the six existing Transplant Cardiologists and one Health Education East of England rotating cardiology registrar as part of the wider Transplant Team. The post will provide experience and training in all aspects of inpatients and outpatient care of advanced heart failure and heart transplant patients.

Successful candidates in the role will receiving training opportunities on par with a UK trainee and the post-holder will have a trained and named educational supervisor, be mentored by the existing team with regular meetings and oversight by the whole team.

Informal visits can be arranged through Dr Pettit or Dr Bhagra.

The post-holder will be responsible to the Clinical Lead of the Transplant Unit and accountable to the Medical Director when undertaking the following duties:

1.Delivery of patient care under Consultant supervision, seeking advice or assistance as required according to level of experience.

2.To read and abide by the standard operating procedures of the Transplant unit.

3.Completion of accurate records, such as patient notes and discharge summaries.

4.Attendance at clinics, catheter labs, ward rounds and clinical meetings.

5.Undertaking procedures which will be directly or indirectly supervised as appropriate for level of experience.

6.Participation in clinical audit and research

7.Participation in regular timetabled teaching of other junior medical staff, students and non-medical staff.

8.Participation in training activities, maintaining portfolio and personal development plan.

9.Attendance at mandatory training.

10.Compliance with the policies and procedures of the Trust.

11.Adherence to the working pattern of the specialty and participating in the monitoring of hours as required by the Trust.

12.Notify the appropriate consultant if unavailable to attend work

13.Booking annual leave in accordance with the departmental arrangements and policies of Trust

Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is the UK's leading heart and lung hospital, delivering care to more than 50,000 patients a year in its new state-of-the-art hospital in Cambridge. We perform the most heart and/or lung transplants in the UK and carried out the UK's first successful heart transplant in 1979. It also offers emergency heart attack treatment, sleep centre care and is one of just five centres nationally for those in severe respiratory failure.

Based on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus the largest centre of medical research and health science in Europe the Trust is at the heart of treatments of the future. Royal Papworth became the first hospital trust in the country to be rated outstanding in all five areas assessed by the Care Quality Commission - a rating it still holds today. The Trust holds its values of compassion, excellence & collaboration at its core, and all colleagues joining the team are expected to uphold these in their day-to-day roles & interactions. Royal Papworth is proud of its diverse workforce and encourages people to embrace their individuality.

The Trust values difference and welcomes all applications irrespective of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy & maternity, race, religion & belief, sex and sexual orientation. Providing they meet the minimum post criteria, applicants with disabilities will be offered an interview.

For a street view tour: https://royalpapworth.nhs.uk/virtual-tour
