employer: Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Radiologist - Non-Vasc Interventional Radiology
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Consultant Radiologist to join a friendly, forward-thinking team of 30 Consultant Radiologists at the Royal United Hospital Bath.

This post is for a Consultant Radiologist with specialist interest in Non-Vascular Interventional Radiology (10 PAs).

This post will help meet the increase in demand for interventional and diagnostic radiology services and to help us establish and provide an interventional oncology service.

The post is full time but anyone wishing to work part time is also encouraged to apply. The post includes participation in the IR on-call rota (participation in the diagnostic on-call rota is optional). Home PACS links are available.

Candidates are encouraged to visit the hospital and can make arrangements through contacting the Clinical Lead: Dr Gary Cross (gary.cross@nhs.net) or Dr Joseph Keighley, Consultant Interventional Radiologist (joseph.keighley@nhs.net).

This is a replacement post following retirement for a substantive Consultant Interventional Radiologist.

The candidate must be able to provide a range of non-vascular interventional radiology procedures and ideally will be competent in haemorrhage control. This role also demands a good level of diagnostic radiology competence and another specialist area of interest is encouraged but not essential. The post holder will contribute to the general radiology work of the department in conjunction with the other radiologists all of whom perform regular sessions in general radiology.

The case mix in interventional radiology at the RUH predominantly comes from our busy Urology, Gastroenterology and Surgical departments and from a wide range of oncological services. Approximately 1300 IR procedures are performed per year. Specialist nurses and radiographers undertake some vascular access in addition to 3 established IR consultants. With this new appointment we will provide a 1:5 IR on call service (weekends 0800-1800 only) and our aim is to establish an interventional oncology practice providing thermal ablation and some elective embolisation. We have links with North Bristol NHS Trust who provide tertiary level IR services.

At the RUH we're proud to put people at the heart of what we do, working together as one team to make a difference for our patients, each other, and our community. No matter what your role is, we value everyone's contribution in supporting the exceptional, person-centred care we pride ourselves on.

We are committed to creating a compassionate and inclusive environment. This can be seen in our growing community of staff networks - celebrating successes and creating opportunities to listen and learn. We value our differences, champion kindness and civility, and truly believe that diversity makes us stronger.

A culture of learning, developing and innovating is the thread that runs throughout our whole organisation. We want to support you to thrive, taking your career to its full potential.

We value staff wellbeing, with a well-established programme of support. We believe in a holistic approach spanning all aspects of living a healthy life, including physical, emotional, spiritual and financial wellbeing. We've even got a pool!

We are committed to supporting you and hope you want to join our team. In the meantime, find out more about living and working the beautiful historic city of Bath, learn about our extensive package of staff benefits, and read about how we're providing healthcare fit for the future with the landmark Dyson Cancer Centre and our passion for research.

title: Consultant Oncoplastic Breast Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Consultant Oncoplastic Breast Surgeon to join Somerset NHS Foundation Trust's county-wide breast service. Based primarily at Musgrove Park Hospital in Taunton, you will join a highly experienced multidisciplinary team delivering comprehensive breast care across Somerset. Clinical sessions at Yeovil District Hospital will be undertaken as required.

Working alongside consultant breast surgeons, breast radiologists, consultant radiographers, breast clinicians, advanced practitioners and specialist nurses, you will play a key role in delivering high-quality, patient-centred breast cancer and benign breast services.

The breadth of expertise within the team supports a truly patient-centred approach to care, fostering close multidisciplinary collaboration across the entire breast care pathway and providing an excellent environment for service development, innovation, education and professional growth.

This post offers an excellent opportunity to contribute to the continued development of an innovative and expanding oncoplastic and reconstructive breast surgery service. It offers a Monday to Friday working pattern with no on call commitment and it attracts a 10 PA per week job plan.

Applications are welcomed whether you are an experienced Breast Surgeon looking to relocate to the beautiful somerset countryside or a newly qualified Consultant who has or will be completing their CCT within the coming months.

  • Deliver expert assessment, treatment and surgical care for patients with symptomatic and screening detected breast disease.
  • Undertake outpatient activity, including one-stop, new diagnosis, reconstructive, surgical planning and postoperative clinics.
  • Undertake regular operating lists, providing oncoplastic and reconstructive procedures within the post holder's scope of competence.
  • Participate fully in breast multidisciplinary team meetings and support evidence-informed treatment decisions.
  • Work collaboratively across the multidisciplinary breast team and with oncology, pathology, genetics and tertiary services.
  • Provide clear and compassionate information to patients, supporting informed and shared decision making.
  • Maintain accurate clinical records and practise in accordance with professional standards, Trust policies and clinical governance requirements.
  • Contribute to service improvement programmes that enhance clinical outcomes, patient experience and staff experience.
  • Support innovative and sustainable models of breast care, aligned with evidence-informed practice and the needs of patients across Somerset.
  • Help develop the oncoplastic and reconstructive breast surgery service, including partial breast reconstruction and perforator flap techniques where appropriate.
  • Use clinical audit, quality improvement methods, service data and patient feedback to identify and deliver improvements.
  • Contribute to the development and review of clinical pathways, guidelines and standards.

At Somerset NHS Foundation Trust, we're committed to supporting our employees with a range of benefits designed to enhance your professional and personal life. We offer:

  • Flexible working options to help you balance work and life
  • NHS pension scheme for long-term financial security
  • Generous annual leave allowance to recharge and relax
  • A strong focus on career development to help you grow and achieve your potential

Additionally, you'll gain access to our Blue Light Card, unlocking exclusive discounts on shopping, dining, and leisure activities, as well as NHS-specific perks to support you both inside and outside of work.

We are proud to foster a diverse, skilled, and inclusive workforce, and we encourage applications from all backgrounds.

Why Somerset? Somerset offers the perfect blend of idyllic countryside, outstanding areas of natural beauty, and breathtaking coastlines, with vibrant cities like Bristol, Bath, and Exeter just a short drive away - and only two hours to London.

The region is home to excellent educational facilities, and with affordable housing compared to other parts of the country, it's a great place to build both your career and your future.

Somerset truly has it all - the peaceful countryside and cosmopolitan city life, with something for everyone to enjoy.

The Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust (PAHT) is proud to care for the communities of West Essex, delivering safe, compassionate, and high-quality services. title: Salaried GP - HMP Haverigg + £1500 Retention Payment
descriptionHtml:

Previous experience working within a secure environment is not essential as full induction and training will be provided. More critical are the personal attributes encompassing a passion for the delivery of high quality primary care, a desire to innovate and transform models of service delivery to meet the current challenges encountered across all sectors of primary care, and a willingness to work as part of a transformative integrated provider team.

Please note the Retention payment is payable to new candidates joining Spectrum Community Health CIC.

We aim to be flexible in matching your availability with our work patterns and the needs of the service and therefore we are also able to offer part time and flexible working options.

As Lead GP your time will be dedicated to on-site clinical care provision as a critical member of an experienced and passionate multi-disciplinary primary healthcare team. You will be involved in blended model of care delivery comprising both face to face primary care and complex case care planning as part of an MDT. You will be responsible for providing clinical leadership and support to members of the prison's healthcare team. Working with your Head of Healthcare and North West Regional Lead GP you will be responsible for overseeing the development and delivery of GP clinical services on site. As Lead GP you will be supported by clinical leaders within Spectrum representing Medical Education, Clinical Substance Misuse, and Remote Clinical working to enable you to support the delivery of an innovative, digitally enabled, future focused primary care model.

BE THE DIFFERENCE IN HEALTHCARE

Join our team

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Join a practice where there is time to do the job properly.

We're looking for a 4-6 session Salaried GP to join our team at Wem and Prees Medical Practice.

We are a Tier 2 Sponsoring Practice, open to a flexible start date.

Serving just over 12,000 patients across two sites, we are an established training practice with a reputation for supporting GPs at every stage of their career, from newly qualified doctors taking their first post after CCT through to experienced GPs looking for a fresh challenge.

Our approach is built around sustainability, collaboration and quality patient care.

What we offer:

  • 15-minute face-to-face appointments,
  • a total of 21 appointments per day,
  • low visiting numbers
  • protected morning coffee break where clinicians come together to share advice, discuss cases and support one another.

Working alongside an experienced multidisciplinary team, you'll be part of a practice that embraces new ways of working while maintaining the personal relationships and continuity of care that general practice is all about.

If you're looking for a role where you'll be valued, supported and given the time to provide high-quality patient care, we'd love to hear from you.

Based in the market town of Wem, with a dispensing branch surgery in nearby Prees, Shrewsbury with it's beautiful riverside walks and quirky independent shopping is only 20 mins away by road or rail, Chester and Birmingham and the wider motorway network are all within an hours driving.

We are seeking a 4-6 session Salaried GP to provide NHS Primary Medical Services to our patients.

The role includes the full range of duties expected of a GP, including clinical sessions, home visits, medical examinations and other day-to-day clinical responsibilities.

We recognise that starting a new role can be a significant step, and we are committed to providing the support needed to help you settle into the practice.

Our salaried GP team is led by a dedicated GP Partner, and you will benefit from regular one-to-one meetings, mentorship and structured support throughout your probationary period to ensure a smooth transition.

Following an initial settling-in period, there will be a shared commitment to the practice duty doctor rota. This responsibility is distributed fairly amongst the doctors, regularly reviewed and supported by an experienced Duty Receptionist team. Our duty system works well, supporting new ways of working while maintaining safe, effective patient care.

We're looking for someone who enjoys working as part of a team, values continuity of care and is committed to providing high quality patient care.

You'll be joining a supportive and collaborative practice where colleagues are approachable, new ideas are welcomed and everyone contributes to the continued development of the service.

If you would like to have an informal conversation or arrange a practice visit, please contact Caroline Morris, Managing Partner, by email caroline.morris22@nhs.net or 01939 238051

About Us

Wem and Prees Medical Practice serves just over 12,000 patients across our surgeries in Wem and Prees, North Shropshire.

We're proud to be a stable, well-established practice with a strong team ethos. Many of our staff have worked here for a number of years, creating a supportive environment where colleagues know each other well and work together to deliver high-quality patient care.

We are committed to developing and retaining our clinicians for the long term. Several of our current Salaried GPs joined us early in their careers and have become valued members of the team. Where partnership opportunities arise, we look to our Salaried GPs in the first instance, providing a potential pathway for those interested in future leadership and practice ownership.

Whether you are an experienced GP or looking for your first role after CCT, you will be joining a practice that invests in its people and supports their development.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary of £11,500 per session
  • BMA model contract
  • 6 weeks annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata)
  • Additional day's leave on your birthday
  • NHS Pension Scheme
  • Free parking and staff refreshments
  • Support for continuing professional development and career progression
  • Tier 2 Sponsorship available

Please note that we reserve the right to close this advertisement early should sufficient applications be received.

title: Care Coordinator (PCN)
descriptionHtml:
At North Liverpool Primary Care Network, we pride ourselves on being a forward-thinking organisation that embraces innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement. Working within our Care Coordinator team, you will thrive in a fast-paced environment where no two days are the same. You will play a pivotal role in supporting patients to access the right services at the right time, helping to improve outcomes and patient experience across our network.

As a key member of the team, you will also act as an ambassador for the work of the PCN, helping to showcase our services, successes and community impact through social media and digital engagement. You will be the link between our teams, patients and wider stakeholders, promoting the valuable work taking place across the network and ensuring our achievements are shared with the communities we serve.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is proactive, organised and passionate about making a difference, with the ability to build strong relationships, adapt to changing priorities and contribute to the continued development of innovative primary care services.

Why join us?

Be part of a progressive and supportive PCN focused on improving patient care.

Work in a varied and dynamic role with opportunities to develop new skills.

Help shape and promote innovative services that make a real difference to local communities.

Join a team that values collaboration, creativity and continuous improvement.

This role offers the opportunity to be at the heart of Primary Care Network development, supporting projects that make a real difference to patients, practices and the wider community. With a varied workload and no two days the same, it is ideal for someone who enjoys building relationships and contributing to innovative healthcare services.

As a Care Coordinator, you will work with PCN leaders, practice teams and partner organisations to improve patient care and access to services. You will support patients with personalised care needs, helping them navigate health and community services and access the right support at the right time.

You will help promote the work of the PCN through social media, patient engagement activities and health campaigns, raising awareness of local services, screening programmes, immunisations and wellbeing initiatives. You will also support the Patient Participation Group, gather patient feedback and contribute to service improvements.

Working closely with the PCN Manager, Clinical Director and partner organisations, you will support quality improvement projects, audits and healthcare programmes while developing partnerships that enhance integrated patient care.

This is an exciting opportunity for a proactive and organised individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and wants to play a key role in improving health outcomes across North Liverpool.

North Liverpool is the largest Primary Care Network (PCN) in Liverpool, comprising 21 aligned GP practices serving a weighted population of approximately 150,000 patients. Our network brings together forward-thinking GP practices and multidisciplinary healthcare professionals who are dedicated to delivering high-quality, patient-centred, and integrated care. Through collaboration and innovation, we strive to improve health outcomes and meet the evolving needs of our diverse local communities.

title: Clinical Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic, confident, patient-focused and practice based Clinical Pharmacist to become a valued member of our friendly, supportive practice team.

Ideally, you will bring previous General Practice experience with an IP qualification and a strong passion for delivering safe, high-quality, and effective care within primary care. This is an exciting chance to make a meaningful impact on patient care.

As a Clinical Pharmacist, you will work as an integral part of the multidisciplinary team, using your clinical expertise to optimise medicines, improve patient outcomes and promote the safe and effective use of medicines.

You will undertake structured medication reviews, support patients with long-term conditions, provide clinical advice to patients and colleagues, and contribute to medicines optimisation and quality improvement initiatives.

Although full time is preferable we can be flexible for the right candidate.

Undertake structured medication reviews and medicines optimisation to improve patient outcomes safety and adherence.

Provide clinical advice to GPs, nurses and the wider multidisciplinary team on prescribing and medicines-related issues.

Support the management of patients with long-term conditions, including medication review, monitoring and follow-up.

Identify and manage medication-related risks, including interactions, adverse effects, contraindications and inappropriate prescribing.

Support medicines reconciliation following hospital discharge and changes in care.

Provide patients with clear advice and counselling on their medicines, promoting adherence and shared decision-making.

Support safe, effective and cost-effective prescribing in line with NICE guidance, local formularies and practice policies.

Contribute to repeat prescribing, medicines safety, clinical audits, quality improvement and prescribing reviews.

Work collaboratively with community and hospital pharmacy teams and other healthcare professionals to ensure continuity of care.

Maintain accurate clinical records and comply with professional, legal, confidentiality and information governance requirements.

Participate in multidisciplinary meetings, clinical governance and service development.

Maintain professional competence through continuing professional development and work within GPhC standards

We are a progressive, friendly GP practice serving a diverse patient population. Our team includes GPs, Practice nurses, Specialist nurses (Respiratory, diabetes and family planning) HCAs, pharmacists, paramedics and administrative staff who work collaboratively to provide safe, effective, and holistic care. We value innovation, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

title: Substance Use Nurse (Registered Mental Health Nurse), Part Time
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Substance Use Nurse to join our service in South Ayrshire.

Our team in South Ayrshire is recruiting for an experienced Substance Use Nurse, to join them in providing high quality recovery care to a diverse service user group. If you are an enthusiastic and creative registered nurse, passionate about changing people's lives for the better, we'd love to hear from you.As our Substance Use Nurse, you will provide a range of health and wellbeing and harm reduction interventions to service users in accordance with the agreed model of service delivery. title: Consultant Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist in Eating Disorders
descriptionHtml:
This is a new post which has been created as part of a successful bid to expand community eating disorders for children and young people.

The post holder will provide senior clinical leadership and psychiatric expertise within a specialist multidisciplinary team delivering evidence-based care for young people with eating disorders. The service combines intensive day hospital treatment and home-based interventions, offering a flexible and family-centred approach to prevent or shorten inpatient admissions and support sustainable recovery. In addition, as it is a new service, the post holder will have the opportunity to provide medical leadership in its development.

Specific responsibilities may include:o Provide specialist psychiatric assessment and management for young people with eating disorders and co-occurring mental health conditions.o Lead on formulation, care planning, and review within a multidisciplinary team including psychologists, nurses, dietitians, family therapists, occupational therapists, and social workers.o Offer psychiatric input for both Day Hospital (maximum 6 patients) and the Intensive Support at Home Team (up to 5 patients) components of the service. While this is a new service, it is anticipated that there will be one new patient for each service weekly, although the day patients will likely already open to the home support team. Therefore, it is expected that the post holder will see one new patient per week for psychiatric assessment and 10 follow up reviews per week.o Oversee pharmacological treatments, physical health monitoring, and mental state management.o Participate in family-based interventions, working collaboratively with carers to promote recovery and resilience.o Support early identification of risk and contribute to crisis management plans.o Liaise effectively with community CAMHS, paediatric, education, and social care services to ensure continuity of care.o Contribute to admission avoidance and step-down care from inpatient units.

At Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust (CWPT), we deliver a wide range of physical, mental health, learning disability and autism services, and are proud to serve communities across Coventry, Warwickshire and beyond.

We put 'people at our heart'; this ethos is at the centre of everything we do and how we do it. We care for our staff and colleagues as much as they care for others and offer a wide range of benefits and development opportunities.

  • generous annual leave entitlement which increases during your time with us
  • excellent learning and development opportunities, including apprenticeship frameworks, distance learning, internal training, coaching and mentoring, and much more
  • salary sacrifice schemes for lease car/ vehicle, Cycle to Work, home and electronics, gym membership and more
  • discounts with a range of retailers, restaurants and entertainment venues through our Employee Assistance Programme and NHS discount schemes
  • wellbeing support, including an in-house counselling service, external helpline and more
  • staff networks and support group

We're always on the lookout for people who share our passion for improving the lives and wellbeing of people in our community, as well as our values of compassion, collaboration, excellence, integrity and respect.

title: Salaried GP - Long Term Conditions

The role has a particular focus on long-term condition management, personalised care planning, advance care planning, and future care conversations. The successful candidate will work collaboratively with patients, carers, and multidisciplinary colleagues to ensure care is coordinated, holistic, and aligned with patients' individual goals, preferences, and values.

The successful candidate will:

  • Be fully qualified and registered with the General Medical Council (GMC).
  • Hold a licence to practise and be included on the NHS Performers List.
  • Have excellent clinical assessment and decision-making skills.
  • Be confident managing both acute and long-term health conditions.
  • Possess strong communication and multidisciplinary working skills.
  • Be committed to maintaining high standards of patient care and clinical governance.

The ideal candidate will have worked with boarding communities in the past and be aware of The Medical Officers of Schools Association. (MOSA). Professional experience providing primary healthcare to children and young adults is essential.

Please note: This vacancy is for 6 sessions per week

Working within the East Northants Neighbourhood Team, you will provide high-quality clinical care while championing personalised care planning and shared decision-making. You will work collaboratively with a range of healthcare professionals to improve patient outcomes, enhance quality of life, and support individuals to manage their health effectively.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Delivering comprehensive Long-Term Condition (LTC) reviews and supporting achievement of QOF targets.
  • Developing and maintaining high-quality, personalised care plans tailored to patients' individual needs and goals.
  • Leading Future Care Planning conversations, helping patients understand and plan their ongoing healthcare needs.
  • Facilitating Advance Care Planning discussions and ensuring patients' wishes and preferences are appropriately documented.
  • Supporting and completing Respect Plans, promoting patient choice, dignity, and shared decision-making.
  • Working collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team to provide coordinated and holistic care.
  • Contributing to service development, quality improvement initiatives, and innovative models of care.

Lakeside Healthcare is a large GP partnership that provides NHS care for around 170,000 patients across Cambridgeshire, Peterborough, Northamptonshire and Lincolnshire. We are made of eight GP practices across 14 sites that are part of their local communities.

We work together as practices to provide resilience, sharing learning and professional back-office support services.

Our most important asset is our people, who provide care for our patients and help run our surgeries smoothly. We employ over 500 clinical and non-clinical staff, and we invest in training and developing to ensure that we retain and attract good quality staff who want to stay with us and be part of our team.

We are proud of what we do and strive to demonstrate our values of Caring, Respect, Quality and Teamwork in everything we do.

Oundle is a beautiful historic market town in Northamptonshire, adjacent to Cambridgeshire, and boasts excellent local educational institutions, including Church of England schools and a prominent private boarding and day school.

title: General Practitioner (Salaried)
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an enthusiastic Salaried GP to join our expanding practice for 4 - 6 sessions per week

We welcome applications from experienced and newly qualified GP's.

The post holder will carry out duties expected of a NHS General Practitioner using expected standards in line with national and local guidelines and policy. We operate on 15 minute appointments and use Systmconnect for e-consultations and triage although we offer flexibility to patients in access to services.

The Garth Surgery in Guisborough is nestled at the edge of the Cleveland hills and maintains access to major urban centres alongside spectacular countryside and the Yorkshire coastline.

We are 7 partners, 3 salaried GP's and 3 ANP's alongside a hardworking nursing and administration team. We are a training practice and active in research. We operate from a recently refurbished and extended practice building. We have a growing list of nearly 11,700 patients and use Systmone clinical software.

We are a member of East Cleveland Primary Care Network and our team is enhanced by ARRS professionals in supportive roles.

We are heavily involved in training and research, having been rewarded Primary Care Research Hub Status by the Department of Health.

employer: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Urology Consultant
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen to join UHB Trust as a Locum Consultant Urological Surgeon preferably with special interest in functional and reconstructive urology on the QE site.

The Urology department at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital includes 13 consultants, 1 clinical scientist and a Cancer and Benign Nursing Team with middle grade and junior doctor support.

The successful applicant will join a team of 2 consultant colleagues providing predominantly subspecialist services in male and female incontinence, complex bladder dysfunction and urinary tract reconstruction.

University Hospitals Birmingham (UHB) is one of the largest teaching hospital trusts in England, serving a regional, national, and international population.

Our sites at Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, Solihull Hospital and Community Services, Good Hope Hospital in Sutton Coldfield and Birmingham Chest Clinic allow people to be treated as close to home as possible.

The Terms and Conditions of service are offered on a 10 Programmed Activity basis. The post includes participation in a 1 in 12 oncall rota supported by an oncall registrar.

The ability to communicate and work effectively as part of a multi-disciplinary team is vital. It is also anticipated that the successful candidate would contribute to increasing the national profile of the department.

A strong commitment from the appointee to the Department and involvement with governance and audit is expected.

The post holder will support the Functional Urology service at UHB (Based at the QE however with an operating list at Solihull), and work as part of a larger Urology Team that includes both Cancer and Benign Subspecialities.

The successful applicant should ideally have post CCT level experience in functional and reconstructive urology.

The post holder will be supported by a dedicated team of specialist trainees and SAS doctors and will have regular outpatient and diagnostic clinics.

The post holder will be expected to also partake in the on-call Rota based at the QE site.

The post holder must be fully registered with the General Medical Council with a licence to practise and is advised to maintain up to date membership of a recognised medical defence organisation. The successful candidate is expected to be aware of local policies and procedures and comply with the standing orders and standing financial instructions of the Trusts.

University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust strives to have an inclusive culture where everyone feels like they belong, can thrive, knows that they add value and feels valued. We do this by developing compassionate and culturally competent leaders, being values driven in all that we do and by creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace that thrives on the diversity of our people. As such we want to attract and recruit talented individuals from all backgrounds, and for each of you to feel supported for the diversity you bring, to achieve your full potential. For those staff with a disability, including physical disability, long term health condition, mental health or neurodiverse condition, this also means being committed to making reasonable adjustments needed for you to carry out your role.

title: Consultant Ophthalmologist
descriptionHtml:
UNLOCK YOUR BEST WORK LIFE

+ MAKE A DIFFERENCE FOR EVERY PATIENT

Were looking for a confident, high-volume Consultant Ophthalmologist to join our friendly, professional ophthalmology team at our Gillingham Surgical Centre. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced consultant who is passionate about delivering outstanding patient care in a safe, supportive and well-run environment.

Youll be joining a centre of excellence in ophthalmology, with access to modern facilities, streamlined pathways and a highly skilled multidisciplinary team. This role is ideally suited to a consultant seeking a part-time employed position, alongside existing NHS or private practice.

If youre looking for a rewarding, stable role where you can focus on high-quality ophthalmic care while maintaining flexibility alongside existing commitments, wed love to hear from you.

As our Consultant Ophthalmologist, you will be:

  • Delivering high-volume cataract surgery, including phacoemulsification under topical anaesthesia
  • Providing pre-operative, intra-operative and post-operative ophthalmic care
  • Contributing specialist expertise in oculoplastics and medical retina / Wet AMD
  • Working closely with fellow consultants, nursing teams and wider MDT colleagues to deliver excellent patient outcomes
  • Participating in outpatient clinics, theatre sessions and clinical governance activity
  • Supporting service development, audit and continuous improvement within the ophthalmology service
  • Playing an active role in maintaining high clinical standards, patient safety and quality outcomes

As a confident, independent high-volume cataract surgeon with at least 5-years experience as a NHS consultant, you will also have:

  • Proven experience in cataract surgery, with additional skills in oculoplastics and Wet AMD

  • A strong clinical quality and outcomes record
  • Excellent communication skills and a collaborative, team-focused approach

What you can expect in return:

  • A competitive salary based on experience

To apply for the role, click on the link below. If you have any questions, contact sarah.melder@practiceplusgroup.com in our friendly resourcing team.

employer: Kingston and Richmond NHS Foundation Trust
title: Specialty Doctor in ENT
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to appoint an innovative and high performing individual to join our well-established and progressive Ear, Nose and Throat Department at Kingston Hospital of Kingston and Richmond NHS Foundation Trust.

The successful candidate would complement a department of multi-disciplinary professionals, (including advanced audiologist practitioners and voice therapists), who collectively deliver acute and elective ENT services, both general and subspecialty, for all disciplines. The service is delivered as part of the Southwest London clinical network, and we have close links with St George's Hospital and Royal Marsden Hospital where patients receive cancer treatment.

We also run ENT clinics at Queen Mary's Hospital and Cobham Day Surgery Hospital. Our Audiology department is fully accredited by UKAS under the IQIPS version 2 standard.

A comprehensive clinical service is provided for the management and treatment of a wide range of diseases and disorders of hearing, balance, voice, swallowing, smell and taste. Our multidisciplinary service is delivered as part of an integrated care network covering South West London and Surrey.

Aspen Building, which is a purpose-built outpatient unit at Kingston Hospital provides six examination and interventional procedure rooms, co-located radiology and histopathology clinics for same day FNAs, voice therapy and a full paediatric and adult audiology suite together with associated office and staff facilities.

Queen Mary's Hospital offers four outpatient consultation and procedure rooms, two audiology consultation and procedure rooms, three sound proofed test booths, an Otoneurology assessment room and hearing aid store.

title: PCN Frailty GP
descriptionHtml:
We have a fantastic opportunity for an experienced and motivated GP to join Folkestone, Hythe & Rural Primary Care Network as a Frailty GP.

We are an ambitious, innovative and forward-thinking PCN, recognised as being at the forefront of Integrated Neighbourhood Working across Kent and Medway.

Having been part of the national Neighbourhood Health Implementation Programme (NNHIP) pilot, we are helping to shape the future of neighbourhood healthcare.

This is a very exciting opportunity to join a progressive and dynamic environment, working within our established Integrated Neighbourhood Team to deliver a more proactive, responsive and joined-up approach to caring for patients living with frailty and complex needs.

We are looking for a GP who shares our ambition and enthusiasm for developing new ways of working.

Previous experience in frailty care would be highly desirable, although not essential.

Above all, we are seeking someone who is enthusiastic about integrated working and wants to play a key role in shaping the future of neighbourhood healthcare.

The post holder will act as a clinical leader for our established Integrated Neighbourhood Team, providing senior clinical leadership, oversight and guidance to a dynamic multidisciplinary team of clinicians and healthcare professionals.

The team delivers a combination of proactive and reactive care, supporting patients living with frailty, complex health needs and those at risk of deterioration or hospital admission.

The GP will play a key role in supporting clinical decision-making, managing complexity and ensuring a coordinated, patient-centred approach to care.

The role will involve working closely with a diverse range of professionals across neighbourhood services, providing clinical leadership and contributing to multidisciplinary discussions and care planning.

An important aspect of the role will be helping to lead and develop our innovative neighbourhood model, supporting new ways of working and shaping the future delivery of integrated care across our PCN.

Folkestone, Hythe & Rural Primary Care Network brings together seven GP practices serving a population of approximately 50,000 patients across a mixture of rural and urban communities.

Our member practices are Oaklands Health Centre, White House Surgery, Harbour Medical Practice, New Lyminge Surgery, Church Road Surgery, Sun Lane Surgery and Hawkinge and Elham Valley Practice.

Our population is diverse, covering communities with areas of significant deprivation alongside a high proportion of older patients and people living with frailty, multimorbidity and complex health needs.

We are an ambitious, progressive and forward-thinking organisation with a strong reputation for innovation, collaboration and developing new approaches to care.

Having participated in the national Neighbourhood Health Implementation Programme pilot, we have been at the forefront of Integrated Neighbourhood Working across Kent and Medway.

We have developed an established Integrated Neighbourhood Team, bringing together professionals from primary care, community health and wider partners to deliver more joined-up, proactive and responsive care.

We pride ourselves on creating a supportive and inclusive working environment where staff are valued, encouraged to contribute ideas and actively involved in service development.

This is an exciting time to join our PCN as we continue to build on our achievements and help shape the future of neighbourhood healthcare.

employer: Wrightington Wigan & Leigh Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Elderly Care Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Now is a really exciting time to Join our Team of forward-thinking Ageing & Complex Medicine (Elderly Medicine) Consultants at Wrightington Wigan and Leigh (WWL) NHS Foundation Trust, and make a real difference to our elderly patients in the Wigan Borough.

Here at WWL we put the patient at the heart of everything we do, as we strive to deliver and develop our modern and comprehensive Elderly Care service. We would love to hear from applicants who have already developed a sub-specialty interest within Elderly Care, and those who have not already done so would be encouraged to do so through in-house training/ attending relevant CPD activities. Opportunities are available across in-patient and out-patient with support from the clinical director and divisional management team to build and develop your area of interest.

AAC interview date is to be confirmed.

The full time post offers a 10 PA job plan, with the potential to negotiate additional PA's on an individual basis for the successful candidate. The needs of our patients are at the heart of everything we do and we are equally committed to the wellbeing of our clinical teams, therefore your contribution will be highly valued. The Trust has a successful track record of staff engagement, and has a range of flexible working options subject to meeting relevant eligibility criteria.

There is commitment for night and weekend on call in general medicine, and as part of the day service.

We also provide training for two Specialist Registrars as part of the Northwest Training rotation which includes an integrated MSc. course in Elderly Care medicine.The needs of our patients are at the heart of everything we do, and we are equally committed to the wellbeing of our clinical teams, therefore your contribution will be highly valued. Choose Well - Choose WWL

Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh NHS Foundation Trust are the proud providers of acute hospital and community services to the people of the Wigan Borough and surrounding areas. WWL are committed to placing the patient at the heart of everything we do, and in the provision of safe, effective care that acknowledges and ensures dignity. With this in mind we are seeking to recruit people who share our values and beliefs.

On-Call

employer: University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust (279)
title: Consultant Rheumatologist
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking to appoint a substantive Consultant Rheumatologist. The appointee will work with Consultant colleagues to provide a comprehensive service for residents across West Sussex. The Rheumatology department is part of the MSK Directorate including Trauma and Orthopaedics and Pain Management. The post will be based predominantly at Worthing and Southlands Hospitals. However there will be some sessions at other Trust locations if and when required.

The post offers an excellent opportunity for you to develop as a Consultant and also contribute to service development.

  • Outpatient clinics: assessment of all new patients at their first appointment; review of follow-up patients; discussion and review of follow-up patients seen by Speciality Doctors and clinical nurse specialists (CNS); joint injections and other procedures.
  • Ward referrals and other DCC duties: specialist review of inpatients referred by other medical teams with rheumatic complaints; weekly combined radiology MDT.
  • Administrative duties directly related to this: out-patient clinic letter dictation and signing; blood and imaging report signing; result letter dictation; GP referral letter grading; prescription of biologic drugs, parenteral osteoporosis and DMARD medication; medical report writing.
  • Telephone and email advice: giving advice on the management of rheumatic diseases to GPs, allied health professionals, other specialists.
  • Clinical audit: writing local audit proposals and reports; collecting clinical audit data; presenting results; participation in regional and national clinical audits (data collection).
  • Clinical and educational supervision of CNSs and clinical assistants
  • Involvement with the Trust Clinical Governance programme. There will be a commitment to supporting the education of medical students from Brighton (BSMS) in their placements, and the potential to develop managerial and research interests. There are strong links to the KSS Deanery and Brighton & Sussex Medical School.
  • Rheumatology On-Call Commitment: None

Working for our organisation

At UHSussex, diversity is our strength, and we want you to feel included to help us always deliver Excellent Care Everywhere, as shown in our Outstanding for Caring CQC rating. Your uniqueness and experiences will be part of our creative and innovative community where everyone is encouraged to succeed. We have a range of staff networks to help break down barriers, and can offer abuddy to help new members settle in. We're proud to be a Disability Confident Employer (Level 3) and a Veteran Aware Trust.

employer: Honeybeerecruitment.com Ltd. trading as Military Medical Personnel (MMP)
title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Locum Doctor (General Practitioner) to cover an assignment with the Ministry of Defence (MoD), at Chicksands Medical Centre, in Shefford, Bedfordshire.

This is a locum role (20 hours per week) and the successful candidate will deliver an exceptional standard of care to the MoD service personnel.

Hourly Rate - £69.12 per hour

Job Description:

  • Undertake Primary Healthcare (PHC) clinics for Military and entitled personnel.
  • Examinations and Occupational Health (OH) fitness for work assessments within the locum doctors scope of experience and qualification.
  • To inform the local medical authority of any case that may affect a servicepersons ability to undertake their duties.

employer: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Hepatologist
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a dynamic and enthusiastic Hepatologist to join our University of Derby and Burton Hospitals (UHDB) team of 6 Hepatology consultants and 8 specialist nurses.

The successful candidate will also work closely with our 14 luminal gastroenterologists in providing a 24/7 gastroenterology and liver service including a daily inpatient endoscopy list and endoscopy nurse supported out of hours GI bleed service.

This is a full-time position, but candidates wishing to work part-time or in a job-share are encouraged to apply. If a part-time or job-share person is appointed modification of the job content will be discussed with the appointee on a personal basis. Informal visits are welcomed.

Hepatology services are primarily based at the Royal Derby Hospital site, which is a level 2 liver centre. In 2023, the service achieved level 2 (full) IQILS (Improving Quality of Liver Services) accreditation. The assessment team highlighted several areas of excellence in the service. The unit is a tertiary referral centre for PTC and TIPSS and works closely with the Liver transplant unit in Birmingham in caring for patients pre and post liver transplantation.

Luminal and Hepatology services are provided on 2 separate dedicated wards at Royal Derby Hospital (RDH) and on 1 ward at Queens Hospital Burton (QHB). At RDH the Hepatology service is supported by 8 Clinical Nurse Specialists including 2 Viral Hepatitis, 2 Hepatology, and 4 HPB cancer nurse Specialists, together with alcohol liaison service. We have excellent endoscopy facilities which are all JAG accredited this includes a 3-room endoscopy suite at QHB and a 2-room endoscopy suite at SRP. We participate in the national bowel cancer screening programme across the Acute Hospitals.

As a trusted organisation at the heart of our communities, we recognise the important role we can play in supporting the public, patients, our own people and local partners in achieving the best of health for the local population and the communities in which they live by providing Exceptional Care Together

Our fundamental Values of Compassion, Openness and Excellence underpin how we intend to work as a Trust and the associated behaviours are becoming embedded in all aspects of how we work.

In return we will offer:

o Development opportunities, including both professional and leadership developmento On-going support through every step of the way from recruitment to when you join our team and beyond.o A variety of other staff benefits including employee assistance programme, discounted gym membership, onsite fitness classes, car schemes

Key Facts about our Trust:

o We see on average 4810 OP appointments per day.o We are the 4th busiest Trauma & Orthopaedic outpatients department in England - an average of 2077 per week.o An average of 1115 patients are seen in A&Es across our network every day - 3rd largest in the country.o Our hospitals admit an average of 195 emergency patients daily.o Last year we undertook almost 33,700 planned surgical operations in our 57 operating theatres.o We are one of only 7 Trusts nationally with more than 50 operating theatres.o We carry out more than 140 elective procedures each working day.

employer: Mersey and West Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Consultant Plastic Surgeon - Skin & Mohs Interest
descriptionHtml:
The post is for a substantive Consultant in Plastic Surgery with a Skin Cancer and Mohs and Surgery interest.

This is an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated surgeon to join a dynamic, rapidly expanding team delivering multidisciplinary care within the Mersey Regional Burns and Plastic Surgery unit based at Mersey and West Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust. This is a whole-time post with a weekly peripheral site clinical commitment.

Applicants are required to hold Membership of the Royal College of Surgeons (UK or equivalent qualifications), to be fully registered with the General Medical Council, and to be on the Specialist Register or due to obtain their CCT within six months of the date of interview.

Interviews will take place on Friday 11th December 2026.

The appointee will have a responsibility for the running of their clinical service, integrating this with the department as a whole and ensuring appropriate communication with general practitioners, managers, and hospital committees. The appointee will be responsible for contributing to the achievement of relevant aspects if the Trusts contractual obligations and business plans.

The appointee will be expected to ensure their clinical service is in accordance with the principles of Clinical Governance which must include appropriate clinical audit, clinical targets, key performance indicators (KPI's), evidence-based practice, continued personal educational and professional development. The post holder will also be expected to comply with existing appraisal procedures, job planning and revalidation procedures.

Mersey and West Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust serves a population of over 600,000 with a workforce of over 10,500 dedicated and skilled staff across 21 sites.

Our services:

Acute Care

Providing emergency and maternity services at Whiston, Southport and Ormskirk hospitals, and medical and surgical specialties across all our sites.

Primary Care

Providing primary care services at Marshalls Cross Medical Centre situated in St Helens Hospital.

Community Services

Providing adult community services for St Helens and a wheelchair service in Chorley, South Ribble, and West Lancashire. Our inpatient unit at Newton Community Hospital is where patients needing acute hospital beds can continue rehabilitation. We also provide urgent care at our Urgent Treatment Centre located in St Helens town centre.

Specialist Regional Services

We provide the Mersey Regional Burns & Plastic Surgery Unit at Whiston Hospital and the Spinal Injuries Unit at Southport Hospital to more than 4 million people across the whole of Merseyside, West Lancashire, Cheshire, Isle of Man and North Wales.

Achievements:

  • Top 100 places to work in the NHS (NHS Employers & Health Service Journal)

employer: Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Oncoplastic Breast Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
A full time 10PA Locum Fixed Term Consultant in Breast Surgery for Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, based at the King's Mill Hospital, Sutton in Ashfield, Nottinghamshire is required. This post will be focussed on oncoplastic breast surgery and as such the candidate must have proven 2 year's experience in an Oncoplastic unit . The post holder may also be required to undertake planned surgery and outpatient clinics at Newark Hospital which is also part of the trust.

The appointee will join an existing multi-disciplinary team providing a comprehensive Breast Service to central North Nottinghamshire and, in particular, the residents of Mansfield, Ashfield and Newark Districts.

The post holder will demonstrate a wide range of skills and will be required to work flexibly within the department and across two sites. The successful candidate will be expected to be aware of local policies and procedures and comply with the standing orders and standing financial instructions of this Trust. In particular, where the consultant manages employees of the Trust, he/she will be expected to observe local employment and personnel policies and procedures.

The over-riding purpose is to support the provision of the highest quality patient care through personal actions and continuous improvement.

  • Provision of a service to Sherwood Forest Hospitals, with responsibility for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of illness, and the proper functioning of the department.
  • Out-of-hours responsibilities, including participation in Consultant on-call rota where applicable.
  • Cover for colleagues' annual leave and other authorised absences.
  • Any responsibility which relates to a special interest.
  • Professional supervision and management of junior medical staff including the observance of local employment and human resource policies and procedures.
  • Responsibilities for carrying out teaching, examination and accreditation duties as required and contributing to undergraduate, postgraduate and continuing medical education activity, locally and nationally.
  • Participating in medical audit, the Trust's Clinical Governance processes and in CPD - CPD is provided in job plans and attendance at audit and other governance meetings is mandatory.
  • Managerial, including budgetary responsibilities where appropriate and compliance with standing orders and standing financial instructions of the Trust.
  • Any other duties which may be required from time to time which are reasonable regarded to be part of the role of a consultant.

Sherwood Forest Hospitals is an award-winning NHS Foundation Trust providing acute and community healthcare services for 420,000 people across Mansfield, Ashfield, Newark, Sherwood and parts of Derbyshire and Lincolnshire. We are working closely with partners in health and social care through the Mid Nottinghamshire Integrated Care Partnership to take collective responsibility for managing resources, delivering NHS standards, and improving the health of the population we serve.

We put the patient at the centre of everything that we do, and it is our aim to make sure that every patient is treated as we would want a member of our own family to be treated. At the same time we expect our staff to be caring, kind and courteous to each other and to look out for each other. We believe that we are truly a clinically led organisation.

title: Locum Consultant Psychiatrist in Substance Misuse
descriptionHtml:
The post will be based in the community between the Two West teams. The exact breakdown of cover and location can of work can be agreed depending on the preference of the candidate and their area of residence.

The post will provide medical support to the community teams on a full-time basis working closely with the current SAS and Specialist doctors.

The post holder will be encouraged to obtain and maintain section 12(2) approval of the Mental Health Act 1983 (2007) and Approved Clinician status in Wales in order to participate in the on call rota for MHLD and to undertake assessments in the community, police custody, 136 suites.

The on call is 1 in 13.

This is a 12-month fixed-term locum post to cover a period of maternity leave.

This post will be based in the West area with clinical input into both the community teams agreed with the successful candidate.

The post involves close MDT working with no individual case load but rather providing medical input and reviews for those open to Substance Misuse services.

The post holder will be expected to work to the BCU Substance Misuse prescribing guidelines for both inpatient and community sessions.

Clinical duties will include liaison with neighbouring CMHT's, inpatient wards (both psychiatric and at the local DGH's) clinical support to the alcohol liaison service and attendance at multi-disciplinary team meetings.

The post holder will be expected to keep up to date in respect of clinical developments.

The post holder is expected to participate in all relevant clinical programme group meetings.

Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB) is Wales's largest health organisation, with a budget of over £2.4 billion and a workforce of over 20,000 staff. The Health Board provides primary, community, mental health and acute hospital services for the population of North Wales.

BCUHB provides a full range of primary, community, mental health, acute and specialist hospital services across 3 acute hospitals and a network of community hospitals, health centres, clinics, and mental health units. It also co-ordinates or provides the work of GP practices and NHS services provided by dentists, opticians, and pharmacists across the region.

The Health Board is an integrated health system that strives for excellent, compassionate care delivered in partnership with the public sector and other statutory and third sector organisations.

title: Speciality Doctor Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Interventions Team
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Specialty Doctor post to support the delivery of care within the Emotional Wellbeing and Mental Health Care Group for under 18s in Cardiff and Vale.

The Emotional Wellbeing and Mental Health Care Group is driving forward the transformational agenda for CAMH services in Wales with the development of existing services in line with the new Mental Health strategy and stepped care model.

Our new colleague will be an enthusiastic and committed psychiatrist with an interest in service development and with a strong desire to help service users and families.

Working alongside the teams, you will provide specialist psychiatric assessment and management to contribute to formulation and diagnosis, and the delivery of care.

As a psychiatrist, you will have experience and knowledge in carrying a service user caseload, including assessing service users with complex needs, and supporting families with care planning.

Care co-ordination, consultation, supervision and supporting other members of the multi-disciplinary team will be key aspects of the role, as well as partnership working with health, education and social care. The post holder will be supported in this role by a Consultant Child Psychiatrist and with appropriate areas of skill that require development and further training.

This is a 0.5 WTE - 5 session permanent post within the EWMH interventions team

Our Single Point of Access (SPOA) manages queries, advice, consultation and the referral process into our services. This model has reduced the number of referrals through providing accessible signposting and advice to both families and professionals. Contacts with SPOA result in a monthly average of circa 200 young people and families being offered a Choice appointment with our core assessment team. Referrals identified as specifically relating to an eating disorder (ED) at SPOA are assessed within the multidisciplinary ED clinic.

The Post Holder will work in the Core Interventions team (previously generic CAMHS) providing Part 1 & Part 2 work under the Mental Health Measure (Wales 2010)

The Main responsibilities of the post:

psychiatric assessment and intervention including pharmacological treatment and Mental Health Act Assessments within the Core Intervention Team

Involvement in prescription rota (depending on working days)

Involvement in Peer Group

Support teaching to medical students and other staff

Maintain CPD

No out of hours duties.

The Consultant Psychiatrists in the Core Intervention Team provide consultation sessions for the wider service to provide advice, manage any necessary medical investigations and identify when and how young people require direct psychiatric input which may result in allocation to partnership work or the offer of one-off joint appointment.

Cardiff and Vale University Health Board is one of the largest Integrated Health Boards in the UK, employing over 17,000 staff, providing over 100 specialist services. Working across 6 hospital sites, we have a diverse range of career opportunities to offer. Serving over 500,000 people living in Cardiff and the Vale, we are focussed on the health and care needs of our local population whilst working with our partners to develop regional services. Together we are committed to improving health outcomes for everyone, delivering excellent care and support.

Our mission is "Living Well, Caring Well, Working Together", and our vision is that every person's chance of leading a healthy life should be equal. Our 10-year transformation and improvement strategy, Shaping Our Future Wellbeing, is our chance to work collaboratively with the public and our workforce to make our health board more sustainable for the future.

descriptionHtml:

title: Consultant Vascular Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board wishes to appoint a full-time substantive Consultant Vascular Surgeon to join the existing team of eight Consultant Vascular Surgeons who provide the service across North Wales.

The post is a combination of replacement and expansion, in part arising as a result of a move to increase provision of surgical services at our spoke sites.

The successful candidates will form part of a rota consisting of 1 week in 8 as Vascular Consultant of the Week (VCOW) and 1 night in 8 on call overnight.

As part of the recruitment process, applicants who are successful at shortlisting will be invited to attend a Stakeholder Interview and an Advisory Appointments Committee (AAC) Interview on 11th December 2026.

Clinical DutiesThe post holder will:

  • work collaboratively with Consultant colleagues, as appropriate, to provide specialist services at the designated hospitals, with responsibility for the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of illness
  • have continuing responsibility for the care of patients in liaison with Consultant colleagues and for the proper functioning of the department in line with the Operational Policy and Strategic Plan (as amended from time to time).

Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB) is Wales's largest health organisation, with a budget of over £2.4 billion and a workforce of over 20,000 staff.

BCUHB provides a full range of primary, community, mental health, acute and specialist hospital services for the population of North Wales, across three acute hospitals and a network of community hospitals, health centres, clinics, and mental health units. It also co-ordinates or provides the work of GP practices and NHS services provided by dentists, opticians, and pharmacists across the region.

descriptionHtml:
We are looking to find a Consultant Paediatrician to join our friendly team at Blackpool Teaching Hospital. Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is a forward looking and innovative place to work and is committed to Values Based Collaborative Leadership and being a 'Great Place to Work'.

Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust was established on 1st December 2007. The Trust gained Teaching Hospital status and became Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust in 2010.   • Act as the primary point of contact for community pharmacy contractors and the LPC, ensuring regular, high-quality communication with these partners.
  • Attend meetings with the LPC and Controlled Drugs Local Intelligence Network (CDLIN) as required.

  • Prescribe, investigate, refer and escalate care as clinically required.
  • Deliver face-to-face, telephone and remote consultations.

  • Provide high-quality patient communication and safety-netting.
