About Vertis Services

Vertis delivers and supports a range of primary care and urgent care services. Current and developing opportunities may include Primary Care Services at or around local Emergency Departments, out-of-hours medical cover for community hospitals, and other services mobilised in response to local system need. Joining the staff bank does not restrict a GP to one service and does not guarantee a minimum number of shifts. Offers of work will reflect service demand, commissioning arrangements, competence, availability and completion of service-specific onboarding.

employer: Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in HIV Medicine and Sexual Health – 56 Dean Street
descriptionHtml:
The post is for a 10 PA Consultant in Sexual Health & HIV Medicine.

56 Dean Street is an award winning HIV and sexual health service based in Soho with a particular emphasis on HIV prevention and the sexual health care needs of LGBTQI+ people. It is Europe's busiest sexual health clinic with an attendance of approximately 110,000 patients per year. It cares for the third largest HIV cohort in the country with approximately 4,600 patients. The clinic also runs an Integrated Gender Dysphoria Service called TransPlus, we are particular interested in candidates who have an interest in Gender Dysphoria Care as part of these Job Plans includes time developing experience within TransPlus.

The HIV inpatient service merged with the Imperial College Hospitals Trust service in 2019 and now provides care on Ron Johnson ward at the Chelsea and Westminster Hospital site for inner northwest London as well as Hertfordshire.

The AAC for this post will be held on 10th December 2026

The post-holder will, in conjunction with the existing consultants, have responsibilities for providing advice, screening, diagnosis and treatment of patients with STIs, including HIV infection. They will be committed to developing integrated HIV & sexual health services, optimize cost efficiency of the service, implement new technologies and develop new initiatives. The post holder will have an opportunity to work within our TransPlus service.

The post-holder will also be required to participate in quality improvement, research and management of the service. It is anticipated that the post-holder will engage in specific management tasks and contribute to monthly departmental meetings in agreement with the Clinical Lead. The post-holder will also be expected to work with the other consultants at Chelsea and Westminster NHS Foundation Trust to deliver and improve outpatient HIV care, including recruitment to clinical trials. They will be expected to manage their own HIV cohort.

They will also be expected to work alongside the other consultants in providing educational supervision for the multidisciplinary team and participate in Wednesday morning educational activities, the virtual clinic and the weekly Directorate HIV resistance meeting. In particular, the post-holder will have educational supervisory responsibility for nominated junior staff. This role will include appraisal of the individuals concerned.

Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is one of England's top-performing and safest trusts. We operate two main acute hospital sites--Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and West Middlesex University Hospital--along with award-winning clinics across North West London.

Our nearly 7,500 staff care for a diverse population of 1.5 million, providing full clinical services, including maternity, A&E, and children's services, plus specialist HIV and sexual health clinics. The Care Quality Commission rates us 'Good' in safety, effectiveness, care, and responsiveness, and 'Outstanding' in leadership and resource use.

We continually invest in our facilities, including a £30m expansion of critical care at Chelsea and Westminster and an £80m Ambulatory Diagnostic Centre at West Middlesex.

We are committed to equal opportunities and believe that diversity drives innovation and excellence. As part of our dedication to equity, we actively welcome applications from individuals from the global majority, veterans and underrepresented communities. We value the unique perspectives and experiences that diverse teams bring and are committed to creating an environment where all voices are heard, respected, and empowered to succeed."

If you haven't heard from us within three weeks of the closing date, your application was likely unsuccessful. Employment is subject to a six-month probationary period.

Some roles may require weekend shifts at multiple sites.

employer: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Anaesthetist with an interest in Neuro Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for Locum Neuro Anaesthesia Consultant post 10PAs and the post holders will join the Neuro on-call rota.

Upon appointment the post holder will be paired with a mentor for the first year. Furthermore, our set-up has much valuable support on-site as every day of the week, there is a senior Anaesthetic Consultant, acting as the Duty Floor Anaesthetist (DFA) for the overall smooth running of the operating theatres and providing urgent help and/or matching skills/experience of allocated anaesthetists with operating lists.

The post holder will join the Group of Neuro anaesthetists which consists of approximately 16 Consultants including Neuro Intensivists. This is a friendly, approachable, dynamic and diverse group, who are enthusiastic in both teaching colleagues and learning new skills from colleagues. There is emphasis in wellbeing and supporting each other. The case mix at St George's tends to be complex and challenging. Given the huge expertise in the department, it is easy to seek advice / discuss with an expert in a certain field or acquire new skills.

The post is for full time posts of 10 PAs, with 9 PAs for direct clinical care (DCC) and 1 for SPA in support of personal CPD, preparation for GMC appraisal, additional responsibilities of the post holder and revalidation with an opportunity to increase as interests develop.

The job plan template is based on an alternating working pattern, weeks AC and weeks BD. Some operating lists are three session lists, for continuity of care and theatre efficiency.

Session times (inclusive of CRA (clinical related activity time)

AM - 08:00-13:00 (5 hours - 1.25PA)

PM - 13:00-18:00 (5 hours - 1.25PA)

EVE - 17:00 - 21:00 (4 hours - 1PA)

All inpatient day sessions start at 08:00 and run until 18:00; 10 hours which equates to 2.5PAs. Half day sessions are 5 hours which equates to 1.25PAs. Three session lists equate to 3.5PA's.

The consultant job plan includes 'annualised sessions' which can be worked flexibly to meet the needs of the individual and the department. Each annualised session is equivalent to the PA value of the session worked. This flexibility allows individuals to organise working patterns to support a better work life balance, whilst also ensuring we have cover within the department. It is expected that the post-holder will contribute to a proportion of annualised sessions within the field of neuroanaesthesia. The remaining annualised sessions will be within the general anaesthesia subspecialties with in the skill mix of the individual anaesthetist.

The St George's Hospital Atkinson Morley Neurosurgical Unit is a leading UK centre for both adult and paediatric neurosurgery. It is a designated trauma centre with a specific neurosurgery service that manages all head injury patients. The Department of Anaesthesia covers all surgical specialities and is currently involved in many exciting initiatives. This is an excellent opportunity for an individual with the appropriate skills to join a first class team in an active and progressive London teaching hospital environment.

employer: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Dermatologist
descriptionHtml:
Be part of a dermatology service recognised for clinical excellence, innovation and specialist care, serving patients across Oxfordshire and the Thames Valley.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is seeking a Consultant Dermatologist to join our highly regarded Dermatology Department. As a regional centre for dermatology and skin cancer care, we provide specialist and general dermatology services to a large and diverse patient population, supported by exceptional facilities and a strong multidisciplinary team. The total workload is 10 PAs and you will be based at the Churchill Hospital, Oxford but may be required to support clinical activity at other clinics.

This role offers the opportunity to develop your clinical interests within a department that combines high-quality patient care, teaching, research and service innovation. You will join an experienced team of consultants, specialist nurses, trainees and allied health professionals, working in a supportive environment that encourages collaboration, professional development and continuous improvement

With increasing demand for dermatology services across the region, this is a chance to help shape the future of the specialty while contributing to one of the UK's leading teaching hospital trusts.

Care to join us...?

As a Consultant Dermatologist, you will provide expert clinical care across a broad range of dermatology services, including general dermatology, vulval dermatology and leg ulcer clinics. Working within a consultant-led service, you will deliver high-quality care for both outpatient and inpatient populations while supporting the continued development of specialist services.

You will:

  • Deliver consultant-led dermatology clinics and specialist services.
  • Participate in the dermatology on-call rota and Advice and Guidance service.
  • Support the education, supervision and development of dermatology trainees and junior doctors.
  • Contribute to clinical governance, audit, quality improvement and service development initiatives.
  • Participate in teaching and training within a leading teaching hospital environment.
  • Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary colleagues and primary care partners to deliver outstanding patient-centred care.
  • Help drive innovation and service improvements to meet the evolving needs of patients across the region.

Joining our team means becoming part of a department with an outstanding reputation for dermatology, skin cancer care, education and research, backed by modern facilities and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional patient outcomes.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the UK's largest and most respected NHS teaching trusts, providing world-class healthcare across four hospitals: the John Radcliffe Hospital, Churchill Hospital, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre and Horton General Hospital and over one hundred satellite sites. Find out more information here OUH at a Glance 2026/27

You'll become part of an organisation at the forefront of patient care, research, education and innovation. You'll have access to excellent learning and development opportunities, work alongside highly skilled multidisciplinary teams, and contribute to services that make a real difference.

Our commitment to Delivering Compassionate Excellence is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our values of compassion, respect, learning, delivery, improvement and excellence, we strive to create an environment where staff feel supported, valued and empowered to thrive. Watch how we set out to deliver compassionate excellence via the OUH YouTube channel and the OneTeamOneOUH - LIVING OUR VALUES video.

We are committed to creating an inclusive, respectful and safe workplace for everyone. As signatories to the NHS Sexual Safety Charter, we have a zero-tolerance approach to inappropriate behaviour and are dedicated to fostering a culture where all colleagues feel welcomed, respected and able to be themselves. We pledge zero tolerance for inappropriate sexual behaviour and commit to the ten core principles.

title: Medical Examiner
descriptionHtml:
"The next of kin are at the heart of everything we do"

We are seeking to appoint a proactive and self-motivated doctor to join our team of medical examiners at North & Mid Hampshire Medical Examiner Service.

Since 9 September 2024 when the service became statutory, all acute, non-acute and community deaths that do not require a coroner's referral must be scrutinised by a medical examiner before the death can be registered.

The successful applicant will

  • provide independent scrutiny of non-coronial deaths
  • ensure the appropriate referral of deaths to the coroner
  • contribute towards a better service for the bereaved, including an opportunity for them to raise any concerns
  • improve the quality of death certification
  • support local learning and improvement by identifying matters that require escalation to local clinical governance and other processes
  • improve the quality of mortality data

The ME service interacts with many clinical specialities from both the acute and non-acute setting, strengthening links between the health services, coroners' offices and register offices.

Medical Examiners are senior doctors from a diverse variety of clinical specialties in secondary and primary care. Relevant governance experience would be a strong bonus. This could be mortality or other case record reviews in secondary care; or actively considering similar issues in the context of team meetings in primary care. You will work closely with our team of Medical Examiner Officers, who are vital to the efficient running of the service.

Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is the major provider of hospital services to the population of North and Mid Hampshire and surrounding areas. The hospitals in Basingstoke and Winchester provide a comprehensive range of acute services as well as being a tertiary referral centre for colorectal, liver, peritoneal carcinomatosis, haemophilia and pseudomyxoma surgery.

employer: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist in Forensic Psychiatry
descriptionHtml:
This is a replacement post. The post is located at Roseberry Park Hospital, Middlesbrough, where inpatient forensic beds and clinical and managerial offices are all co-located.

There is a need for a Consultant on Ivy/Clover/Kestrel ward a low secure female learning disability ward.

There is a system of weekly MDT meetings for the ward which the post holder is expected to attend, in addition to meetings for CPA (6 monthly), formulation and risk management meetings. The length of stay currently on the ward is around five years.

The consultant will be supported by a ward manager, clinical lead working on each ward. In addition, they will receive support from occupational therapist, psychologist and social worker. Pharmacist will attend when support is required. A SAS/trust doctor, which is shared (50% time) will be supporting the post holder. The post holder can be the identified supervisor for the junior doctor. There will be opportunity to become a trainer for trainees in the future.

All patients will be detained under the Mental Health Act. As Responsible Clinician, the post holder will be expected to write statutory reports and attend First Tier Tribunals, Hospital Manager Hearings, S117 and MAPPA meetings as appropriate.

Referral rates for the ward are anticipated to be 4 per year from both internal and external sources. They can be seen jointly with the other staff members (psychologist/ nursing staff). The average length of stay on the ward is approx. 5 years.

Within the Secure Inpatient Services Directorate, the post-holder will be working alongside 14 consultant colleagues, 4 specialty grade doctors, and up to 3 core trainees.

We are one of the largest specialist mental health and learning disabilities trusts in the country providing a range inpatient and community services to 2m people living in County Durham, the Tees Valley, Scarborough, Whitby, Ryedale, Harrogate, Hambleton and Richmondshire. We also provide additional specialist services to other parts of Northern England.

From education and prevention, to crisis and specialist care our talented and compassionate teams work in partnership with our patients, communities and partners to help the people of our region feel safe, understood, believed in and cared for.

We nurture the recovery journey of anyone in need of our help. In Our Trust, everyone has a say in how they are supported and treated because we listen to every person in our care until they feel understood. Our patients, their families and carers work together with us towards better mental health.

We're committed to new thinking that improves the wellbeing of our region. We connect with our communities and partners to get mental health care right, in areas that really need it.

We won't rest until everyone in our region has the mental health care they need, to lead their best possible life.

Psychiatrists are essential contributors to the majority of our mental health teams. Service users expect and are justified to expect collaborative relationships with dedicated psychiatrists who work consistently as part of effective services.

employer: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Acute Trauma Radiology Consultant
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Consultant Radiologist to join a friendly and cohesive team of radiologists with diverse expertise in a busy department and a strong record in teaching and training. The applicant would be expected to join the existing radiologists in providing a comprehensive diagnostic radiology service and providing support for multidisciplinary meetings. The post-holder will also support the running of service in our main department at St George's Hospital.

The successful applicant will be expected, in collaboration with the other radiologists in the department, to oversee and ensure the provision of high-quality clinical services within the Radiology Department. This would consist of providing a comprehensive diagnostic radiology service which includes general plain radiography,, CT, ultrasound, and MRI.

In addition the post will contain general diagnostic adult sessions in CT and plain film reporting. The successful applicant would take part in general oncall and have participation in training and quality improvement activity would also be expected.

The post-holder will also participate in a full-time diagnostic on-call rota (approximately 1:15), alongside regular weekend working (with time off in-lieu).

It is expected that applicants will have the Fellowship of the Royal College of Radiologists and a CCT in Radiology or equivalent training and experience.

St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest healthcare units in the UK accommodating more than 1000 beds and employing 6000 members of staff, and is closely integrated to the St George's Hospital Medical School, part of the University of London. We have an established national and international reputation as a leading hospital for specialist care including neurosciences, cardiac care, stroke and oncology. We provide an integrated mix of secondary care and specialist services to children of Wandsworth, Merton and South West London, Surrey and further afield. We have a comprehensive range of paediatric medical and surgical specialist services supported by PICU and NICU and are a joint treatment centre for oncology with the Royal Marsden Hospital. The Trust is a designated level 1 Major Trauma Centre and has been granted Foundation Trust status.

title: Practice Nurse

employer: Torbay and South Devon NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Acute Medicine
descriptionHtml:
As a Consultant in Acute Medicine at Torbay Hospital, you will provide the highest quality patient care across our Acute Medicine domain, which includes our Acute Medicine Unit (AMU), Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) and the Acute Assessment Aerea.

Patient safety, dignity and care are central to our ethos, and as a senior member of the team, you will be responsible for the assessment, diagnosis, and management of patients with acute medical conditions, ensuring that they receive a 'second-to-none' standard of care from admission to discharge. You will work closely with other consultants, resident doctors, and multi-disciplinary teams to ensure patient pathways operate unhindered.

Why Work With Us

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a highly motivated GP to become part of a forward thinking, dynamic and friendly practice located on the Fylde Coast. This position would involve working within our extensive clinical team which currently comprises of: 5 GP Partners; 2 Salaried GPs; 2 ANPs; 2 Clinical Pharmacists and Pharmacy Technician; 1 Physicians Associate; 3 Practice Nurses; 1 Nurse Practitioner; 1 Nurse Associate; 2 Health Care Assistants and a Phlebotomist. The team works hard to ensure that the patient care is at the forefront of their mind and that the care they deliver is of an extremely high standard and we are searching for a like minded individual to further enhance the team. We have just been successful in retaining our Investors in People Gold Award - an achievement that as a team we are immensely proud of. We offer a very supportive environment for all members of the team. The clinical team meet virtually on a daily basis to discuss any complex cases, share ideas and provide support to each other. This was introduced at the beginning of the pandemic and has been revolutionary for the practice, a positive change that has now become embedded in our daily routines at the surgery. We are keen to find the right individual to join Fernbank Surgery and will therefore consider applicants from applicants looking for both part time and full time positions.

The successful applicant would be expected to work as an autonomous practitioner, responsible for the provision of medical services to the practice population, delivering an excellent standard of clinical care whilst complying with the GMS contract.

Furthermore, the post-holder will adhere to the GMC standards for good medical practice, contributing to the effective management of the practice, leading by example, maintaining a positive and collaborative working relationship with the multidisciplinary team.

Fernbank Surgery has a positive working relationship with many external stakeholders in the local area and we would be keen for the successful applicant to continue with these positive relationships.

Fernbank Surgery is a busy practice made up of a team of 5 very versatile partners, who are supported by a host of salaried GPs, ANPs, Clinical Pharmacists, Practice Nurses, Health Care Assistants, a Management Team and a pillar of administration and reception staff members. We are a close knit team that is able to work together efficiently and effectively to ensure that our patients receive an exemplary level of care and service from all that are part of team Fernbank. We are a training practice and take pride in being able to pass on our knowledge, support and guidance to the clinicians of the future. Fernbank Surgery is located in Lytham, a beautiful coastal town located on the Fylde Coast. Lytham has plenty to offer in the local community from sea front walks, picnics in the park or a vast choice of bars and restaurants Lytham really does cater for all.If you are interested in the post and want to visit the Practice or find out more, please contact Stephanie Sweeney, Practice Manager by email onlscicb-fw.fernbankmanagers@nhs.net

title: Treatment Doctor / Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
Are you a treatment doctor who has experience of operating with Termination of Pregnancy between 13+6 and 24 weeks or do you have a willingness to train and progress towards working safely and competently at higher gestations within the legal limit?

We have 50 clinics nationwide and we are currently looking for doctors who can provide terminations of pregnancy from 7.5hrs a week to 30 hours a week supporting any of our surgical clinics.

Birmingham, Leicester, Peterborough, Northampton, Nottingham, Bournemouth, Portsmouth, Reading, Richmond, London East, Finsbury Park, Merseyside, Doncaster, Leeds, Middlesbrough.

Please contact recruitment@bpas.org if you are interested in working for us - include your CV - and we can arrange for a further discussion.

BPAS are looking for dynamic, skilled doctors who can work as part of a multi-disciplinary team to support our national services. You will hold a Bachelor of Medicine or equivalent, full GMC registration with a license to practice, and are passionate and committed to reproductive healthcare.

  • We can provide substantive, fixed term and casual contracts.
  • We have family friendly policies, supporting flexible working and we are currently setting up robust job plans for our doctors to ensure our roles are structured and interesting.
  • If you have a special interest in an area e.g training, coaching, research or policy development etc.. please let us know!
  • Carry out termination of pregnancy by the appropriate method to evacuate the products of conception and ensure complete abortion and in accordance with BPAS clinical policies and procedures
  • Complete client consultation if needed and complete the statutory documentation
  • Assess and provide advice on the management of clients with medical or other conditions which may affect the abortion process.
  • Be present in the operating theatre throughout each procedure and remain on site until all clients have been assessed fit for discharge from recovery or passed to the care of another on-site doctor
  • Provide support, advice and guidance to nursing staff in the management of unexpected outcomes

We are also looking for:

  • Experience of independent practice for any abortion procedures/gestations relevant to the post, or willingness to be trained in-house.
  • Knowledge of termination of pregnancy procedures and the assessment and management of complications
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to be pro-active and flexible
  • Experience of IUD/Implant insertion along with knowledge of sexual health issues
  • Willing to travel to other locations within the region and/or work flexibly

The British Pregnancy Advisory Service (BPAS) is the UK's largest independent reproductive healthcare charity, providing evidence-based, not-for-profit reproductive healthcare. We work mainly on behalf of the NHS, offering abortion care, contraception, and STI testing and treatment across the country.

When you join BPAS, you become part of a values-driven organisation where compassion, professionalism, and choice guide everything we do. You will help remove barriers to safe reproductive care while supporting people to make informed choices about their health and futures.

Working with us - benefits include:

  • 34 days annual leave (including bank holidays)
  • Life assurance at 3 salary
  • Defined contribution pension scheme
  • Access to GP 24/7, 365 days a year
  • MyMindPal mental fitness app and 24/7 counselling support
  • Online discounts, discounted gym membership, and other lifestyle benefits
  • Family-friendly policies to support work-life balance

Safeguarding, Equality & Diversity

BPAS is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of everyone who uses our services, and all staff share this responsibility. Recruitment follows safer-recruitment principles and includes appropriate pre-employment checks.

We actively welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. We are proud to be an inclusive employer and will make reasonable adjustments to ensure a fair and accessible recruitment process for all candidates.

title: Receptionist / Administrator at GP Surgery

title: Support Worker (Males only)
descriptionHtml:

*Please note that due to a genuine occupational need, we are looking for males only to fill this position*

Person-centred planning is at the heart of everything we do and we are able to meet the changing needs of individuals we support as they progress through their care pathway, while ensuring their safety is maintained and their independence supported.

At Cygnet, our perks go way beyond pension schemes and excellent professional development - you'll also enjoy discounts with our free NHS blue light card, perkbox with vouchers for everyday purchases and shopping, private health cash plans, free confidential mental health support and much more, to support your wellbeing in and out of work.

Apply now to enjoy excellent career prospects while reaping the rewards of making a difference to others - every day.

title: Senior Support Worker
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a confident Senior Support Worker with a passion for delivering outstanding care.

You'll be working 42 hours a week (12 hours days and nights shift), making a positive difference to the lives of the people in our care at Cygnet Lodge Salford.

At Cygnet, we support our people to grow their careers, gain new skills and keep stepping up. Apply now to enjoy excellent career prospects while reaping the rewards of making a difference to others every day.

title: CAMHS Practitioner – Eating Disorders Transitions Worker
descriptionHtml:
Join our specialist Community Eating Disorders Service and play a key role in supporting young people and their families as they transition from CAMHS to Adult Eating Disorder Services. This rewarding role offers the opportunity to provide expert assessment, therapeutic intervention, care coordination and advocacy, working collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams and partner agencies. We are looking for an experienced and compassionate mental health professional with a passion for eating disorders, strong clinical skills, and a commitment to delivering high-quality, person-centred care while helping shape and develop innovative services across Rotherham, Doncaster and North Lincolnshire.

  • Lead and coordinate the transition of young people with eating disorders from CAMHS to Adult Eating Disorder Services, ensuring seamless, person-centred care planning.
  • Undertake specialist mental health, risk and eating disorder assessments and develop comprehensive care and transition plans.
  • Deliver evidence-based therapeutic interventions, including individual, family and group work, for young people with eating disorders and their families.
  • Act as a key resource and advocate for young people, families and professionals, providing advice, guidance and emotional support throughout the transition process.
  • Work collaboratively with CAMHS, Adult Services and partner agencies to ensure effective communication, joint working and coordinated care.
  • Participate in multidisciplinary meetings, transition reviews, inpatient reviews and safeguarding processes as required.
  • Provide clinical supervision, training and support to colleagues, students and other professionals.
  • Contribute to service development, quality improvement, audit and research activities to enhance outcomes for young people and families.
  • Promote innovative, evidence-based practice and support the continual development of eating disorder services across Rotherham, Doncaster and North Lincolnshire.
  • Manage a complex caseload autonomously whilst maintaining high standards of clinical governance, safeguarding and risk management

Rotherham Doncaster and South Humber NHS Foundation Trust (RDaSH) employ around 4000 talented colleagues who are very much appreciated, valued, and respected.

We have a wide portfolio which includes mental health, physical health, learning disability and drug and alcohol services.

We are dedicated to the development of our our people and hold a learning half day every month for our colleagues.

We are passionate about enhancing the quality of our service and we work hard to attract and select the right colleagues for our organisation. Our goal is to employ those who share our passion for providing first class care while remaining committed to our vision and values. Please view our Strategy using the link below:

https://www.rdash.nhs.uk/documents/clinical-and-organisational-strategy-2023-to-2028/

To find out more about working for RDaSH and the fantastic benefits we offer visit our website:

https://www.rdash.nhs.uk/about-us/getting-involved/work-with-us/

We are committed to inclusive cultures and really value people in our organisation, view our Allyship video on YouTube to find out more:

https://youtu.be/WMJSkLoTk4Q

The main terms and conditions of service can be found here:

https://www.nhsemployers.org/publications/tchandbook

title: Clinical Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
Highcroft Surgery is a well established GP Practice serving 11,000 patients in the heart of Arnold.

We are looking for a Clinical Pharmacist to work full time in our Practice and become part of a friendly, supportive and forward thinking team, committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care. We offer a collaborative working environment, manageable workloads, and strong multidisciplinary support. With involvement in service improvement and strong team work, this is an excellent role for a Clinical Pharmacist seeking job satisfaction, balance, and a welcoming Practice culture.

* Structured Medication Reviews - Carry out face to face and telephone call reviews for patients with complex needs or those taking multiple medication

* Long-Term Condition Management - Monitor, manage and adjust treatments for chronic illnesses

* Acute and Repeat Prescriptions - Handle medication requests, reauthorise repeat prescriptions and address acute queries

* Safety and Medicines Optimisation - Reconcile medications for patients recently discharged from the hospital to prevent discrepancies, identify high-risk medications (such as monitoring blood tests for specific drugs) and implement strategies to reduce adverse effects and counsel patients on how to use their medicines safely and effectively to reduce wastage

* Practice Support and Governance - Act as the primary expert contact for medicine-related questions from Doctors, Nurses, patients, and local pharmacies and help the Practice meet quality targets like the Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF) and optimise local prescribing costs

Our organisation is supported by a dedicated team of 30 staff members, including 2 GP Partners, 4 Salaried GPs, 1 Nurse Partner, 3 Nurses, 1 Nurse Associate, 2 Health Care Assistants, 1 Practice Manager, 1 Operations Manager, alongside teams including Pharmacy, Reception and Administration. We also have a number of ARRS staff supporting the Practice.

We all work together to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care. We pride ourselves on a warm, welcoming atmosphere where people feel valued, supported and respected. The work ethic is collaborative and professional, with a strong emphasis on teamwork, mutual support and continuous improvement.

Working here offers the benefits of a positive workplace culture, open communication, and opportunities for learning and development. Staff are encouraged to contribute ideas and take pride in their work, creating an environment where both employees and patients can thrive.

We use clinical systems including SystmOne, Ardens and eConsult.

title: Health Care Assistant
descriptionHtml:
The HCA will work strictly in accordance with specific practice guidelines and protocols.

The HCA will assist the practice clinical team in the provision and delivery of prescribed programmes of patient care.

The post will include some administrative duties.

The HCA will be responsible for seeing patients with booked appointments for clinical procedures.

Clinical

  • Phlebotomy
  • New Patient Health Checks
  • Learning Disability Health Checks
  • ECG Recording
  • Blood Pressure monitoring
  • Flu vaccination under PSD
  • B12, Shingles, Pneumococcal Vaccinations under PSD
  • Wound care
  • Urinalysis
  • Chaperoning
  • Preparation and processing of laboratory samples i.e. MSU, Sputum and Faeces.
  • Preparing medical equipment by ensuring infection and control procedures are adhered to.
  • Removal of sutures and clips
  • Ensure clinical waste collection runs smoothly
  • Working strictly within the guidelines and boundaries that are set.
  • Maintaining a professional attitude at all times towards patients and displaying an understanding and caring attitude.

Non clinical

  • Maintain general tidiness and cleanliness of treatment rooms
  • To have a thorough knowledge of Practice procedures
  • Maintain accurate and timely records, ensuring the clinical system is kept up to date
  • Any other delegated duties appropriate to the post

Macklin Street Surgery is a busy, friendly inner city GP Practice with 6 GP Partners and over 12,000 patients.

We are forward thinking and pro-active, always aiming to maintain the highest standards of practice to deliver excellent care to our patients as well as protecting the safety and well-being of staff.

The way that we work is continually evolving, especially so in the last year, and we need to adapt quickly to new ways of working and embrace improvements to practice processes and technology as they become available.

title: Recovery Worker, Weston-Super-Mare Ref:0188ZS
descriptionHtml:
Join us as a Recovery Worker in Weston-super-Mare.

Our team in Weston-super-Mare are recruiting for Recovery Workers to join their team in providing high quality recovery care to a diverse service user group. If you are an enthusiastic and creative individual and are passionate about changing peoples lives for the better, wed love to hear from you.

As a leading charity supporting people with drug, alcohol, and mental health challenges, we operate over 80 services across England and Scotland, providing free and confidential support to more than 100,000 people each year. Find out more about us on our website.

Please refer to the linked Job Description to support your application.

As a Recovery Worker, we offer a starting salary of £26,250 pro rata, per annum. The salary for this role is on an incremental scale and will rise each year in line with our pay progression salary bands, to £30,900 per annum. For further details please reach out to a member of the recruitment team via recruitment@wearewithyou.org.uk.

The closing date for applications is 4th November 2026. This advert may close early should sufficient applications be received. Please include a cover letter in your application.

As a Recovery Worker you will be providing support and advice to people who are experiencing difficulties due to substance misuse. You will be working within a highly skilled and knowledgeable multi-disciplinary team who will support you in your development and your ability to deliver the best care you can to our clients.

Our Recovery Workers play a vital role in supporting clients to identify their goals, ambitions, and passions. Youll work with them to create the best treatment plan for their needs and to guide them on their path to recovery. This is an integral role for With You - as a frontline worker, you will deliver continuity of care through effective partnership working, care coordination, delivery of interventions and key work responsibilities.

We are looking for a full time Recovery Worker, working 37.5 hours per week between 09:00 - 17:00, you would be working in our Criminal Justice team. We are also looking for a Part Time Recovery Worker working 22.5 hours per week (this can be worked over 4 days if suitable).

As an organisation, we continue to build an inclusive culture that encourages, supports and celebrates the diverse voices and experiences of our staff. We know that representing the communities we serve is key to us meeting our vision of a future where everyone lives a life free from the harm associated with drugs and alcohol. We welcome the unique contributions that you can bring and we encourage people from underrepresented communities and backgrounds to apply to join our team, including people with lived experience, people with disabilities, people from racialised communities, LGBTQ+ people, people of all ages and armed forces veterans.

As part of our commitment to the Armed Forces Covenant we provide a guaranteed interview scheme for candidates that are veterans and meet all the essential criteria for a role. With You is also a Disability Confident Employer and we offer a guaranteed interview scheme for candidates with a disability and meet all the essential criteria for a role.

If you have a disability, a learning difficulty such as dyslexia or a medical condition which you believe may affect your performance during any aspect of our selection process, well be happy to make reasonable adjustments to enable you to perform at your best.

Please review our recruitment FAQs before submitting your application.

Internal Applicants - please note that fixed term roles will be offered as secondments.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic Salaried GP to join our friendly, supportive and forward-thinking practice in the heart of Cornwall.

Based in Truro, Cornwall's cathedral city, Lander Medical Practice is committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care while maintaining a strong focus on clinician wellbeing and work-life balance. We are looking for a GP to join our team of 8 partners and 4 salaried GPs, working a negotiable number of sessions, ideally 6 per week.

This role offers the opportunity to work in a highly regarded training practice, within a thriving Primary Care Network, supported by an experienced multidisciplinary team.

The successful candidate will provide high-quality general medical services to our practice population, delivering safe, effective and compassionate care.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Undertaking routine GP consultations and clinical assessments.
  • Managing acute and chronic conditions in line with best practice.
  • Participating in practice meetings, clinical discussions and service development activities.
  • Supporting education and training within the practice where appropriate.
  • Working collaboratively with the wider multidisciplinary team, including pharmacists, physiotherapists, paramedics, community services and Integrated Neighbourhood Teams.

Opportunities are available to develop special interests, teaching and research activities.

Lander Medical Practice serves a population of over 20,000 patients and is recognised as one of Cornwall's highest-performing practices, with excellent quality outcomes. We share modern premises with Three Spires Medical Practice, and together form a highly successful Primary Care Network.

We benefit from a well-established multidisciplinary workforce, including paramedics, pharmacists, physiotherapists, GP assistants and workflow administrators, helping to reduce administrative burden and support excellent patient care.

As a long-standing GP training practice and partner of the University of Exeter Medical School, we are committed to education, professional development and innovation. We offer regular clinical meetings, protected learning time and practice development days, alongside a supportive team culture that values collaboration, continuity of care and clinician wellbeing.

Located within easy reach of Cornwall's coastline and countryside, Truro offers an outstanding quality of life alongside excellent transport links and a vibrant cultural community.

The postholder will undertake anaesthetic duties in cardiothoracic theatres, cardiothoracic critical care and cardiology. The successful candidate will work a flexible, rolling rota with his cardiothoracic anaesthetic colleagues, and will participate in the on call rota.

This is a replacement appointment to join a dynamic team of specialised Cardiothoracic Anaesthetists at our tertiary centre. The successful candidate will be expected to deliver anaesthesiology for a wide range of cardiology and cardiothoracic procedures; trans-oesophageal echocardiography and will give direct care in the integrated cardiothoracic intensive care unit.

title: Consultant Orthopaedic - Complex Upper Limb Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for this full time Complex Upper Limb (Shoulder / Elbow / Wrist / Hand) & Trauma Surgery Consultant in Trauma & Orthopaedics, on a 10-11PA basis. This post is to join the existing Consultant Orthopaedic team based across two DGH sites at Hastings and Eastbourne. This post is initially on a locum basis, with a view to conversion to a substantive role.

The East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust (ESHT) provides a comprehensive service in orthopaedic specialties for the surrounding districts of Hastings and Eastbourne. The post is required to support the surgical needs of the elective and trauma patients and supporting/lead the multidisciplinary team based on the trauma wards to enhance the quality and recovery of patients following trauma episodes.

The Eastbourne and Hastings Hospitals have an integrated Trust for the past 13 years. In line with reconfiguration of our service, orthopaedic trauma has been centralised on the Hastings site with elective surgery continuing both sites.

The orthopaedic department has long standing links with both GKT Medical School in London and Brighton Medical School and we receive regular medical students within the Orthopaedic department from both institutions.

Potential AAC Date: 13th January 2027

  • KEY SPECIALTY RESPONSIBILITIES/INFORMATION:
  • Surgical care of Trauma & Orthopaedic patients.
  • Pre-op, perioperative and post-operative care of trauma and orthopaedic patients.
  • Maintaining the highest clinical standards in the management of patients on the trauma, elective, outpatient units and other clinical areas, as required.
  • To share with colleagues' responsibility for the day-to-day management of the Trauma & Orthopaedic patients within our unit, in line with national and local clinical guidelines.
  • Teaching and training of junior staff, medical students and Allied Health Professional
  • To have responsibility for ensuring active participation in continuing medical education (CME)
  • To actively participate in both departmental and Trusts matters concerning Clinical Governance and audit
  • To attend meetings as appropriate.
  • Fulfil duties of weekly timetables, including out of hours and weekend duties in-line with the Consultant of the Week (7 days) and on call night rota.
  • The post holder will be expected to record their findings and investigate appropriately, optimising their patients prior to their orthopaedic surgery or other treatment and maintain the patients' surgical care during their inpatient episodes.
  • The post holder will be required to attend the 8am daily Trauma meeting when on duty and may be required to present patients as needed.
  • The post offers excellent experience in all aspect of Trauma & Orthopaedic care.

A wide range of staff benefits are available to our staff including staff development, enrolment in the NHS pension scheme, auto-enrolment to our Temporary Workforce Service, access to nurseries at Conquest Hospital and Eastbourne District General Hospital, staff restaurants and on-site staff accommodation.

In addition to an internal Occupational Health department, all staff also have access to free psychological support through our confidential Employee Assistance Programme which is available to staff 24 hours a day 7 days a week. Onsite parking is available for a small administration fee.

There has never been a better time to join East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust, submit your application today.

title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Meddygfa Glan Cynon is seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Salaried GP to join our friendly, supportive and forward-thinking training practice in the heart of the Cynon Valley.

Working alongside experienced GP Partners and a skilled multidisciplinary team, you will provide high-quality, patient-centred care to a diverse and welcoming community. The role offers a varied mix of routine and urgent clinical work, opportunities to develop specialist interests, and involvement in undergraduate and postgraduate medical education.

We are committed to clinician wellbeing, continuity of care and professional development, offering a collaborative working environment, modern premises, EMIS Web, a working day aligned to BMA recommendations and genuine flexibility around working patterns.

Whether you are approaching CCT or are an experienced GP looking for a rewarding new opportunity, this is an excellent chance to join a practice where your contribution is valued and your career can thrive.

The successful candidate will provide high quality primary medical care to our patient population through a mixture of routine and urgent clinical appointments, including house calls and low frequency on call requirements.They will work collaboratively with the wider multidisciplinary team to deliver safe, effective and patient-centred care.

The role offers opportunities to develop individual clinical interests, contribute to teaching and training activities, participate in quality improvement initiatives and support the ongoing development of practice services. The successful applicant will be encouraged to work autonomously while benefiting from the support of experienced GP Partners and a welcoming clinical team.

This is a varied and rewarding position within a practice that values continuity of care, innovation and professional development.

Meddygfa Glan Cynon is a friendly, supportive and forward-thinking training and teaching practice located in the heart of Mountain Ash, serving the communities of the Cynon Valley. We are proud of our reputation for delivering high-quality, patient-centred care while maintaining a positive, collaborative and enjoyable working environment for all members of the team.

Our clinical team consists of five experienced GP Partners, Salaried GPs, Practice Nurses, Healthcare Assistants, Clinical Pharmacists and a wider multidisciplinary team. We foster a culture of teamwork, mutual respect and open communication, where everyone's contribution is valued and professional development is actively encouraged.

As an accredited teaching practice, we are heavily involved in both undergraduate and postgraduate medical education. Clinicians have opportunities to participate in teaching, mentoring and supervision activities, alongside developing their own specialist interests and clinical skills.

We operate from modern, well-equipped premises using EMIS Web and benefit from strong administrative and clinical support systems. We are committed to clinician wellbeing and work-life balance, with a working day aligned to BMA recommendations, a manageable approach to workload and a culture that recognises the importance of supporting one another.

title: Nurse
descriptionHtml:
Join our growing Lung Cancer Screening Programme and play a vital role in the early detection of lung cancer and other respiratory conditions.

Working across our mobile screening locations, you'll help identify patients at risk, support healthier lifestyles, and contribute to a service that is transforming lives through earlier diagnosis and intervention.

This is an excellent opportunity to combine your clinical expertise with patient education, health promotion and autonomous clinic management, all whilst enjoying a compressed working week of just three shifts per week.

  • Deliver virtual and face-to-face nurse-led clinics as part of the lung health assessment pathway.
  • Carry out comprehensive respiratory assessments and identify patients at increased risk of lung disease.
  • Refer suitable patients for Low-Dose CT scans to support early cancer detection.
  • Provide evidence-based smoking cessation advice and ongoing health education.
  • Promote healthier lifestyle choices and empower patients to take control of their respiratory health.
  • Recognise and escalate safeguarding concerns, red-flag symptoms and medical emergencies appropriately.
  • Maintain professional competencies and complete training requirements, including IRMER and ARTP spirometry accreditation where required.

InHealth is the UKs largest specialist provider of diagnostic and healthcare solutions, working in partnership with the NHS for more than 30 years to make healthcare better for more than 5 million patients each year.

For clinical colleagues, that means delivering high-quality care within modern settings, with state-of-the-art equipment across a wide range of community, hospital and mobile settings.

With flexibility, strong learning and development opportunities, and the chance to support people at important moments in their healthcare journey, you can build a rewarding career while making a real difference locally and nationally.

InHealth is a place where you're trusted to do your job well, supported by people who value your expertise and give you the space to act on it. Teams show up for each other, leaders back your judgment and help remove blockers rather than create them.

New opportunities open as we grow - whether that's progressing, moving sideways or taking on something different as your strengths evolve. And everything we do is focussed on making healthcare better - for patients, partners and the people delivering care.

Read more about us here: Who We Are - InHealth Group

title: Social Prescriber
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to recruit to the post of social prescribing link worker, to work within our primary care network multi-disciplinary healthcare team, providing 1:1 personalised support to people who are referred to them by team members and local agencies. The social prescriber will work across the practices who are part of the West Enfield Collaborative Primary Care Network: Winchmore Hill Practice, Abernethy House Surgery, The Town Surgery.

This post empowers people to take control of their health and wellbeing by giving time to focus on what matters to me. The social prescribing link worker will build trusting relationships with people, create a shared personalised care and support plan and connect them to local, diverse and culturally appropriate community groups, VCSE organisations and services. They will also work with a diverse range of partners to provide support to community groups and VCSE organisations involved in social prescribing.

This role helps people to work on their wider health and wellbeing, specifically addressing health access and outcomes and wider determinants of their health, such as debt, poor housing and physical inactivity, as well as other lifestyle issues and low-level mental health concerns by increasing peoples active involvement with their local communities. This approach particularly helps people with long term conditions (including support for mental health), people who are lonely or isolated, or who have complex social needs which affect their wellbeing.

employer: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: GP Cardiologist
descriptionHtml:
OUHFT seeks to recruit qualified GPs to be trained to deliver cardiology services as part of a unified team at one of a number of community locations in the region.

The roles are part time, and GP Cardiologists are asked to consider undertaking 1-2 sessions per week (with time off for annual leave, study leave and CPD). Full training will be provided, as will a shadowing programme at OUHFT.

This approach to community cardiology is highly innovative, and seeks to integrate primary and secondary care; to make care more accessible and closer to home; to improve patient experience; to improve outcomes and quality of care, particularly via the identification and holistic treatment of risk factors and co-morbid conditions - including mental health conditions - in patients with known or suspected heart disease.

Each clinic will be supported by a healthcare assistant and secretarial support, who will support you with administrative tasks and enhance the patient experience. Consultant cardiologists will act as mentors, and will be available for advice and help when you need it.

The GP will be a substantive employee of Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, and will have access to the resources of this tertiary centre cardiology service. It is anticipated that, when trained and where appropriate, GP Cardiologists will be able to refer patients directly for cardiac procedures, including advanced imaging, angiography, cardioversion, ablation and pacing.

Integration between primary and secondary care is widely acknowledged to bring advantages to patients and their families through, increased accessibility and improved patient experience; to health care economies through enhanced cost-effectiveness and better value; and to practitioners who may experience opportunities for enhanced professional satisfaction.

OUH seeks to appoint several GP-Cardiologists to develop our services to patients closer to home. Our approach to Community Cardiology is to recruit and train a of motivated, high-caliber general practitioners, who are committed to seeking high standards of patient care for those with known or suspected cardiovascular disease, and who are committed to enhancing both the patient experience of care, and the value created by the healthcare system.

The aims of the posts are

  1. To improve access to expert cardiovascular care
  2. To improve patient experience and provide care closer to home
  3. To enhance holistic patient assessment and treatment, particularly to improve the identification and treatment of co-morbid conditions, including mental health conditions
  4. To create value in the healthcare system by allocating resources effectively
  5. To strengthen primary care by enhancing interactions with secondary care and providing a wider variety of career paths for GPs.

GP Cardiologists will contribute to the management, organisation, governance, educational and academic programs of the clinical service unit. GP Cardiologists will attend and contribute to teaching sessions; will contribute to the intellectual development and academic activities of the department, and may contribute to teaching and training.

title: Consultant Child & Adolescent Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
City & Hackney Specialist Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service

6 PA'S (6 Sessions)

Consultant Child & Adolescent Psychiatrist

A Consultant Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist is required for City & Hackney Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service. These clinical sessions are located within our Behaviour Support and Outreach Pathway. These are long-established consultant sessions, with the vacancy having arisen following the previous post holder moving on to a new role.

The post-holder would be expected to provide Consultant input and clinical leadership to the Behaviour Support and Outreach Pathway three days per week as well as contribute the assessment clinic and the consultant duty rota. The role of the Consultant is to provide psychiatric assessment and treatment, contribute a psychiatric perspective, provide senior clinical leadership to the multidisciplinary team, offer consultation to other professionals and agencies and facilitate the development of the team and wider service.

Closing date: 15th November 2026

AAC panel date: TBC

A vacancy has arisen for an innovativeand enthusiastic Consultant Psychiatrist to provide senior clinical consultant psychiatry input and leadership to the Behaviour Support and Outreach Team in City & Hackney Specialist CAMHS. This post has arisen due to the previous post holder moving to a new role.

The role of the consultant is to provide psychiatric assessment and treatment where appropriate, contribute a psychiatric perspective, provide senior clinical leadership to the multidisciplinary team, offer consultation to other professionals and agencies and facilitate the development of the team and wider service. employer: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust
title: Specialist in Plastic Surgery (Skin)
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a specialist plastic surgeon to deliver dermatology skin procedures in an outpatient setting with 1 session a month in theatres. If you are looking for a specialist post where you can genuinely shape the future of dermatology in Shropshire, train your dermatology colleagues to expand their surgical scopes of practice, influence major service redesign and integration with our community partners, and be part of one of the most ambitious hospital transformation programmes in the NHS -- this is it.

Our Trust is on the brink of a once-in-a-generation change. Backed by £312 million of investment, the Hospital Transformation Programme will create:

o A single acute site at The Royal Shrewsbury Hospital, home to a new 30-bed Critical Care Unit, a modern Emergency Department, and a state-of-the-art Women's and Children's Hospitalo A dedicated planned care site at The Princess Royal Hospital, supporting high-quality elective surgery and improved patient flowThis is your opportunity to join us at the perfect moment -- early enough to influence the design and delivery of future services, but close enough to opening that you'll see your impact become reality.

Our dermatology service will be undergoing significant improvement. We are looking for a specialist grade who wants to continue this momentum -- colleagues who are energised by improvement, motivated by challenge, and excited to help shape a service that women and families can trust.

Main Clinical Duties include:

  • Undertake outpatient dermatology skin procedures.
  • Partake in the skin MDT as a core member.
  • Undertake 1 session per month skin surgery in theatres.
  • Provide support to the dermatology service and medical students by actively contributing to training and continuity of service.
  • To have excellent team-working skills with the abilities and professional attitude to work well in a multi-professional team.
  • The post holder will also contribute to service development. This may involve contributing to Ockenden recommendations, QIPs, audit projects, guideline updates or teaching and training. Including supporting the shift of elective activity out of a theatre environment and into an outpatient setting inline with GIRFT.
  • To deliver clinical and quality targets agreed both nationally and locally with clinical teams and commissioners.

The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust (SaTH) is the main provider of acute hospital services in Shropshire, Telford & Wrekin and mid Wales.

Our main service locations are the Princess Royal Hospital (PRH) in Telford and the Royal Shrewsbury Hospital (RSH) in Shrewsbury which are located 20 minutes' drive apart. Together they provide 99% of our activity. Both hospitals provide a wide range of acute hospital services including accident & emergency, outpatients, diagnostics, inpatient medical care and critical care.

Our Poppy's Promise Commitment

We believe that compassionate care sits at the heart of everything we do. Every member of our team -- clinical or non-clinical -- plays a vital role in ensuring that patients, families, and colleagues are treated with dignity, empathy, and respect at all times.

We expect all staff to demonstrate compassion not only through their words, but through their actions: by listening attentively, communicating clearly and kindly, and recognising individual needs, feelings, and circumstances of those in our care.

Effective communication is central to safe and high-quality healthcare. We value colleagues who take the time to understand others, explain information in a meaningful way, and respond to concerns with patience and understanding.

By joining our team, you are committing to uphold these values -- ensuring that every patient feels heard, respected, and valued, and that compassion is embedded in every interaction, every day.

title: Training Programme Director - Endocrinology & Diabetes (NCEL)
descriptionHtml:

descriptionHtml:

Working remotely for one programmed activity each week, you will bring specialist endocrine expertise to an experienced multidisciplinary service and provide advice on gender-affirming hormone therapy for the prescribing team. The role is primarily advisory and supervisory rather than one of routine direct patient management. You will support medical and non-medical prescribers with complex clinical decisions, strengthen prescribing governance and help develop evidence-based practice across the service. You will have scope to influence protocols, education and service development while working collaboratively with colleagues who are committed to person-centred care and continuous improvement. We welcome applications from consultants who want to use their endocrine expertise in a focused, clinically influential role. Job-share applications are welcomed.

You will provide specialist endocrine advice to the clinics medical and non-medical prescribing teams on medical readiness for GAHT, treatment initiation, adjustment, monitoring and ongoing management. You will advise on complex cases, including physical health comorbidity, treatment complications, atypical blood results, contraindications, clinical risk and uncertainty about treatment options. You will review cases submitted through the agreed referral process, provide documented specialist recommendations and contribute to multidisciplinary discussion when required. This includes advising on individualised care for people with non-binary gender goals and liaising with primary, secondary and specialist services where needed. You will contribute to the weekly hormone prescribing forum, offering case-based advice and teaching as time allows. You will also support the development and specialist review of prescribing guidelines, standard operating procedures, clinical protocols, shared-care agreements and teaching materials. The role includes supporting prescriber education and safe practice, and contributing to clinical governance, audit, quality improvement and service development relating to endocrine care and prescribing.

Our team is collaborative, values-driven, and committed to long-term relationships with patients and each other.

Please apply by submitting your CV with a covering letter letting us know why you want to work with us and your preferred days/times to work.

Please direct any questions to onewirral.cic@nhs.net

Closing date:Midnight 06/09/2026

    • Day-to-day, you'll:

      • Provide high-quality, person-centred care across the full scope of general practice
      • Support good care through the efficient use of digital tools for, clinical triage, repeat prescribing, clinical correspondence and test results.

Improving peoples health and wellbeing takes time. Fortunately, that is our purpose and passion here at One Wirral.

We collaborate across sectors and organisations finding areas that require extra assistance to reduce health inequalities helping to bridge gaps in health services and support. Our agile approach means we can help people through practical and innovative solutions that really make a difference.

Our Vision:Wirral is a place where everyone can live their healthiest possible life.

Our Mission:To remove barriers to health and wellbeing - targeting support where it's most needed for people to thrive. By partnering with local people and organisations, we shape solutions that promote long-term health and wellbeing.

Our Core Values are:

Working Together: We promote trust and collaboration, believing that working together achieves better outcomes for everyone.

employer: University Hospital of North Midlands NHS Trust
title: Consultant Musculoskeletal Radiologist
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity to join a team of 48 WTE Consultant Radiologists, including 8 substantive Consultants with sub-specialty interest in musculoskeletal imaging.

At UHNM the cross-sectional radiologists work closely with their colleagues in the Surgical and Medical Directorate through cancer MDT meetings and joint clinico-radiological meetings.

The successful applicant will share responsibilities to support the Trauma and Orthopaedics, Spinal and Rheumatology Departments through Multi-Disciplinary team meetings. Currently Spine, Rheumatology, Diabetes, Orthopaedic and Tumour MDTs are in place and there is rotation between all relevant radiologists.

Duties will include providing a comprehensive diagnostic and interventional musculoskeletal imaging service across the Trust. The post holder should be a dedicated clinician wishing to actively assist and further develop Musculoskeletal Radiology services in the Trust.

There is a well established skill-mix within MSK with a large number of advanced practitioners and consultant radiographers who report plain films, sonographers who perform and report MSK diagnostic US examinations and an advanced practitioner who reports knee and spine MRI exams.

As a MSK consultant radiologist at UHNM you will be working with some of the latest equipment available in a purpose built department.

UHNM is a tertiary referral centre for Trauma and Orthopaedics serving Staffordshire, Shropshire, South Cheshire and Wolverhampton. The Trauma and orthopaedics department has 28 consultants and 3 SAS and the spinal team has 9 dedicated spinal consultants and 1 SAS surgeon providing all aspects of trauma and orthopaedics and spinal services including deformity correction, oncology surgery and trauma. There is a huge demand for MSK intervention services for procedures including image guided injections, arthrography, myelography, biopsies, nerve root blocks and vertebroplasty and the post holder is expected to contribute to this type of work.

The department performs and reports approximately 400,000 examinations per annum, with a high proportion of complex imaging and procedural radiology.

A Community Diagnostic Centre opened in Spring 2026.

We use an award-winning PACS which allows for easy streamlined, efficient and trouble-free reporting from either centre utilising PACS based reporting.

The post holder will contribute to the delivery of a high quality radiology service within a busy imaging department providing both general and specialist services in diagnostics and interventional imaging.

You will contribute to the weekday on-call service on rotation with also a 1 in 8 rota for Saturdays or Sundays.

The job plan will include CPD SPA

We are the specialist centre for major trauma for the North Midlands and North Wales. Happy staff make for happy patients, and with the help of both we have put together a wide range of development and support packages aimed at ensuring that everyone at the Trust has the opportunity to fulfil their potential and meet their aspirations as well as the tools to provide great care.

UHNM is a tertiary referral centre for Trauma and Orthopaedics serving a population of approximately 1.5 million from Staffordshire, Shropshire, South Cheshire and Wolverhampton.

The Trauma and orthopaedics department provides all aspects of trauma and orthopaedics and spinal services including deformity correction, oncology surgery and trauma. There is a huge demand for MSK intervention services for procedures including image guided injections, arthrography, myelography, biopsies, nerve root blocks and vertebroplasty and the post holder is expected to contribute to this type of work.

The Haywood Hospital has specialist services for rheumatology and rehabilitation. The Rheumatology centre at the Haywood Hospital welcomes patients from North Staffordshire, Derbyshire and Cheshire. The Haywood hospital is a centre of excellence and has an active research team known nationally and internationally for its work.

title: Clinical Director for Obstetrics and Gynaecology
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced and inspirational Consultant Obstetrician and Gynaecologist to join Somerset NHS Foundation Trust as Clinical Director for Obstetrics and Gynaecology.

This full-time 10 PA leadership post offers the opportunity to shape the future of women's health services across Somerset at both Musgrove Park Hospital and Yeovil District Hospital.

As Clinical Director, you will provide strategic, professional and operational medical leadership across a broad portfolio including maternity, obstetrics, benign and acute gynaecology, specialist women's health services, diagnostics, workforce development and research.

Working closely with clinical, operational, nursing and midwifery colleagues, you will lead service transformation, quality improvement and workforce development to ensure the delivery of safe, effective and compassionate care for women, babies and families across the county.

This is a rare opportunity to influence strategy, drive meaningful change and leave a lasting legacy within one of England's most integrated healthcare organisations. We are committed to appointing the right individual and will work collaboratively to develop a job plan that reflects your experience, strengths and aspirations whilst ensuring the leadership requirements of the service are met.

We would be delighted to discuss the role, introduce you to colleagues across both sites and share our ambitions for the future of Women's Services in Somerset.

As Clinical Director for Obstetrics and Gynaecology, you will:

  • Provide visible clinical leadership across women's health services, fostering collaboration between Musgrove Park Hospital and Yeovil District Hospital.
  • Develop and deliver a clear county-wide strategy for Obstetrics and Gynaecology, aligned with Trust and system priorities.
  • Lead on quality, safety and clinical governance, ensuring learning from incidents, reviews, audits and patient feedback drives sustained improvement.
  • Support delivery of the Maternity and Neonatal Improvement Plan and provide strategic oversight of maternity, obstetric and gynaecology services.
  • Work with multidisciplinary teams to improve patient experience, access standards, elective recovery, cancer pathways and service performance.
  • Share accountability for workforce, operational, quality and financial objectives across the service.
  • Support recruitment, retention, succession planning and the development of future clinical leaders.
  • Lead transformational projects and pathway redesign across acute, community and primary care services.
  • Build strong relationships with patients, families, commissioners, education partners and regional networks to support the delivery of high-quality services.
  • Promote a culture of inclusion, innovation, research, continuous improvement and compassionate leadership.

At Somerset NHS Foundation Trust, we're committed to supporting our employees with a range of benefits designed to enhance your professional and personal life. We offer:

  • Flexible working options to help you balance work and life
  • NHS pension scheme for long-term financial security
  • Generous annual leave allowance to recharge and relax
  • A strong focus on career development to help you grow and achieve your potential

Additionally, you'll gain access to our Blue Light Card, unlocking exclusive discounts on shopping, dining, and leisure activities, as well as NHS-specific perks to support you both inside and outside of work.

We are proud to foster a diverse, skilled, and inclusive workforce, and we encourage applications from all backgrounds.

Why Somerset? Somerset offers the perfect blend of idyllic countryside, outstanding areas of natural beauty, and breathtaking coastlines, with vibrant cities like Bristol, Bath, and Exeter just a short drive away - and only two hours to London.

The region is home to excellent educational facilities, and with affordable housing compared to other parts of the country, it's a great place to build both your career and your future.

Somerset truly has it all - the peaceful countryside and cosmopolitan city life, with something for everyone to enjoy.

title: Consultant in Acute Medicine
descriptionHtml:
At Macclesfield District General Hospital we are are excited to welcome a Consultant Acute Physician to join a dynamic and forward thinking team. The successful applicant will join a team of 5 Consultant Acute Physicians during an exciting stage of growth and expansion for the service. With the guidance of our inspiring clinical team, this role will allow you the opportunity to enhance your skills, leadership and confidence while holding management and clinical responsibility for patients on the Medical Admissions Unit (MAU).

The new Consultant Acute Physician will join our outstanding team in the delivery of acute care across the Medical Admissions Unit (MAU), Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC), Acute Medical Receiving Unit (AMRU)and will support the Emergency Department staff with assessments of patients with acute medical problems. Your expertise will play a key role in leading and coordinating the junior medical staff to ensure that patients are assessed and admitted or discharged in line with Emergency Department targets.

The team is part of an exciting project in which an extension in the form of a receiving unit (AMRU) has been added to MAU in June 2026.

Offer of dynamic rostering / flexible work spread between General Virtual Ward (GVW), SDEC and AMRU (Acute Medical Receiving Unit). The role outlined will be pivotal in guiding the department toward our long-term vision and strategy of providing excellent care to the local community.

MAU / AMRU ward cover - Managing admissions and flow of between 30 - 35 patients per day.

Monday to Friday until 8pm, working as the Physician of the Day (POD) 1x weekly.

Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) cover - on call cover on Friday

Emergency department in reach

Weekend post take ward rounds.

Medical Sub-specialty interest OPD clinics

General virtual ward rounds

Play a vital role in the training, mentoring and leading of junior medical staff with the assessment and management of acutely unwell medical patients, and contribute to MRCP PACES teaching. Postgraduate medical training of foundation year doctors and speciality trainees while working towards GIRFT recommendations as well as Royal College frameworks for Acute Medicine patients.

To be able to work flexibly and provide high quality care with particular emphasis on:

  • Education and training of medical students, doctors and professionals allied to medicine including Advanced Clinical Practitioners
  • Demonstration and engagement with the principles of clinical governance. Maintaining robust systems for effective clinical audit in the specialty and general medicine, as appropriate.
