Care delivered the way it should be.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Haven Health are seeking a Salaried GP to join their team in Felixstowe for 6-8 sessions per week with flexibility to discuss working arrangements. We welcome applications from experienced and newly qualified GPs who share our commitment to excellent patient care, enjoy working collaboratively and are keen to contribute to a positive team culture.

We are looking for someone who is approachable, compassionate and adaptable, with a positive attitude towards teamwork and continuous improvement. The successful candidate will be keen to contribute to the life of the practice, share ideas and help us deliver the best possible care for our patients.

You will provide high-quality, holistic care to our diverse patient population, including routine consultations, the management of acute and chronic conditions, and preventative healthcare. You will also have opportunities to contribute to the ongoing development of practice services, pursue areas of clinical interest and become involved in teaching and quality improvement initiatives.

We are committed to supporting the next generation of GPs and helping our clinicians build rewarding, sustainable careers within our organisation.

If you are looking for a practice where you can develop professionally, enjoy working as part of a supportive team and make a real difference to your patients, we would love to hear from you.

  • Provide comprehensive general medical services to registered patients, including assessment, diagnosis, treatment and ongoing management of acute and chronic conditions.
  • Undertake face-to-face, telephone and online consultations, as appropriate to clinical need and practice procedures.
  • Prescribe safely and effectively, following current guidance and practice policies.
  • Refer patients to secondary care and other services where clinically indicated.
  • Provide preventative healthcare, health promotion, screening and appropriate monitoring of long-term conditions.
  • Recognise and manage urgent and emergency presentations appropriately.
  • Maintain accurate, contemporaneous and confidential clinical records using the practice clinical system.
  • Support patients with complex needs, working collaboratively with the wider multidisciplinary team.
  • Duty doctor sessions
  • Minimal home visiting as a paramedic team is available
  • Clinical lead for an aligned Care Home

Suffolk Primary Care (SPC) is a forward-thinking partnership of GP surgeries across Suffolk. Our collaborative approach enables doctors and staff to share resources, ensuring the continued delivery of high-quality healthcare.

Why Join Haven Health ?

  • A supportive team: Work alongside an approachable partnership, experienced clinicians and highly trained multidisciplinary teams
  • A focus on clinical care: Benefit from well-developed systems and workflows designed to reduce administrative burden and support efficient working
  • Professional development: As a teaching practice covering a full range of specialties, we encourage learning, teaching and the development of individual interests.
  • A high achieving practice: We are proud of our strong QOF performance and high patient ratings.
  • Support at every stage: Whether you are experienced GP or newly qualified, we offer in-house learning and ongoing support to help you develop your skills and achieve your career ambitions.
  • A sustainable working pattern: We value work-life balance and aim to provide a positive environment where our GP's feel supported and able to thrive.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Greenwich Home Treatment Team
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen to join Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust as a valued Consultant based at Oxleas House, providing medical input into the Home Treatment Team in Greenwich.

The home treatment team is a busy multidisciplinary service providing acute treatment to adult patients with a range of mental health diagnosis and psychosocial stressors across the borough of Greenwich. There is an additional home treatment team that will cover older adults over the age of 65 but the three boroughs' for the Trust; Bexley, Bromley and Greenwich general adult mental health HTTs support this and with this in mind there may at times be patients on the general adult HTT workload who will be >65 years of age. The caseload size varies and is not capped, please refer to the Job Description with details on the referrals made to the team for the last few months. Greenwich HTT as part of Trust acute and crisis service line will work in close liaison with Bromley and Bexley HTTs.

The post-holder will work with other members of the MDT including but not limited to nursing, social workers and psychologists who will work together to monitor individuals' safety, providing a range of interventions and working closely with families and carers.

The team work closely with the other wards based at Oxleas House; Shrewsbury, Avery and The TARN and will be involved in the bed-management programme for the unit helping to facilitate discharges and help prevent unnecessary hospital admissions by working closely with community teams.

At Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust, we offer a wide range of NHS healthcare services to people living in South-East London and to people in prison across England. Our wide array of services includes community health care, such as district nursing and speech and language therapy, care for people with learning disabilities and mental health such as psychiatry, nursing and therapies.

Oxleas is a great place to work. It has been recognised as one of the Top 10 Best Places to Work 2023 by the Sunday Times amongst very big employers. Our staff survey results show that we are in the Top 5 in England and the highest in London for staff experience amongst similar trusts.

"We are always delighted to welcome new colleagues to the Oxleas family. We care about making Oxleas a great place to work - it's a big priority in our strategy. Come and join us - it's a place where our values, teamwork, equity, and wellbeing matter and where you can really help to improve people's lives."

title: GP ARRS (SDUC)
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking qualified GPs to work in Same Day Urgent Care at The Pembroke Centre in Ruislip / The Civic Centre in Uxbridge.

This is a position for qualified GPs to work in Hillingdon. The post-holder will manage a caseload and deal with a wide range of health needs in a primary care setting, ensuring the highest standards of care for all registered and temporary patients.

This post will require you to travel to The Pembroke Centre in Ruislip / The Civic Centre in Ruislip.

The Confederation, Hillingdon CIC works with General Practice and other healthcare providers to deliver its vision for Hillingdon to deliver the best primary care outcomes for patients in the whole of London. We are a not for profit community interest company. The Confederation works to develop and support individual GP practices, PCNs and Neighbourhoods and their changing needs. We deliver excellent clinical services ourselves both at scale and complementary to General Practice. We are the provider representative voice for local General Practice into the wider NHS and other Partners. We are of the NHS but independent, innovative and transformational.

The Confederation determines to develop as an attractive place to work, providing rewarding roles and opportunities to grow in order to attract and retain great staff that in turn delivers our vision.

Our Values

  • We work together to make a difference for patients
  • We care enough to go the extra mile
  • We support, trust, and empower
  • We sincerely value each other
  • We support primary care to own its destiny

employer: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside Integrated Care Board
title: GP Clinical Lead for Primary Care and Neighbourhoods
descriptionHtml:
Clinical leads are responsible for providing clinical leadership and support into the various aspects of the work of the ICB, playing a pivotal role in ensuring that strategic commissioning decisions, and service transformation programmes are underpinned by robust clinical insight and aligned with national clinical standards and specifications.

Clinical leads are required to build strong partnerships across provider collaboratives, local authorities, public health bodies, primary care, community services, voluntary sector partners, and local populations. The role supports the Executive Clinical Director in improving population health outcomes, tackling health inequalities, enhancing productivity, and ensuring value for money in line with ICS objectives.

Clinical leads must demonstrate exceptional leadership, clinical credibility and the ability to collaborate across complex system boundaries. This role is critical in enabling the ICB to fulfil its statutory duties, drive continuous improvement, and deliver high quality, joined up care for local communities.

Portfolio responsibilities may vary and adapt over time to respond to the needs and strategic priorities of the ICB/ICS. However, the postholder is expected to fulfil the key functions of providing clinical leadership across primary care, shaping neighbourhood models, integrated working, and population health improvement.

Whilst there will be areas you will be responsible for leading across Cheshire and Merseyside, most of your work with practices and neighbourhoods will be based in Liverpool City Region

NHS Cheshire and Merseyside serves a population of over 2.7 million people across nine localities, working with 16 NHS provider organisations, 51 Primary Care Networks, local authorities and voluntary sector partners.

We are proud of Cheshire and Merseyside's record of collaborative working and there are countless examples of brilliant care, but there are also examples of variation in service which only serve to exacerbate health inequalities.

Our vision is for everyone in Cheshire and Merseyside to have a great start in life and get the support they need to stay healthy and live longer.

We will do this by working together, as equal partners, to support seamless, person-centred care and tackle health inequalities by improving the lives of the poorest fastest.

Our values are rooted in the NHS Constitution, and we strive to create a compassionate, collaborative and innovative culture where staff can thrive and make a real difference to local communities.

title: Practice Manager
descriptionHtml:
The Alton Practice is seeking an enthusiastic, experienced and highly motivated Practice Manager to lead the operational and business management of our friendly, established GP practice in Roehampton, South West London.

This is an exciting opportunity for a confident and proactive manager to join our team and play a pivotal role in the continued development and success of the practice.

Working closely with the GP Partners, the successful candidate will take responsibility for the effective day-to-day running of the practice, providing strong leadership across operational management, workforce development, financial performance, regulatory compliance and patient services.

We are looking for someone who combines excellent organisational and interpersonal skills with commercial awareness, sound judgement and a genuine commitment to delivering high-quality patient care.

The ideal candidate will be an approachable, supportive and decisive leader who can motivate staff, manage competing priorities and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and service delivery.

Previous experience of general practice management would be highly advantageous, although applications from experienced managers with a strong NHS or healthcare management background will also be considered.

This is an excellent opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to a well-established practice serving a diverse local community.

The Practice Manager will provide effective leadership and management of all non-clinical aspects of the practice, working in partnership with the GP Partners to ensure the delivery of safe, efficient, high-quality and patient-centred services.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Providing effective day-to-day operational management and leadership of the practice.

  • Leading and supporting the reception team, including recruitment, staff development, appraisals and performance management.

  • Overseeing practice finances, budgets, payroll processes, income monitoring and financial efficiency.

  • Ensuring compliance with Care Quality Commission (CQC) requirements, NHS contractual obligations, information governance and relevant legislation.

  • Monitoring performance against the Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF), enhanced services and other contractual requirements.

  • Managing patient access, appointment systems, complaints and patient feedback to improve the patient experience.

  • Overseeing premises management, health and safety, IT systems and business continuity arrangements.

  • Maintaining effective relationships with the Integrated Care Board (ICB), GP Federation and other organisations.

  • Working with the GP Partners to implement the practice's strategic objectives, operational improvements and service development plans.

The successful candidate will be expected to work independently, demonstrate initiative and provide reliable, proactive management support to the GP Partners and wider practice team.

The Alton Practice is a well-established NHS GP surgery located in Roehampton, South West London (SW15), providing primary medical services to approximately 4,500 registered patients.

We are committed to delivering accessible, compassionate and high-quality healthcare to our diverse local population.

Our friendly and dedicated multidisciplinary team includes GPs, nursing staff, allied healthcare professionals and an experienced reception team. We aim to maintain a supportive, collaborative working environment where every member of staff is valued and encouraged to contribute to the ongoing improvement of our services.

The practice is a member of West Wandsworth Primary Care Network (PCN), working collaboratively with neighbouring practices and community services to improve healthcare provision and patient outcomes.

We are established teaching and training practice, hosting GP registrars as well as medical students from two different universities.

We are looking for a Practice Manager who shares our commitment to excellent patient care, effective teamwork, staff wellbeing and continuous quality improvement.

The successful applicant will work closely with the GP Partners and have the opportunity to make a significant contribution to the management, development and future direction of the practice.

Practice address: 208-210 Roehampton Lane, London, SW15 4LE

employer: The Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust
title: Specialty Doctor in Paediatrics
descriptionHtml:
The normal working day consists of covering the Paediatrics ward (C2) , Neonatal unit

(NNU) or the Paediatrics assessment unit (PAU) as per rota allocation as a level 2 doctor (Registrar level). You will also be doing out-of-hours including long days and night shifts as per rota schedules. During out of hours, you will be carrying the Tier 2 crash bleeps and attend any emergencies.

Providing resident doctors cover for the HDU

Running independent outpatient clinics and ward rounds with Consultant supervision

Undertaking rounds in wards and neonatal unit

Attending abnormal deliveries.

Admitting emergencies and booked cases and undertaking routine ward duties

The post holder will be required to participate in the Paediatrics, Neonates and PAU on-call rota and will be paid accordingly.

Working collaboratively with colleagues to further develop and improve the service and create a culture that is respectful, fair, supportive, and compassionate by role modelling behaviours.

Undertake duties on the ward and in the outpatient clinic.

adequately assess a patient's condition(s), taking account of their history, including

o symptoms

o relevant psychological, spiritual, social, economic, and cultural factors

o the patient's views, needs, and values

carry out a physical examination where necessary

title: Recovery Workers - Glasgow
descriptionHtml:
Join our team as a Recovery Worker in Glasgow.

Are you a compassionate and motivated individual who wants to change peoples lives? Our team in Glasgow is looking for four Recovery Workers to join them in providing high-quality recovery care to a diverse client group. If you are enthusiastic, creative and passionate about helping others, wed love to hear from you. The roles are based across our services in North East, North West and South Glasgow.

As a leading charity supporting people with drug, alcohol, and mental health challenges, we operate over 80 services across England and Scotland, providing free and confidential support to more than 100,000 people each year. Find out more about us on our website.

Closing date: 22nd November 2026. Please note: This role may close earlier than the stated deadline if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. All applicants must submit a CV along with a cover letter explaining why they should be considered for this role. Applications will not be accepted without a cover letter.

Our vibrant and busy services across Glasgow provide support to people concerned about their own or someone else's alcohol or drug use. We have three Recovery Hubs (in North East, North West and South Glasgow), however much of our work is carried out in the local community. We work with people at all stages on their journey providing both one to one appointments and group work.

We are looking for a enthusiastic and dynamic Recovery Workers who are motivated to work as part of a thriving and diverse team, ensuring recovery opportunities are available for individuals at any point in their recovery journey. You will strive to work collaboratively with partners and communities, ensuring that we are as accessible as possible and that the principles of a Recovery Oriented System of Care and true person centred practice are at the heart of all that we do.

Our Recovery Workers play a vital role in supporting clients to identify their goals, ambitions, and passions. Youll work with them to create the best treatment plan for their needs and to guide them on their path to recovery.

This role is permanent and will work 37,5 hours per week across 7 days, evening and weekend work will be required. As a Recovery Worker, we offer a starting salary of £26,250 per annum, rising each year in line with our pay progression salary bands, to £30,000 per annum.

WithYou provides free and confidential support, without judgement, to more than 100,000 people every year experiencing challenges with drugs, alcohol and mental health across England and Scotland. Our name reflects who we are - a positive place where people can progress, connect with others and get friendly, expert help in a way that's right for them. Our staff team changes lives. If you're passionate about helping people get the support they need for issues with drugs, alcohol and mental health, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Resident Medical Officer
descriptionHtml:
Planned Start Date: 01 April 2027

We are looking for an experienced and motivated Resident Medical Officer (RMO) to provide high-quality medical care for patients undergoing elective orthopaedic and spinal surgery within OHG Surgical Hub.

The successful candidate will provide continuous medical support to inpatients throughout their admission, working closely with consultants, anaesthetists, nursing staff and the wider multidisciplinary team to ensure safe, effective and responsive patient care.

This is an exciting opportunity to become part of a developing specialist elective surgical service committed to clinical excellence and outstanding patient outcomes.

  • Provide medical assessment and management of elective surgical patients throughout their inpatient stay.
  • Respond promptly to clinical concerns, patient deterioration and medical emergencies.
  • Undertake admission reviews, post-operative assessments and ongoing daily patient management.
  • Support the recognition and escalation of deteriorating patients using appropriate clinical pathways.
  • Liaise with consultant surgeons and anaesthetists regarding patient management and treatment plans.
  • Prescribe medications safely in accordance with local policies and national guidance.
  • Interpret clinical investigations including blood results, ECGs and diagnostic imaging where appropriate.

  • Participate in discharge planning and ensure appropriate follow-up arrangements.

One Health Group was established in Sheffield in 2004 and has steadily and successfully grown to become a significant healthcare provider in the region. Commissioned by the NHS, we provide services for patients referred for Orthopaedics, General Surgery, Spine, Urology and Gynaecology and with clinics located in over 30 locations across Yorkshire, Derbyshire, Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire and Lincolnshire, we bring healthcare closer to where people live. We are committed to clinical excellence, and our mission is to provide innovative, high quality medical and clinical services for our patients, optimising outcomes so they can quickly continue healthy lives.

The One Health Group PLC Elective Surgery Hub is a specialist purpose-built elective surgical facility providing high-quality care for patients undergoing major orthopaedic and spinal procedures.

Our service includes:

  • One operating theatre.
  • Three-bay recovery unit.
  • Twelve inpatient bedrooms.
  • Dedicated pre-assessment clinic and outpatient facilities.

We specialise in elective surgery including:

  • Total hip and knee replacement.
  • Revision arthroplasty.
  • Spinal procedures including:
    • Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF).
    • Cervical/lumbar decompression.
    • Lumbar discectomy.
    • Spinal fusions

Our aim is to deliver safe, high-quality elective surgical care through excellent clinical practice, multidisciplinary teamwork and patient-centred care.

employer: Honeybeerecruitment.com Ltd. trading as Military Medical Personnel (MMP)
title: Consultant in General Psychiatry
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Locum Doctor (Consultant in General Psychiatry) to cover an assignment with the Ministry of Defence (MoD), at Donnington DCMH, in Telford, Shropshire.

This is a locum role (40 hours per week) and the successful candidate will deliver an exceptional standard of care to the MoD service personnel.

Hourly Rate- £83.47 per hour

Job Description:

  • To undertake clinical sessions (remote and face to face) for the Department of Community Mental Health (DCMH), carrying out fresh case assessments and reviews of all service personnel referred to the DCMH. This will include liaison with referrers and line management as required to facilitate the clinical and occupational management of the patient.

  • Must have completed sufficient Continuing Professional Development (CPD) in accordance with Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on CPD.

About Military Medical Personnel and Our Benefits:

We are a contracted supplier to the MOD and have locum vacancies on military bases throughout the UK and occasionally overseas locations.

Military Medical Personnel offer an attractive package for candidates which may include the following:

  • Free mandatory training
  • Weekly payments

All job placements are subject to the receipt of satisfactory compliance requirements.

Please note that MMP is unable to sponsor work visas. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK, such as a valid visa with no restrictions on hours.

Due to the volume of applications received, only candidates who meet the essential criteria will be contacted regarding their application.

employer: Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:
The department works across all 3 hospital sites and is busy with daily trauma lists and other activity consisting of elective inpatient and daycases lists, fracture and outpatient clinics, and emergency department streaming clinics for minor injuries. The Trust also has onsite access to CT and MRI. The Trauma and Orthopaedic Department works very closely with the Rheumatology Department within the Trust and it is expected that any appointee will continue with this team approach

As a senior employee of the Trust the post-holder will work in close co-operation with, and support, other clinical, medical professional and managerial colleagues in providing high quality healthcare to the Trust's patients.

Integral to the responsibilities of the posts are the following requirements:

  • To provide effective leadership to all staff engaged in the specialty
  • To undertake all work in accordance with the Trust's procedures and operating policies
  • To conduct clinical practice in accordance with contractual requirements and within the parameters of the Trust's and Business Unit's services plans

The post would suit a good team player dedicated to high quality patient care. The opportunity exists to work in a non-hierarchical setting and offer a wide range of orthopaedic procedures in this busy Trust. The postholder must be prepared to work cross site to allow development of services across northern Lincolnshire and Goole.

We are looking for an orthopaedic surgeon who has subspecialty interests in hand and wrist surgery.

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

employer: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist with interest in Oculoplastics
descriptionHtml:
We wish to appoint a 12-month, fixed term Consultant Ophthalmologist, specialising in Oculoplastics, Lacrimal and Orbits, to cover a career break. The post holder will work within the multi-disciplinary teams providing and further developing elective and emergency care for ophthalmology patients within the general and subspecialty services, focusing on the provision and development of the glaucoma service to King's patients.

The post holder will develop and provide outpatient and surgical services for Oculoplastics, Lacrimal and Orbital patients from complex to routine. There will be commitment to the lid treatment and minor operations service with involvement in development, training and supervision. The timetable advertised, whilst indicative, is a fair representation of the needs of the service at this current time; however, reasonable adjustments will be considered. If there any aspects of the advertised job plan / timetable that you wish to discuss, please feel free to contact Danielle Moore, (daniellemoore2@nhs.net) or Bill Hartigan (william.hartigan@nhs.net).

The Trust provides a full range of local and specialist services across its five sites. Transforming Healthcare is the vision at the heart of the King's Strategy - 2026 to 2031. Together, we are pursuing six strategic ambitions: delivering high-quality patient care; being a great place to work; leading pioneering research, innovation and education; building strong and successful partnerships; providing timely and efficient care; and ensuring long-term financial sustainability. Achieving these ambitions will require all of us to work as one Team King's, united by a shared commitment to our values of being caring, collaborative, inclusive and innovative. By living these values every day, we will transform healthcare for our patients, our communities and each other

We are at a pivotal point in our history and we require individuals who are ready to join a highly professional team and make a real, lasting difference to our patients and our people.

King's is committed to delivering Sustainable Healthcare for All via our Green Plan. In line with national Greener NHS ambitions, we have set net zero carbon targets of 2040 for our NHS Carbon Footprint and 2045 for our NHS Carbon Footprint Plus. Everyone's contribution is required in order to meet the goals set out in our Green Plan and we encourage all staff to work responsibly, minimising their contributions to the Trust's carbon emissions, waste and pollution wherever possible.

title: PCN GP
descriptionHtml:
St Helens North PCN is seeking a motivated and enthusiastic newly qualified GP to join our Primary Care Network under the Additional Roles Reimbursement Scheme (ARRS), in line with the NHS Directed Enhanced Service (DES). This is an excellent opportunity for a GP at the start of their career to gain valuable experience working within an innovative, supportive, and multidisciplinary PCN environment.

Whilst this post has been advertised for full time, we would also welcome part time applications.

We are unable to accept applications from applicants who require Visa Sponsorship.

No recruitment agencies please.

The successful applicant will join our friendly Urgent Care Hub team, working alongside one other GP and the Hub Manager. The purpose of the Urgent Care Hub (UCH) is to support the increasing demand in general practice for same day / urgent care and provide patients with increased and improved access to urgent care.

You will work in partnership with the six practices that make up the PCN, as well as with other ARRS staff and partner organisations, supporting the care of patients requiring urgent same-day appointments. You will play a key role in helping to redesign and refine how we deliver care to these patients, contributing to improved outcomes and service efficiency.

The Urgent Care Hub (UCH) which runs Monday to Friday, 10am to 6pm aims to help meet the growing demand for same-day and urgent care within general practice, offering patients of the PCN enhanced and timely access to urgent medical services.

Please refer to the job description and person specification attached for full details.

As part of the PCN, you will collaborate closely with a diverse range of healthcare professionals, delivering high-quality, patient-centred care while developing your clinical skills and experience. The post holder will be an integral part of St Helens North Primary Care Network, a collaborative team comprising six practices: Garswood Surgery, Windermere Medical Centre, Bethany Medical Centre, Kenneth MacRae Medical Centre, Rainford Health Centre, and Billinge Medical Centre. Together, we serve a combined patient population of approximately 30,000.

Our PCN prides itself on being a friendly, close-knit team driven by a strong work ethic focused on motivation, productivity, respect, and innovation. This is a new and exciting opportunity to join an expanding and diverse Primary Care Network, dedicated to improving patient care while supporting your professional development and enhancing your clinical skills.

Our mission is to provide pro-active care to patients to improve their health and wellbeing and to make a positive impact to their lives, with respect and compassion. Working in partnership with local people, health and social care, voluntary sectors, community groups and colleagues to bring communities together and helping to reduce health inequalities.

title: Urgent Primary Care Doctor (GP) - Bank
descriptionHtml: Urgent Primary Care Doctor  Bank (Home Visiting) Bring urgent primary care to the patients who need it most - in their own homes. Urgent care is General Practice at its most immediate. Not every patient who needs urgent care can come to us. Some are housebound, frail, approaching the end of life or have been clinically assessed as needing a face-to-face review in their own home. What they need is an experienced doctor who can listen, assess, make confident clinical decisions and get them to the right care. At IC24, we're looking for Urgent Primary Care Doctors to work within our Home Visiting Service across Kent. You'll work alongside our drivers, dispatch teams and wider urgent care colleagues, providing safe, timely and effective care to patients in their own homes. If you enjoy the variety of General Practice, the autonomy of home visiting and the clinical challenge of assessing and treating patients in their own environment, this could be the role for you. What you'll focus on  Assessing and treating patients in their own homes You'll provide face-to-face assesAs an Urgent Primary Care Doctor (GP) - Bank, you'll provide urgent primary care to patients in their own homes, primarily targeting individuals who are housebound, frail, or approaching the end of life. The role involves making autonomous clinical decisions, assessing risk, and ensuring patients receive appropriate care and management. You will work within the IC24's Home Visiting Service alongside drivers and dispatch teams, administering safe, timely, and effective care. The position requires GPs to be experienced in face-to-face consultations, confident in autonomous decision-making, and skilled in managing complex cases in various home environments. Flexibility is important, as the role includes work during evenings, weekends, overnights, and holidays, responding to the urgent needs of patients. The role offers an hourly pay of £58.69 plus enhancements for unsociable hours, along with opportunities for professional development and participation in the NHS Pension Scheme.Integrated Care 24 (IC24) is a leading not-for-profit Social Enterprise committed to providing primary and urgent care services. Being patient-focused, IC24 aims to improve access to health and social care, thereby reducing pressure on secondary care services. IC24 provides a wide range of healthcare services, including GP Out of Hours, NHS 111, Primary Care, and Integrated Urgent Care Services. Serving over six million patients, IC24 works tirelessly to ensure patients receive timely and effective care, tailoring services to meet immediate healthcare needs. IC24 celebrates diversity and offers equal opportunities to all applicants, fostering an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and feel they belong. IC24 is dedicated to patient safety and operates with high clinical standards, ensuring staff meet regulatory requirements such as GMC guidance and strive for continuous improvement through learning and development opportunities. The organisation is headquartered in Ashford, operating several locations throughout Kent, such as Canterbury and Margate.

employer: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust

We regard this flexibility as essential if we are to continue to provide first class patient care in the future.   • 2.5 General Allergy clinics per week

  • 1 Challenge clinic per week

The Trust consists of St Thomas' Hospital at Waterloo, including the Evelina Children's Hospital, Guy's Hospital at London Bridge, Royal Brompton Hospital at Chelsea and Harefield Hospital at Harefield. We are also part of King's Health Partners (KHP), which comprises King's College London, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust and South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust. KHP is one of just five accredited UK Academic Health Sciences Centres (AHSCs). Through our AHSC, we are committed to making research and education integral to the delivery of high quality clinical care. The King's Health Partners Integrated Cancer Centre (ICC) is the vehicle for developing and managing cancer research, clinical services, and training and development across all the KHP partner organisations.

Our hospitals have a long and proud history, dating back almost 900 years, and have been at the forefront of medical progress and innovation since they were founded. We continue to build on these traditions and have a reputation for clinical, teaching and research excellence.

employer: South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Respiratory Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Consultant in Respiratory Medicine

10 PA CONTRACT

Current NHS Consultant Terms and Conditions

We are looking for a Respiratory Consultant to join our team in delivering high-quality respiratory medical services at University Hospitals of Tees. The successful candidate will have a subspecialist focus on TB, COPD and Pleural diseases.

The successful applicant will join the enthusiastic and well-established respiratory team to provide clinical sessions within the Department of Respiratory Medicine.

The primary base will be the James Cook University Hospital, Middlesbrough.

We support the'Making Every Contact Count'approach to behaviour change in the promotion of health and wellbeing of individuals and communities.

At University Hospitals Tees our main priority is, and always will be, to provide safe and high quality care to our patients every day; the kind of care we would want for ourselves and our loved ones. We want our organisation to be the best place to work with the right staff, in the right roles, at the right time, to ensure we deliver exceptional patient care and experience.

We will support staff through providing an inclusive and supportive workplace with health and well-being initiatives, staff benefits and opportunities for personal and professional development. Staff recognition is very important to us; as well as performance reviews and appraisals, we recognise staff through Star and Team of the month, colleague recognition - a note of thanks, Managers Awards, Shining Stars and Service Awards.

We support the Making Every Contact Count approach to behaviour change in the promotion of health and wellbeing of individuals and communities.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
This is a new consultant post created to provide medical leadership to Hounslow's new Intensive Outreach & Rehabilitation Service, which brings together the existing Community Rehabilitation Service (CRS) and a new Intensive Outreach (IO) function under a single clinical and operational structure, each delivered as a distinct pathway with a single Team Manager. The post holder will hold overall medical responsibility for the Intensive Outreach pathway working closely with the Consultant responsible for the Community Rehabilitation Service (CRS) pathway (already in post).

This is a full-time post of 10 programmed activities, made up of two components. Six PAs (0.6 WTE) are allocated to the Intensive Outreach pathway described above. The remaining four PAs (0.4 WTE) are allocated to the Hounslow Early Intervention in Psychosis (EIP) service, where the post holder will provide consultant psychiatrist input to the EIP multidisciplinary team.

Provide medical leadership for the Intensive Outreach (IO) pathway, working in partnership with the Band 8a Team Manager.

Undertake senior assessment and direct clinical input for the most complex cases within the IO pathway, including risk and medication management, diagnostic assessment, Mental Health Act assessments and CTO reviews.

Support the team's duty function for urgent concerns and assessments.

Provide consultant psychiatrist input and clinical leadership to the Hounslow EIP multidisciplinary team, working in partnership with the EIP Team Manager.

Undertake senior assessments and direct clinical input for more complex EIP cases, including diagnostic assessment, risk and medication management, Mental Health Act assessments and CTO reviews, and hold senior medical responsibility for care delivered by the EIP team.

Provide early, easy-access advice to GPs and Primary Care Networks under a liaison and consultation model, contactable by telephone or email during working hours.

Facilitate smooth transitions into and out of the EIP service, including transition of young people from CAMHS at 18, and onward transfer to MINT or the IO and CRS pathways where appropriate.

West London NHS Trust is one of the most diverse healthcare providers in the UK, delivering a range of mental health and physical healthcare and community services. The Trust runs Broadmoor Hospital, one of three high secure hospitals in the country, with an international reputation.

Our high secure services care for patients from South of England and we provide low and medium secure services across eight London boroughs. The Trust also provides mental and physical healthcare in three London boroughs (Ealing, Hounslow and Hammersmith & Fulham). We employ 4,500 staff, of whom 56% are BME. Our turnover for 2023-24 is £426m.

The Trust is rated as 'Good' overallby the Care Quality Commission. Forensic services are rated as 'Outstanding'.

The Trust is an established partner and contributor in the development of the evolving North West London Integrated Care System and the Integrated Care Board. The Trust leads the NW London Children and Adolescent Mental Health provider collaborative.

title: Health Care Assistant /Nursing Associate in Primary Care
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic and motivated qualified Health Care Assistant / Nursing Associate to join our team.

You will be joining a well-established successful nursing team of 2 ACPs, 1 trainee ACP, 2 very experienced Practice Nurses, 1 healthcare assistants who work in conjunction with a great wider team of clinicians, a very supportive management team, as well as administrative function.

The applicant must be a qualified HCA/ Registered Nurse Associate on the NMC register and must have the Nursing Associate foundation degree qualification.

The ideal candidate would work 25 hours per week ideally Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, but there is some flexibility around this.

You will provide and maintain a high standard of nursing care for patients, as well as providing nursing assistance to the Doctors and other members of the primary healthcare team.

The duties will include all tasks normally undertaken by a HCA/Nursing Associate working in General Practice, including health promotion, room checks (infection control duties).

We have 6 strong GP team which also includes 2 ACPs, 1 trainee ACPs,2 Practice nurses, Practice Pharmacist and Health Care Assistant who work closely to deliver care to our 10,500+ patient population. Our premises also house Community mental health and Social prescribing clinics. We practise from purpose-built premises with easy access to Manchester city centre and the North West motorway network. As an established training practice, we are proud to have trained Advanced Nurse Practitioners, Foundation year doctors and GPST trainees.

Closing date: 25th of November 2026

Band 3/4 depending on experience

We are keen to develop and support staff to excel their career aspirations whilst making a positive difference to patients and the community.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
Consultant Psychiatrist in Forensic Psychotherapy

6 Programmed Activities, 0900-1700 3 days or flexible of 4 days

We are looking for an enthusiastic and committed Consultant Psychiatrist in Forensic Psychotherapy with excellent clinical, interpersonal, and risk management skills, and who enjoys teaching, training and consulting to a wide range of colleagues, teams, and institutions within health, forensic and social care settings.

Candidates are requested to use the section "Supporting Information" on the application form to set out their reasons for applying and their suitability, referring to the person specification, for this post.

This is a six programmed activity (PA) Consultant Psychiatrist post to provide clinical services and contribute to the consultancy, teaching, and research activities of the Clinic.

Specifically, the post holder will provide assessments, individual and/or group psychotherapyfor patients, supervise a psychiatry specialist trainee in forensic psychotherapy, engage in the Clinic's other teaching and training programmes, offer consultancy to teams and organisations in the forensic field and engage in clinical governance, audit and outcomeresearch.

The Portman Clinic is a NHS England commissioned national specialist outpatient clinic offering psychoanalytically orientated assessment, treatment and management for children, adolescents and adults who suffer from problematic sexual behaviours or engage in delinquent, criminal or violent behaviour. Treatment offered is individual, group and couple therapy. The aim of the Portman Clinic is to develop a body of knowledge on criminality, sexual deviancy and violence through its clinical work and to disseminate this expertise through consultancy, teaching and training, research and publication.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist in Learning Disabilities - Carmarthen
descriptionHtml:
Join Hywel Dda University Health Board and play a key role in delivering and developing specialist Learning Disability Psychiatry services within one of the most picturesque regions of the UK, combining a rewarding clinical career with an exceptional quality of life. Working within a supportive and experienced multidisciplinary team, you will have the opportunity to provide expert clinical leadership, drive service improvement and make a meaningful difference to the lives of individuals with learning disabilities and their families.

Based in the heart of West Wales, this role offers the opportunity to combine a rewarding and varied clinical career with an exceptional quality of life. Hywel Dda serves the beautiful counties of Carmarthenshire, Pembrokeshire and Ceredigion, an area renowned for its stunning coastline, rolling countryside and welcoming communities. With award-winning beaches, national parks and excellent opportunities for outdoor activities, the region provides an enviable work-life balance for individuals and families alike.

The successful candidate will contribute to the future development of Learning Disability services, helping to shape innovative models of care, influence service delivery and support the Health Board's commitment to providing high-quality, person-centred care. The role offers the opportunity to engage in service improvement, education, leadership and multidisciplinary collaboration, while maintaining a fulfilling clinical practice.

The post holder will:o Communicate effectively with patients, families and carers, ensuring they remain central to all aspects of care and decision-making.o Manage patients with complex clinical presentations and provide specialist psychiatric expertise.o Maintain accurate, timely and high-quality clinical records in accordance with professional and organisational standards.o Liaise effectively with multidisciplinary teams and partner agencies to ensure coordinated care and positive patient outcomes.o Promote and apply evidence-based practice in all aspects of clinical work.o Participate in clinical governance, audit, quality improvement and patient safety initiatives.o Contribute to postgraduate education, teaching programmes, research activity and the supervision of trainees and other healthcare professionals.o Participate in departmental, professional and organisational meetings at local, regional and national level as required.o Work collaboratively with clinical and managerial colleagues to support the efficient and effective operation of services.o Contribute to the responsible use of resources in line with the principles of prudent healthcare.

Hywel Dda University Health Board plans and provides NHS healthcare services for people living in Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire, and bordering counties.

We have over 13,000 staff and together we provide primary, community, in-hospital, mental health and learning disabilities services.

We work in partnership with the three local authorities, as well as public, private and third sector colleagues, including our valued team of volunteers.

Our services are provided in:

  • Four main hospitals: Bronglais Hospital in Aberystwyth; Glangwili Hospital in Carmarthen; Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli; and Withybush Hospital in Haverfordwest
  • Five community hospitals: Amman Valley and Llandovery hospitals in Carmarthenshire; Tregaron Hospital in Ceredigion; and Tenby and South Pembrokeshire hospitals in Pembrokeshire
  • Two integrated care centres: Aberaeron and Cardigan in Ceredigion, and several other community settings
  • 47 general practices (six of which are health board managed practices); dental practices (including four orthodontic); 97 community pharmacies; 43 general ophthalmic practices; and 8 ophthalmic domiciliary providers
  • Numerous mental health and learning disabilities service

title: Associate Dean (South East)
descriptionHtml:
The role of the Associate Dean helps support the Postgraduate Dean in embracing corporate, statutory and non-statutory functions, aligning with the NHSE mandate. The role is focused firmly upon improving patient and learner safety and experience and ensuring effective educational outcomes.

The Associate dean is professionally accountable to the Postgraduate Dean and managerially by a deputy dean.This is a South East role and the exact balance of this role, and how it co-ordinates with other Associate Deans in the South East will be considered through the recruitment process.

Quality and safety

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

employer: University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust (279)
title: Anterior Segment Fellow in Ophthalmology
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited to a one year Anterior Segment Fellowship which is unique in offering exposure to two subspecialities: Cornea and Glaucoma.The fellow will gain experience in the medical and surgical experience in the management of glaucoma, cornea and the anterior segment. The candidate is expected to already be competent and independent in cataract surgery.

We are a small, friendly department and provide world class care in our two Ophthalmological surgical centres, at St Richard's, Chichester and Southlands Hospital which is a state of the art centre, built in 2017. There has been a substantial investment in the service in recent years to help us manage our workload.

Outside of work, West Sussex is an incredible place to live, offering a life on the South coast, with Southlands Hospital within walking distance of the sea. Life with us offers opportunities outside of work - please get in touch and come for a look around.

The post will involve travelling between the 2 sites on the basis of a set timetable, which may change after 6 months, depending on progress and departmental factors.

The doctor's timetable may need to be flexible, to allow for internal unexpected staff leave cover.

Participation in the on-call rota is expected 1:9

The post holder accepts that they will also perform duties in occasional emergencies and unforeseen circumstances at the request of the appropriate consultant, in consultation, where practicable, with their colleagues, both senior and junior. While it has been agreed between the professions that they will perform such duties, the Secretary of State stresses that additional commitments arising under this sub-section are exceptions and you should not be required to undertake work of this kind for prolonged periods or on a regular basis.Attend mandatory training updates as required.Undertake training as necessary in line with the development of the post and as agreed with the line manager as part of the personal development process.Achieve and demonstrate agreed standards of personal and professional development within agreed timescales.Identify own learning needs and jointly plan training requirements with your line manager

At UHSussex, diversity is our strength, and we want you to feel included to help us always put the Patient First. Your uniqueness and experiences will be part of our creative and innovative community where everyone is encouraged to succeed. We have a range of Staff Networks to help break down barriers, and can offer a buddy to help new members settle in. We're proud to be a Disability Confident Employer (Level 2) and a Veteran Aware Trust.

We treat our patients and staff with the same compassion and empathy we expect for ourselves. We're here for them when they need us, and we go above and beyond to meet their needs. This can be seen in ourWellbeing Programme for staff which is extensive and designed to support you when you need it, including where possible, flexible working to support work life balance - because we know that to look after others we must first look after ourselves.

As a university trust and a leader in healthcare research, we value learning, teaching and training so that we can be the best that we can be. From the moment you start with us and throughout your career we will help you to grow and develop. We hope that in choosing UHSussex you are choosing a long and happy career where you will be able to see the difference you make and feel valued for all that you do.

We look forward to receiving your application and the start of your journey with UHSussex.

title: Clinical Fellow in Endometriosis and Gynaecological Robotic Surgery
descriptionHtml:
The post is for a 6+ month period, and is due to become available to start as soon as possible. Applications are invited from a committed and enthusiastic doctor for the above post who will work within the BSGE accredited Endometriosis Centre at St Michael's, supported by the friendly and cohesive team. This post may suit candidates with various aims, including those looking to gain experience prior to applying for SITMs in Management of Complex Non-Malignant Disease or Robotic Assisted Gynaecological Surgery, gain first author publications in peer reviewed journals, learn specialist endometriosis ultrasound scanning and gain experience of advanced laparoscopic and robotic techniques including excision of rectovaginal disease. They will NOT have any on-call commitments and have 1 day per week protected for research, quality improvement projects or pursuing related areas of specialist interest. They will also gain experience in regular endometriosis, specialist endometriosis scan, reproductive medicine and general gynaecology clinics.

This post has no on-call commitment.

Annual leave and study leave are covered prospectively. As a valued member of the team you will be included in the educational and training activities of the unit and encouraged to contribute to the teaching of nurses, and other junior doctors. St Michael's Hospital is a large teaching hospital and is part of Bristol NHS Foundation Trust with close linked with the University of Bristol.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust brings together more than 28,000 staff to deliver over 160 clinical services across thirteen hospital locations,operatingfrom three main sites at Southmead, Bristol citycentreand Weston.

With an annual turnover of £2.3 billion, we are now one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom. Our hospitals are spread across Bristol and Weston, join us and you can enjoy the very best of both worlds; city living within a stone's throw of the countryside or beside the seaside, both with easy access to all that theSouth Westhas to offer.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust values all people as individuals. As an equal opportunities employer actively working towards a diverse workforce we aim to recruit andretaina workforce whichrepresentsthe rich diversity of the local population at all levels and are committed to designing our services around the needs of individual patients and those around them. title: Specialist Clinical Fellow in Intensive Care Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the above position at Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust, Wexham Park Hospital, Slough.

Applicantsmust have full registration with the General Medical Council.

Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust comprises two acute sites- the Wexham Park Hospital, Frimley Park Hospital and an elective centre, the Heatherwood Hospital in Ascot. The base site for this job will be Wexham Park Hospital.

Wexham Park Hospital is renowned for its excellent clinical care and friendly atmosphere. The Intensive Care department is funded to an acuity of 12 level 3 patients and has a team of 11 Consultant Intensivists supported by speciality doctors as well as intensive care and anaesthetic trainees. The Intensive Care Unit is accredited to deliver all stages of training as per the College of Intensive Care Medicine curriculum. The Unit was rated Outstanding as part of the latest CQC inspection (2025).

This Clinical Fellow post in Intensive Care Medicine (ICM) is aimed at anaesthetists or trainee intensivists with background interest in acute medicine, A&E and ICM.

The post is for 12 months with scope for extension upon discussion once in post.

All training and experience will take place in a department recognised by the Royal College of Anaesthetists (RCoA) for training in anaesthesia, by the College of Intensive Care Medicine (CICM) for ICM training and by the GMC. Training / experience is competency-based and follows the curriculum developed by the RCoA and CICM.

The post will last for 12 months and will be based at Wexham Park Hospital. The content of training and experience will be based on the competencies defined by the CICM.

The successful applicant will play a full role in the day to day running of intensive care, including the management of individual patients within and outside the unit.

In addition, they will also respond to resuscitation and trauma calls to the emergency department, adult and paediatric cardiac arrest calls.

Out of hours support for the Outreach service which is 24/7 and staffed with nursing colleagues is an essential requirement which allows the Fellow to demonstrate leadership and teamworking skills which need to be of a high standard.

The Fellow will take part in the speciality trainee level on-call rota, being on call for the intensive care unit usually as the senior trainee. There is a full shift resident commitment with internal leave cover.

We are also open to the option of the Fellow working the required out of hours component as weekend daytime shifts instead of nights. This will be agreed upon only following a discussion and mutual agreement of the job plan.

title: Respiratory LED Higher –  Solihull and Community Respiratory Services
descriptionHtml:
The Respiratory Registrar will support the delivery of safe, effective and patient-centered respiratory care for the population of Solihull and East Birmingham, with a specific focus on integrated working across acute, community, primary care, urgent community response, respiratory virtual ward and locality hub pathways. The post has been developed to strengthen the clinical interface between hospital respiratory services and community-based respiratory care, supporting earlier intervention, avoidance of unnecessary hospital admission and safe escalation where specialist consultant input is required.

The post holder will work in partnership with the Solihull Community Respiratory Team, Birmingham Community Healthcare Trust, Virtual Wards, Urgent Community Response, Locality Hubs, primary care colleagues, acute respiratory services and wider neighbourhood partners. The role will contribute to assessment, treatment planning, review and escalation for people with respiratory deterioration or complex respiratory need, including patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, bronchiectasis, breathlessness, recurrent chest infection and other long-term respiratory conditions.

The post holder will contribute to respiratory admission avoidance and care closer to home by providing registrar-level clinical input into multidisciplinary case discussion, virtual ward decision-making, community respiratory pathway coordination, diagnostics, treatment optimisation and step-up or step-down arrangements. The role is not intended to replace consultant respiratory oversight; rather, it will operate within a consultant-supported governance model, escalating complex clinical decisions appropriately and ensuring that patients receive the right level of care in the right setting.

The post offers an opportunity to work across an innovative integrated respiratory model within Solihull, supporting both reactive pathways for deteriorating patients and proactive approaches for people at risk of deterioration. The post holder will also contribute to clinical governance, audit, quality improvement, education and pathway development, ensuring that respiratory services continue to develop in line with UHB values, national clinical guidance and local population need.

title: General Practitioner with Special Interests-South Bristol Com Hospital
descriptionHtml:
The GP role is sat within the medical team as part of a wider Multi-professional service at South Bristol Rehabilitation Units - based in South Bristol Community HospitalYou will primarily support the medical function(s) of the service ensuring that;

  • Patients are medically optimised to engage within their rehabilitation and recovery whilst an inpatient
  • New patient deterioration is flagged and managed appropriately to ensure that patients receive the right care in the right place, whilst promoting admission avoidance where appropriate
  • Non-acute medical issues continue to be proactively managed within a CGA and stroke framework to continue the patient's recovery, support managing long term conditions and reduce the risk of patient deterioration on discharge from the inpatient unit.

The units consist two 30 bedded wards, aimed at providing a safe environment where individuals who are 'medically stable' can receive specialist rehabilitation along with focused therapy and support from our multidisciplinary team, to support independence before they return home.

One ward is specifically a Stroke step down facility and the other accepts admissions from all other clinical backgrounds.

The stroke specialist unit has direct input from a Stroke consultant twice weekly, so the role is on both units is specialist frailty GP role given the wider frailty of the cohort of patients on both units.

  • Provide senior oversight for the medical input for the cohort of inpatient service users within the ward.
  • Use broad medical knowledge to manage a range of clinical presentations that will sit outside of the regular cohort of conditions that are routinely managed within the Advanced Practice scope of practice and conditions regularly seen in primary care - including and not limited to; skin disease, rheumatological conditions and management of heart failure.
  • Use a holistic approach to ensure factors within the Biopsychosocial model are considered
  • To consider whether there may be any reservable factors contributing to presenting conditions, including a thorough review of medication, in conjunction with pharmacy colleagues.
  • Medicines optimization and de-prescribing to reduce burden of medication for older people.
  • Initiating further investigations for abnormal blood tests, ordering radiology interventions including X-ray, USS and CT scans.
  • Referring, if clinically indicated via 2 week wait for suspected cancer and referring or liaising with other specialist services within secondary care and specialist services.

title: Salaried GP - St Peters Surgery
descriptionHtml:
Invicta Health has a Salaried GP opportunity available at St Peters Surgery, with up to 4 - 6 sessions available.

Invicta Health has seven GP practices working within the organisation. We are a well-known community interest company, devoted to supporting and improving primary care in the Kent area.

We are looking for an enthusiastic and compassionate GP who enjoys a team focus in problem solving and also enjoys sharing knowledge. You will have excellent verbal and written communication skills and you will be an excellent listener. You will be on the General Medical Council's GP register, having passed the MRCGP (or equivalent) and gained a certificate of Completion of Training (CCT). An interest in teaching would be ideal, and the development of areas of special interest would be welcomed and nurtured.

As a Salaried GP, you would provide a wide range of primary care based general medical services to our patients in a non-judgemental, respectful manner, using a patient centred and fully team-based approach. Good communication between colleagues is essential to the role, as we routinely share our experience and knowledge within the practice in order to optimise patient care.

Home visits by the GPs are rare.

Invicta Health is a non-profit company, with a passion for primary care. We have a wide range of services such as hub-based GPs services, GP surgeries, services in Urgent Care Centres and A&E, a Community Primary Care mental health service, GP staff training service and the list is growing all the time.

We are formed by a federation of General Practitioners working in Canterbury and South Kent Coast areas of East Kent. Our aim is to provide local, high quality services for local people by collaborating with other established organisations in the health and social care community.

What perks can we offer you?

  • 90% indemnity reimbursement
  • Support for newly qualified GP's via new to practice programme
  • Support for fellowship opportunities
  • Opportunity to work within our local urgent treatment centres
  • Learning and Development opportunities
  • Tier 2 sponsorship
  • Approved blue light card provider
  • Salary Sacrifice Schemes
  • Company Car Scheme
  • Employee Assistance Programme

title: Consultant Radiologist with a Special Interest in Breast Radiology
descriptionHtml:
Make a real difference to breast imaging services across West Wales as a Consultant Radiologist with a specialist interest in Breast Radiology, joining a supportive and established team within Hywel Dda University Health Board.

We are seeking a Consultant Radiologist with expertise in Breast Radiology and experience in both general radiology and symptomatic breast imaging. This is an opportunity to join a team of 24 consultants and contribute to the continued development of radiology services across the Health Board.

We welcome applications from candidates interested in full-time or less than full-time working, as well as those wishing to focus exclusively on breast radiology. There is also the potential to undertake screening sessions as part of the Welsh Breast Screening Programme delivered by Breast Test Wales.

The successful candidate will be based at Bronglais General Hospital, Ceredigion, with occasional travel to Prince Philip Hospital, Llanelli and Withybush General Hospital, Pembrokeshire to support symptomatic breast clinics in line with service requirements.

Working alongside experienced radiology colleagues, you will play an important role in delivering high-quality diagnostic services and supporting the continued development of breast imaging pathways across the region.

This is a new post based at Bronglais General Hospital, Aberystwyth joining 1 Consultant Breast Radiologist, 1 Speciality Grade Doctor and 1 Consultant Radiographer providing breast radiology services to the population of Hywel Dda University Health Board. The post holder should be competent in mammography reporting, breast and axillary ultrasound, and image guided biopsy of the breast and axilla. It would also be desirable if the Radiologist has experience in additional procedures such as vacuum assisted biopsy/ excision, preoperative localisation techniques, Digital Breast Tomosynthesis (DBT) and breast MRI reporting. Experience of contrast enhanced mammography would also be desirable. The post holder will be expected to undertake symptomatic breast assessment clinics and actively participate in the breast MDT. Cross-site collaboration with respect to reporting or MDT meetings is usually done via Teleradiology and video conferencing. Office accommodation, secretarial support and full IT facilities including access to intranet and internet is provided.

Hywel Dda University Health Board plans and provides NHS healthcare services for people living in Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire, and bordering counties.

We have over 13,000 staff and together we provide primary, community, in-hospital, mental health and learning disabilities services.

We work in partnership with the three local authorities, as well as public, private and third sector colleagues, including our valued team of volunteers.

Our services are provided in:

  • Four main hospitals: Bronglais Hospital in Aberystwyth;GlangwiliHospital in Carmarthen; Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli; and Withybush Hospital in Haverfordwest

  • Five community hospitals: Amman Valley and Llandovery hospitals in Carmarthenshire; Tregaron Hospital in Ceredigion; and Tenby and South Pembrokeshire hospitals in Pembrokeshire

  • Two integrated care centres: Aberaeron and Cardigan in Ceredigion, and several other community settings

  • 47 general practices (six of which are health board managed practices); dental practices (including four orthodontic); 97 community pharmacies; 43 general ophthalmic practices; and 8 ophthalmic domiciliary providers

  • Numerous mental health and learning disabilities services

title: Phlebotomist
descriptionHtml:
Job description

The University Medical Group is a dynamic and high-quality practice caring for 32 000 patients. We operate over one site. We have a diverse patient population with around 9,000 student as patients.

Due to our large, registered list size we are a single practice PCN. This has enabled us to employ 3 Paramedics, 7 Pharmacists and a Physician Assistant to work as a multi-disciplinary team alongside the Doctors and Nurses .

The Nursing team consists of 3 Nurses, a Diabetes Nurse Specialist, 1 Nursing Associate and 1 Health Care Assistant. The team is supported administratively by a Care-coordinator.

Part time, Permanent. Working Monday to Friday 08:00 - 15:30 and one Saturday per month 08:00 - 12:00.

Main duties of the job

The main duties of the job are:-

  • Phlebotomy
  • BP monitoring.
  • Re-stocking of all clinical areas and maintaining stocks and keeping all areas clean.
  • To maintain and order clinical supplies.
  • Using appropriate templates in EMIS/Ardens for all procedures, training will be given in this area.
  • Any other duties that are deemed appropriate.

Being a centre of education is one of our objectives , therefore staff development is a priority to us . We also have student paramedics, PA students, Pharmacy students and two GP trainees . There is an in-house educational programme with protected time given to attend and a GP supervisor each day available for learners plus the Urgent care team consisting of a GP and paramedic for those patients who are more unwell. This enables all clinicians to be supported if they have any clinical concerns about their patients.

High quality patient care is our top priority, and we are pleased and proud to have achieved Outstanding from CQC in its last two inspections.

We are seeking an experienced, passionate, and motivated practice Phlebotomist to join our friendly nursing team who has experience in primary care.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Cuffley and Goffs Oak Medical Practice is looking to recruit a flexible, motivated and committed GP to join our friendly practice for six sessions per week, days to be decided.

Our practice is based over two sites (one mile apart from each other) in Cuffley and Goffs Oak, Hertfordshire which has accessible transport links into London. Access to own transport essential.

title: Salaried GP - fixed term
descriptionHtml:
Mount Farm Surgery is seeking a salaried GP to join our friendly, supportive, and well-established practice team on a 6 month fixed term contract to provide maternity cover from September 2026. We are flexible to sessions worked so please apply to discuss.

title: Consultant Gastroenterologist
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and experienced Consultant Gastroenterologist with a specialist interest in Clinical Nutrition to establish our Nutrition Support Team (NST) within a leading tertiary cancer centre. This substantive part-time post (5 PAs) offers a unique opportunity to focus exclusively on nutrition support, with no general gastroenterology, endoscopy, or on-call commitments.Based within the Nutrition and Dietetics Department, the successful applicant will work in close partnership with the Head of Nutrition and Dietetics and the Complex Artificial Nutrition Support Dietitian to provide clinical leadership for patients with complex nutritional needs, including cancer-related intestinal failure, malnutrition, enteral feeding, and parenteral nutrition.Working within a highly skilled multidisciplinary team, you will collaborate closely with dietitians, specialist nurses, pharmacists, oncologists, palliative care teams, and surgeons to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and develop a specialist nutrition support service within a world-renowned cancer centre while contributing to education, research, service development, and quality improvement. The role offers a predictable job plan and excellent work-life balance, making it ideal for consultants seeking a specialist leadership role in clinical nutrition

The postholder will provide specialist gastroenterology expertise to the Nutrition Support Team, supporting patients with complex nutritional needs requiring parenteral nutrition, and complex enteral feeding and including those with cancer-related intestinal failure and advanced gastrointestinal complications.Working alongside the Head of Nutrition and Dietetics and the Complex Artificial Nutrition Support Dietitian, the successful candidate will lead Nutrition Support Team ward rounds, outpatient clinics, and multidisciplinary discussions, ensuring safe, effective, and evidence-based nutritional care. They will provide expert advice to clinical teams across the Trust, support decision-making regarding home parenteral nutrition, and contribute to complex discussions around artificial nutrition, including palliative and end-of-life care.The role includes developing and enhancing the Nutrition Support Service, promoting best practice in line with national guidance, leading audit and quality improvement initiatives, supporting research activity, and delivering education and training to medical, nursing, pharmacy, and dietetic colleagues.We are looking for a collaborative consultant with expertise in clinical nutrition, excellent communication skills, and a commitment to multidisciplinary working and patient-centred care

The postholder will contribute to the delivery of high-quality consultant-led care across 7 days. This includes participation in planned weekend and weekday clinical activity to support safe, timely decision-making and continuity of care for patients.

The Christie is one of Europe's leading cancer centres, treating over 60,000 patients a year. We are based in Manchester and serve a population of 3.2 million across Greater Manchester & Cheshire, but as a national specialist around 15% patients are referred to us from other parts of the country.We provide radiotherapy through one of the largest radiotherapy departments in the world; chemotherapy on site and through 14 other hospitals; highly specialist surgery for complex and rare cancer; and a wide range of support and diagnostic services. We are also an international leader in research, with world first breakthroughs for over 100 years. We run one of the largest early clinical trial units in Europe with over 300 trials every year. Cancer research in Manchester, most of which is undertaken on the Christie site, has been officially ranked the best in the UK.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and dedicated GP to work alongside our clinical team to play an important role complementing and enhancing the Rise Park Surgery Team. This is a 4-6 session a week role; days of work by negotiation. We are open from 0700h on Wednesdays and Thursdays and every fourth Saturday morning and you may be required to cover these sessions occasionally.

We have recently undertaken an extension of our building and we are now looking for a like-minded team member to help us care for our patients. Successful applicants will be working in a brand-new clinical space which has been constructed and modified to our requirements.

We welcome applications from both experienced and newly qualified/early career GPs. We would support the successful applicant wishing to join the Phoenix program or who are on the GP retainer scheme.

Annual leave entitlement will be 30 days plus statutory bank holidays and 5 days study leave (pro rata). Additionally, your medical defence indemnity expenses will be covered by the practice for work undertaken at Rise Park Surgery.

Closing date for applications is 22 November 2026 however we reserve the right to close early if we receive sufficient applications for the role. Therefore if you are interested please submit your application as early as possible.

Please email your application (covering letter and CV) to David Marks at nnicb-nn.c84129.nhs.net.

The post holder will work as an autonomous practitioner, responsible for the provision of medical services to the practice population and delivering an excellent standard of clinical care (including being the duty doctor on call) whilst complying with the GMS contract.
