title: Consultant in Intensive Care Medicine and Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and experienced Consultant in Intensive Care and Anaesthesia to join the expanding team at Kettering General Hospital, part of University Hospitals of Northamptonshire (UHN). This is an exciting opportunity to work within a modern 16-bed Intensive Care Unit, with planned expansion to 20 beds, alongside a broad and varied anaesthetic service. The successful candidate will provide consultant-led critical care and anaesthesia, contributing to the delivery of high-quality, safe and compassionate care across the hospital. The role offers an attractive balance between Intensive Care and Theatres, with opportunities to develop specialist interests and contribute to teaching, research, quality improvement and service development.

The post-holder will provide daytime consultant cover within Intensive Care, including leading multidisciplinary ward rounds, supervising resident doctors and supporting the management of complex critically ill patients. They will also undertake general anaesthesia across a broad range of surgical specialties and participate in the 1:10 Intensive Care on-call rota, supported by resident ICU doctors and established outreach services. The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, clinical governance, audit, research and quality improvement, as well as supporting the continued development of the critical care and peri-operative services. This is an excellent opportunity to play an active role in shaping the future of the service as UHN progresses with critical care expansion, digital transformation and the HIP2 new hospital development.

University Hospitals of Northamptonshire (UHN) brings together Kettering General Hospital and Northampton General Hospital in a collaborative Group Model, providing opportunities to work across a progressive and developing organisation. We are committed to delivering safe, compassionate and clinically excellent care while creating an environment where our people can thrive, develop and make a difference.

Our Dedicated to Excellence values are at the heart of everything we do:

Compassion | Respect | Integrity | Courageous | Accountable

We are proud to offer a supportive and inclusive working environment, with excellent opportunities for teaching, research, professional development and service innovation. Joining UHN means becoming part of a forward-looking organisation with strong academic links, including our partnership with the University of Leicester, and an exciting future ahead as we develop our services and prepare for the HIP2 new hospital build.

employer: Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Hepatologist
descriptionHtml:
Our thriving and dynamic Gastroenterology department is based at Oldham, Fairfield and Rochdale, and is part of the Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust (NCA).

This is a unique and exciting time to join an NHS service that is focused on delivering the best healthcare services to our local population, demonstrated by recent investment in an award winning Community Diagnostic Centre in Oldham (CDC), away from the acute site.

This state of the art modular build has PET-CT (to be upgraded to one of the first digital PET CT scanners in the country), MR, CT, Ultrasound and physiological testing. It has been the focus of national attention, visited by the Prime Minister, Professor Sir Mike Richards & the National Clinical Director for Elective care. It recently won two HSJ Partnership awards and has featured in National news articles about diagnostics.

In Autumn 2024 the CDC will be enhanced further by a co located 3 room endoscopy unit with clinical rooms and on site decontamination. Our ambition at the CDC is to transform the way that we traditionally deliver healthcare and to explore new and innovative delivery models that reflect the needs of both our staff and our patients. There cannot be a better time to join our team.

We have an award winning Tertiary Inflammatory Bowel Disease Centre, led by Professor J.K.Limdi, recognised nationally and internationally for clinical services and research.

Team members have the opportunity to influence the development of services.

This subspecialty post is focused on expanding our dedicated Hepatology service line. The post holder will lead clinical governance for advanced liver diseases, drive the institutional expansion of non-invasive liver fibrosis screening, and manage specialized Liver MDTs and rapid hot clinic models.

The post holder will complement and develop existing services through the provision of specialist knowledge & expertise in Hepatology and General Internal Medicine. The post holder is therefore required to have full registration with the General Medical Council & a valid licence to practice and be on the specialist register (Gastroenterology and preferably also General Internal Medicine) or be within 6 months of CCT or equivalent at the time of interview.

Alongside the CDC, there are 3 endoscopy units across Oldham, Fairfield & Rochdale sites, making this one of the largest endoscopy services in the country. The Endoscopy service offers NHS Bowel Cancer screening colonoscopy, ERCP, HPB, EUS, advanced Lower GI EMR/ ESD.

The non elective inpatient services are centralised on The Royal Oldham Hospital site, the gastroenterology team provide gastroenterology in reach and outpatients at the 3 sites. There is an excellent, long established GI physiology department.

The Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust (NCA) provides hospital and integrated health and social care services to over one million people living across Greater Manchester. Our 20,000 colleagues care for people in hospital and in the community, working across Bury, Rochdale, Oldham, and Salford, to save and improve lives.As a large NHS trust we are committed to enhancing the health of our local population by delivering consistently high standards of care and collaborating closely with local authorities and key partners. We believe in our power and potential to make a difference and we are always looking for people who demonstrate our three core values - care, appreciate and inspire - to join our team.In return, we can offer you a job role with purpose and flexibility. The size and scale of the NCA means we can provide more challenge and opportunities so your career can always be moving in the right direction. By joining us you can also access a competitive benefits package, including, a fantastic annual leave allowance, flexible working opportunities and protected hours for health and wellbeing activities, helping you to achieve more personal downtime and a better work-life balance.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Salaried GP to join our friendly and supportive team at Walnut Tree Health Centre, working 4 to 8 sessions per week.

We are a growing three-Partner practice serving approximately 15,000 patients, with a strong focus on teamwork, mutual support and excellent patient care.

You will work alongside our GP team, experienced nursing and paramedic teams, and our wider Primary Care Network (PCN) team, including physiotherapists, mental health practitioners, social prescribers and clinical pharmacists.

We are looking for a GP who enjoys collaborative working and values being part of a supportive team. You will contribute to shared GP administrative responsibilities alongside your clinical work, with duties shared across the team.

We can offer:

  • 4 to 8 sessions per week
  • A friendly, supportive three-Partner practice
  • Approximately 15,000 patients and a growing list
  • Strong multidisciplinary team working
  • Experienced nursing and paramedic support
  • Access to a wide range of PCN professionals
  • Shared GP administrative responsibilities
  • Opportunities to contribute to practice development
  • A positive and welcoming working environment

We value our staff and encourage colleagues to share ideas, develop their skills and support one another. If you are looking for a practice where teamwork and high-quality, patient-centred care are valued, we would be pleased to hear from you.

The successful candidate will work as a Salaried GP for 4 to 8 sessions per week, providing high-quality, safe and effective medical care to our registered patients. You will work as part of our wider clinical team, making effective use of skills and expertise across the practice and PCN.

Main duties include:

  • Conducting face-to-face and telephone consultations.
  • Assessing, diagnosing and managing acute and chronic conditions.
  • Providing treatment, advice, safety-netting and follow-up.
  • Managing long-term conditions and contributing to preventative care.
  • Making appropriate referrals to secondary, community and primary care services.
  • Working collaboratively with GPs, nurses, paramedics, pharmacists and the wider MDT.
  • Supporting continuity of care and communication across the clinical team.
  • Reviewing investigations and taking appropriate clinical action.
  • Completing clinical correspondence and administrative work.
  • Contributing to shared GP administrative responsibilities, including prescription tasks.
  • Participating in practice meetings and service development.
  • Maintaining accurate clinical records and working within relevant guidelines.
  • Contributing to clinical governance, quality improvement and practice development.
  • Supporting a positive, respectful and collaborative working environment.

We are looking for a GP who communicates well, works effectively as part of a team and is willing to share the day-to-day clinical and administrative responsibilities of general practice.

Walnut Tree Health Centre is a well-established, supportive GP practice serving approximately 15,000 patients, with a growing list. We are a three-Partner practice committed to high-quality, patient-centred care and a positive working environment.

We work as a multidisciplinary team, with GPs, experienced nursing and paramedic teams, supported by our Ascent Primary Care Network (PCN). Our wider MDT includes physiotherapists, mental health practitioners, social prescribers and clinical pharmacists, enabling patients to access a broad range of expertise within primary care.

We are also a training practice, regularly supporting GP Registrars, F2 doctors on rotation and trainee nurses. We value the contribution trainees make and are committed to creating a positive learning environment where colleagues share knowledge, support developing clinicians and help bring the next generation of healthcare professionals into primary care.

We believe learning works both ways, encouraging all team members to share knowledge, reflect and continue developing their skills.

Teamwork is central to our practice. We encourage colleagues to share ideas, support one another and contribute to practice development. GP administrative responsibilities are shared across the team to support a fair and collaborative approach.

We are continually looking to improve our services, make best use of our multidisciplinary team and provide an excellent experience for both patients and staff.

descriptionHtml:

This is a fixed term post (until August 2027) to meet the RCPCH standards for Paediatric middle grade rota. Applicants with experience in general paediatrics/Neonates and specialty paediatrics who wish to consolidate or gain experience in general paediatrics are encouraged to apply.

Applicants will be supported in gathering the experience and portfolio evidence needed to support their applications to the GMC for portfolio pathway (previously CESR), or to add to their existing training experience".

The James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (JPUH) provides medical services for a population of approximately 230,000 living in South East Norfolk and North East Suffolk, plus a large number of visitors to the coast and Broads National Park during the summer months. In addition, it provides approximately a third of the secondary care teaching for the UEA Norwich Medical School. The Trust has foundation status and is highly regarded within the region.

The Trust is an equal opportunities employer and operates a no smoking policy.

employer: Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Paediatrician
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity to join the specialist Paediatric Palliative Care Teamand play a key role in the development of paediatric palliative and end-of-life care services across Birmingham and the West Midlands. The post combines direct clinical care for babies, children and young people with life-limiting conditions with the opportunity to support service development across the Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin (STW) footprint.

Working alongside an experienced multidisciplinary team of consultants, specialist nurses and family support staff, the post holder will contribute to the delivery of high-quality symptom management, advance care planning and holistic family-centred care across hospital and community settings.

This is a 5 PA locum consultant post offering a unique opportunity for an established paediatrician with an interest in palliative care to further develop specialist knowledge and skills within an accredited training centre. Depending on experience, there may be opportunities to work towards paediatric palliative medicine SPIN competencies under consultant supervision.

Applicants must hold full GMC registration with a licence to practise and demonstrate the skills and experience required to work at consultant level within paediatrics.

The successful candidate will provide specialist paediatric palliative care for babies, children and young people with life-limiting conditions across Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust and the wider West Midlands. Working alongside the existing consultant and specialist nursing team, the post holder will support children with malignant and non-malignant conditions across both hospital and community settings.

The role includes delivering expert symptom management, advance care planning and end-of-life care, whilst working closely with multidisciplinary teams, community services, hospices and other partner organisations. The post holder will also contribute to service development, education and the ongoing delivery of high-quality specialist paediatric palliative care across the region.

More information included within the JD.

Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust is the first of its type in the UK. Our Trust was formed in February 2017 to drive forward our commitment to provide the highest quality, world-class physical and mental health care for our women, children and families. Uniting our hospitals means more seamless care; more investment to make greater advances in our specialist treatment and world-leading neo-natal and fetal work. Importantly, it also gives us a greater voice in shaping the future of family-centred care.

Birmingham Children's Hospital is a UK leading specialist paediatric centre with an international reputation in several areas.

Birmingham Women's Hospital is one of two dedicated women's hospitals in the UK, with the busiest single site maternity unit, delivering more than 8,200 babies a year offering a full range of gynaecological, maternity and neonatal care.

Our Trust is committed to creating the best place to work. We believe in promoting and enhancing inclusion, diversity and equality and encourage applications from all areas of the community, who meet the criteria for the role, regardless of age, gender identity, disability, race, religion or sexual orientation.

title: Consultant Gynaecologist with interest in Early Pregnancy/Acute Gynae
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited to apply for the above post in the Gynaecology Department at the Oxford University Hospitals NHS Trust. The department is seeking a capable and motivated doctor who enjoys working in a tertiary referral service and wishes to effect change and improve care for patients within this service

The postholder will join an existing team of 18 NHS gynaecologists who together provide both a local gynaecology service to the population of Oxford and a highly specialist tertiary service in urogynaecology, reproductive medicine, endometriosis and Gynae-oncology. This post is a Trust wide position and may involve clinical sessions at the Horton Hospital in Banbury and the John Radcliffe Hospital sites, as well as the community based Early Pregnancy Assessment Unit (EPAU) in Rosehill, Oxford.

The aim of this post is to better align capacity with demand in general gynaecology and to provide additional consultant capacity in the urgent care service as well as high quality gynaecological ultrasound. The post also offers general and specialist clinics, and regular operating lists. Applications from candidates willing to participate in the termination service will be particularly welcome.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Trust provides gynaecology services across three sites (John Radcliffe Hospital Oxford, Horton Hospital Banbury and the Churchill Hospital, Oxford). The successful applicant will work across all sites. The post holder will be expected to undertake a combination of general gynaecology and specialist clinics. It is anticipated that the specialist clinics will be undertaken in Rosehill Early Pregnancy Assessment Unit

The post-holder will be expected to undertake theatre lists (the majority of the surgery undertaken is minimal access) at the John Radcliffe hospital.

The post holder will manage in-patients at the John Radcliffe Hospital and undertake gynaecology on-call duties of no more frequent than 1:10 paid at a Band A supplement. Competency should be maintained in diagnostic laparoscopy, management of miscarriage and ectopic for out of hours work.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest NHS teaching trusts in the country. It provides a wide range of general and specialist clinical services and is a base for medical education, training and research. The Trust comprises four hospitals - the John Radcliffe Hospital, Churchill Hospital and Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre in Headington and the Horton General Hospital in Banbury.

Our values, standards and behaviours define the quality of clinical care we offer and the professional relationships we make with our patients, colleagues and the wider community.

We call this Delivering Compassionate Excellence, and its focus is on our values of compassion, respect, learning, delivery, improvement and excellence.

These values put patients at the heart of what we do and underpin the quality healthcare we would like for ourselves or a member of our family. Watch how we set out to deliver compassionate excellence via the OUH YouTube channel.

In 2023NHS England launched its first sexual safety charter, and our Trust proudly signed it. We pledge zero tolerance for inappropriate sexual behaviour and commit to the ten core principles

Oxford University Hospitals promotes a safe, respectful hiring environment.

If you want to make a difference with us, come and join our team. Together, we will uphold the highest standards of care and professionalism.

descriptionHtml:

This is an exciting opportunity for a successful candidate to join a busy orthopaedic department at Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. The post will be based primarily at Basingstoke & North Hampshire Hospital.

The successful candidate will need be fully committed to the provision of high-quality orthopaedic knee service and will be expected to take a lead role in the department's current knee research portfolio.

The department has a strong track record in research with on-going industry funded projects and systematic reviews.

In addition to research commitments, there is a clinical role involving supervised and independent operating sessions, and outpatient clinics, forming part of a highly motivated multidisciplinary team. There may be opportunities to supplement the quoted salary with additional elective sessions and on calls as required by the department on an ad hoc basis.

This is an ideal opportunity for a post FRCS (Tr & Orth) surgeon to gain further specialist knee experience in a senior role before applying for a consultant post. The post holder must have FRCS (Tr & Orth) or equivalent, be on the Specialist Register or be within 12 months of completion of specialist training.

The clinical duties will include those normally expected in the Trauma & Orthopaedic Department of any large acute District General Hospital in the United Kingdom.

Our clinical staff have a continuing commitment to their patients and for the proper functioning of the Department. The post holder will be required to undertake administrative and managerial duties and exert leadership as necessary to fulfil this responsibility.

The post holder will be asked to cover a weekend on-call on an up to 1 in 18 basis. There will also be opportunities to contribute to the general on-call rota should individual applicants wish to do so.

Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (HHFT) provides hospital services to around 570,000 people living in Hampshire and parts of West Berkshire, and specialist services to patients from all over the country. We deliver a full range of district hospital services in a variety of locations.

title: Integrated Care Team GP
descriptionHtml:
Shore Medical is seeking an enthusiastic and compassionate Integrated Care Team GP to support our housebound and care-home population.

The post holder will provide proactive, coordinated care to patients with complex health needs, frailty and long-term conditions, working alongside the wider health and social care team. The role will focus on improving patient outcomes, reducing avoidable hospital admissions and supporting patients to remain safely in their usual place of residence.

We are looking for a GP who enjoys collaborative working and is committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care.

Job Type: Permanent Part Time

Hours: 4 Sessions per week

  • Provide comprehensive, person-centred GP care to housebound and care-home patients with frailty, multimorbidity and complex health needs.
  • Undertake proactive assessment, diagnosis, treatment, medication reviews and personalised care planning.
  • Work collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team, care homes, patients, families and carers to coordinate care and support safe transitions between services.
  • Identify patients at risk of deterioration, support anticipatory and end-of-life care, and reduce avoidable hospital admissions.
  • Contribute to population health, preventative care, quality improvement and proactive management of the PCN's housebound and care-home population.

Shore Medical is a GP Super Partnership with 6 practices across Poole and Bournemouth. We aspire to offer exceptional care to our 58,000 patients and are innovative in our approach to developing new teams and pathways to ever improve how general practice is delivered.

We have a friendly and supportive team of more than 200 staff, with over 40 GPs, Pharmacists, Paramedics, Nurses, Mental Health specialists and our range of administrative staff. We have a great social side to our team with Summer and Christmas parties, running and paddle boarding groups as well as many other events throughout the year.

The Practices in the Partnership are:

  • Lilliput Surgery
  • Poole Road Medical Centre
  • Wessex Road Surgery
  • Heatherview Medical Centre
  • Fernside Surgery
  • Parkstone Tower Practice

We offer

  • Competitive salary
  • Friendly and supportive working environment
  • Continuous CPD
  • NHS Pension Scheme with Life Insurance
  • Free parking at most of the sites
  • Cycle to work scheme
  • Refer a Friend scheme
  • Summer & Christmas parties

title: Pharmacy Dispenser - Bank/Flexi Contract

title: Speciality Doctor - Inpatients (Harbour Ward)
descriptionHtml:
Harbour ward is a 12-bed acute unisex inpatient unit based within the Berrywood Hospital. Harbour ward provides psychiatric care for patients, aged 18-65, with acute mental health problems. Patients can come from all trust areas and occasionally from other areas if the home area does not have capacity to admit their own. You will be supported in this role by range of junior doctors (FY2 and GPVTS), and it is expected you will have regular dialogue with the Consultant psychiatrists on other two adult inpatient wards onsite. Berrywood Hospital is a modern stand-alone 6 ward psychiatric inpatient unit and is staffed by a MDT including nursing staff, occupational therapists and psychologists. Cross cover will be provided by both inpatient and outpatient consultant colleagues on a rotational basis as is the system currently.

The Specialty Doctor will play a pivotal role in ensuring proactive, recovery-focused, individualised treatment plans are in place and being followed for each patient. They will be supported with a team of professionals who have been recruited specifically for this unit. Our intention is to have a short length of stay to manage only the acute phase of illness and support care in the least restrictive manner.

NHFT is an NHS Community and Mental Health Foundation Trust, providing physical, mental health and specialty services in hospital settings and in the community. We provide over 200 services across the county - as well as some specialist services in bordering and nearby counties. We work together with our partners to ensure that everyone who comes through our doors receives compassionate, person-centred care, regardless of their background or circumstances.

NHFT promotes a culture of learning, to improve the care and safety of our patients and colleagues. We have achieved our 'outstanding' rating by encouraging opportunity, innovation, development and growth across our workforce.

At NHFT we believe that work should be rewarded in every sense which is why we are proud to an accredited living wage employer.

We aim to support financial wellbeing and create an environment where are people feel valued and able to thrive.

title: Consultant in T&O Surgery with interest in Foot and Ankle
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Consultant in Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery with a specialist interest in Foot and Ankle to join our busy Trauma and Orthopaedic department. This is an exciting opportunity to join our friendly, enthusiastic and innovative team of orthopaedic consultants. Our region serves the population of Buckinghamshire, across the Stoke Mandeville and Wycombe Hospital sites. Most of the scheduled operating care is provided at Wycombe Hospital, with elective clinical work across both sites.

Applicants should possess FRCS (Tr & Orth) or equivalent, be registered with the General Medical Council and be eligible for inclusion in the Specialist Register. The successful applicant could start asap.

Please note - Applicants should be on the GMC Specialist Register. It is Trust policy that without CCT, an offer as Locum Consultant can be given for a 6 months fixed term contract, with possibility of it being extended for a further 6 months, but cannot go over 12 months in total.

Date of interview - 13/01/2027 Please see Candidate Pack for further information on the role and about our organisation:

https://buckshealthcare.pagetiger.com/consultant-in-tando-surgery/consultant-in-tando-surgery

This post will offer a great professional challenge, as we are looking to appoint a dedicated, visionary and enthusiastic individual to join committed, reputable teams to deliver high quality, compassionate care to trauma and orthopaedic patients at this exciting time. We pride ourselves on the high quality of our clinical care, leadership, quality improvement and innovation, pastoral development of a multi-professional team and - above all - on our team-working and cohesion.

The successful applicant will participate in a 1:12 trauma rota, and will join a team of 22 consultants. This is a Orthopaedic Consultant post attracting 10 PAs.

Elective surgery is carried out at Wycombe Hospital. There is a dedicated ward for elective orthopaedics in addition to a day surgery unit. The trauma service is based at Stoke Mandeville Hospital. The hospital has a designated Trauma Unit and provides acute surgical care to a population of 500,000. All trauma is centralised on the 'hot site' and this post will be working alongside a dedicated team of nurses, junior doctors, therapists and ortho-geriatricians to provide a first class, consultant led service. Two consultants manage the trauma service for a week rotating every 6 weeks, and this post will be working closely alongside a consultant colleague.

There is an excellent musculoskeletal radiology support with 24-hour CT scanning.

What do we stand for?

  • Our vision is to provide outstanding care, support healthy communities and be a great place to work.
  • Our mission is to provide personal and compassionate care every time.
  • Our CARE values are collaborate, aspire, respect and enable.

Applicants should be on the GMC Specialist Register. It is Trust policy that without CCT, an offer as Locum Consultant can be given for a 6 months fixed term contract, with possibility of it being extended for a further 6 months, but cannot go over 12 months in total.

employer: University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery
descriptionHtml:
University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust is seeking a skilled Consultant in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery with a specialist interest in Head and Neck Oncology. This is an exciting opportunity to join a friendly multidisciplinary team delivering high-quality, patient-focused care across Dorset.

This role supports the Trust's vision for transforming healthcare through the Dorset Clinical Service Review. The successful candidate will join us at a time when we have transitioned to delivering care across Emergency (Bournemouth Hospital) and Planned Care (Poole Hospital) sites, and be part of the development of the largest Elective Surgical Hub in the country.

The OMFS department serves the population of Dorset, providing a full range of services, including:

  • Head and Neck Oncology: Management of cancers, including sentinel lymph node procedures for melanoma.
  • Trauma and Reconstruction: Management of complex facial injuries.
  • Orthognathic Surgery: Correction of facial deformities.
  • Dentoalveolar Surgery and Oral Medicine: Including the management of chronic facial pain.
  • Head and Neck Melanoma Services: Delivered at Dorset County Hospital (DCH) and University Hospitals Dorset (UHD).

The service is fully integrated with multidisciplinary teams (MDTs) and supported by cutting-edge facilities, including 3D software, reconstruction technologies, and a milling machine.

The appointee will manage a varied clinical workload, encompassing inpatient and outpatient care, theatre sessions and multidisciplinary meetings, with a focus on head and neck oncology and reconstructive microvascular procedures. They will also participate in the emergency on-call rota ensuring comprehensive care for urgent and emergency OMFS cases, including microvascular and general surgery needs.

In addition to clinical responsibilities, the appointee will actively participate in teaching, training, and research initiatives. Opportunities include mentoring junior staff, teaching medical students, and collaborating with Bournemouth University to further educational and research objectives.

Candidates need to demonstrate broad experience in OMFS including head and neck oncology, the management of adult OMFS patients as well as excellent clinical skills and experience of clinical governance.

We are looking for someone who enhances our multidisciplinary team building effective working relationships amongst all colleagues from all professions, with the desire to continue to build on their organisational and leadership skills. Experience of change management is advantageous.

Our values define who we are as #TeamUHD. They underpin everything we do now and in the future. They define how we treat our patients, visitors, and each other, our valued teammates and colleagues.

UHD are investing in services across the Trust, with many being transformed and developed following merger and the New Hospital Programme.

This means that some services may move site this year or next, either temporarily or long term. Recruiting Managers interviewing for this role will be happy to answer any specific questions that you have about this at interview.

There is a planned move for this service anticipated during April 2027, when thisrole and base of work will relocate to Bournemouth site. Upon relocation of the role/service, excess mileage allowance / reimbursement will not apply, and any travel between the postholder's home and work base will be classified as a commute. Any other changes unrelated to this, will be handled in line with Trust/National terms and conditions.

As part of our commitment to delivering high-quality care across seven days, this post may involve participation in an out-of-hours rota, including evenings, weekends, and/or bank holidays, in accordance with service needs. Any work undertaken outside standard hours/PA's will attract remuneration in line with the respective NHS Medical and Dental Terms and Conditions of Service.

employer: Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist- Brookfield locked / Sutton End
descriptionHtml:
The Trust is seeking to recruit a consultant psychiatrist to join Brookfield Centre, a locked rehabilitation unit for patients with Learning Disability with or without Autism. This is a full time post and the post holder will be working at Brookfield Centre for 32 hours per week, and at Sutton End community residential placement in Maidstone for 8 hours per week.

The Appointee will be responsible for leading a multidisciplinary team on Brookfield Centre and provide care and treatment of 13 inpatients. This includes restricted and non-restricted patients. The post holder will also be responsible for overseeing the care and treatment of 5 patients at Sutton End, a community placement. The multi-disciplinary team on Brookfield Centre will comprise of the consultant, a speciality doctor, a clinical psychologist, a social worker, an occupational therapist, nursing staff, SaLT and a music therapist. There is also access to a senior pharmacist. The Appointee will act as a Responsible Clinician within a multidisciplinary team. As part of the multi-disciplinary team, they will take part in assessments of new referrals, pre-admission planning, management of inpatients and discharge planning. The post will require liaison with other agencies, including the Ministry of Justice, police, probation, social care and other mental health services.

The post holder will be the Responsible Clinician for up to 13 patients at the Brookfield Centre and provide psychiatric care during their admission. This includes participating in clinical team meetings and 6 monthly CPA reviews.

The post holder will also be the Responsible Clinician for up to 5 patients at Sutton End, a community residential placement with 5 beds for service users who have been discharged from the Tarentfort and Brookfield Centre. It is a joint initiative working with a private residential service provider to offer psychiatric and specialist support to this unit.

To manage, appraise and give professional supervision to Resident doctors as agreed between Consultant colleagues and the Chief Medical Officer and in accordance with the Trust's personnel policies and procedures.

To undertake the administrative duties associated with the care of patients.

To participate in annual job plan review and appraisal for Consultants.

To attend and participate in the academic programme of the Trust, including lectures and seminars as part of the internal CPD programme.

To work with local managers and professional colleagues in ensuring the efficient running of services, and share with Consultant colleagues in the medical contribution to management.

To maintain professional registration with the General Medical Council, Mental Health Act Section 12(2) approval, and to abide by professional codes of conduct.

We are Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust. We care for the mental health and wellbeing of people across Kent and Medway and are rated 'Good' by the Care Quality Commission (CQC).

Our teams support children, young people and adults with a wide range of mental health needs. We also provide specialist services, including all-age eating disorder services and neurodevelopmental assessments for children and young people, such as autism and ADHD.

Because we work across the whole county and across hospital and community settings, we can make care more joined up and easier to access for the people we serve.

Our vision is simple: we are here to help communities not just live with mental illness, but live well. It's why we're passionate about working with communities to make mental health care better for everyone. Everything we do is guided by our values: caring, inclusive, curious and confident.

Join us if you share our passion for better mental health care and want to be part of a team that's working well together.

employer: Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow NICU- London NTS Fellowship
descriptionHtml:
Job summary

An exciting opportunity has arisen for Senior Clinical Fellows aiming to achieve specialist registration in Neonatal Medicine through the Portfolio Pathway by rotating between a busy surgical neonatal unit (Chelsea and Westminster Hospital) and the London Neonatal Transfer Service. The programme is also open to candidates looking to gain valuable neonatal and transport experience via the Out of Programme (OOP) route.

The fellowship programme will run over a period of 1 to 2 years, depending on the candidate's needs and the availability of training spaces in participating hospitals:

a) 12 months: 6 months Chelsea and Westminster Hospital, 6 months London NTS

b) 24 months: 12 months Chelsea and Westminster Hospital, 12 months London NTS

It will include working across 2 hospitals: Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and the Royal London Hospital. Chelsea and Westminster Hospital will be the main employer, with honorary contracts offered when rotating to the London Neonatal Transfer Service (located at Royal London Hospital).

The programme consists of structured rotation through the 2 centres where bespoke educational supervision and support will be provided depending on the needs of the candidate. Both services provide care to a wide variety of patients including premature babies, surgical conditions and those with complex medical needs. There will be access to learning opportunities across clinical care, research, governance, teaching and risk management with a focus on helping candidates achieve the competencies and sign-offs they need for the Portfolio Pathway (previously called CESR pathway).

Chelsea and Westminster Hospital

Main duties of the job

Chelsea and Westminster Hospital is internationally reputable for their research excellence. C&W is home to the National Neonatal Research Database used for national and international population neonatal epidemiological studies.

Applicants must have middle-grade experience in Neonatology and be able to demonstrate competency in neonatal resuscitation, intubation and management of ventilated infants. The post holder will gain extensive experience in managing sick surgical infants.

The post would suit both UK trainees seeking out of programme experience/training to enhance their level 2/3 neonatal training and international trainees seeking a training opportunity that parallels UK grid training.

About us

Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is one of England's top-performing and safest trusts. We operate two main acute hospital sites--Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and West Middlesex University Hospital--along with award-winning clinics across North West London.

Our nearly 7,500 staff care for a diverse population of 1.5 million, providing full clinical services, including maternity, A&E, and children's services, plus specialist HIV and sexual health clinics. The Care Quality Commission rates us 'Good' in safety, effectiveness, care, and responsiveness, and 'Outstanding' in leadership and resource use.

We continually invest in our facilities, including a £30m expansion of critical care at Chelsea and Westminster and an £80m Ambulatory Diagnostic Centre at West Middlesex.

We welcome applications for flexible working arrangements, accommodating requests where possible to support our staff and patient needs.

The Trust is committed to equality and welcomes applications from all, regardless of background. Adjustments can be made for disabled candidates. Early application is advised as vacancies may close once sufficient applications are received. If you haven't heard from us within three weeks of the closing date, your application was likely unsuccessful. Employment is subject to a six-month probationary period.

Some roles may require weekend shifts at multiple sites.

employer: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Dermatologist
descriptionHtml:
This is a substantive replacement Consultant Dermatologist post based at Denmark Hill, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust. We are seeking an enthusiastic and committed consultant to join our friendly and dynamic multidisciplinary dermatology team within one of the UK's largest teaching hospitals. The successful candidate will play a key role in delivering high-quality general and specialist dermatology services, with a particular focus on medical dermatology. The Denmark Hill Dermatology Unit provides comprehensive adult and paediatric inpatient and outpatient services and is recognised for its specialist expertise in skin cancer, cutaneous infection, connective tissue disease, sarcoidosis, severe drug reactions, haematodermatology and complex medical dermatology. The department works closely with a wide range of specialties through established multidisciplinary clinics and regional networks, providing opportunities for service development, teaching and research. As a major teaching hospital and part of King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, the department has strong links with King's College London and offers excellent opportunities to contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate education, clinical research and innovation. The successful candidate will join a supportive consultant team committed to delivering outstanding patient care whilst continuing to develop and enhance specialist dermatology services.The post is based at Denmark Hill, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, and comprises 6 Programmed Activities (PAs). The successful candidate will provide consultant-led care across general dermatology and skin cancer services, delivering outpatient clinics and supporting the management of patients with a broad range of dermatological conditions. They will also contribute to dermatological surgery activity and participate in the departmental skin cancer and histopathology MDTs. The postholder will work closely with colleagues across the multidisciplinary team to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care and support the development of dermatology services at Denmark Hill. They will participate in the consultant on-call rota and contribute to clinical governance, audit, teaching and training of undergraduate and postgraduate healthcare professionals. As part of a leading teaching hospital, there will also be opportunities to become involved in research, quality improvement and service development activities.

The Trust provides a full range of local and specialist services across its five sites. The trust-wide strategy of Strong Roots, Global Reach is our Vision to be BOLD, Brilliant people, Outstanding care, Leaders in Research, Innovation and Education, Diversity, Equality and Inclusion at the heart of everything we do. By being person-centred, digitally-enabled, and focused on sustainability, we aim to take Team King's to another level.

We are at a pivotal point in our history and we require individuals who are ready to join a highly professional team and make a real, lasting difference to our patients and our people.

King's is committed to delivering Sustainable Healthcare for All via our Green Plan. In line with national Greener NHS ambitions, we have set net zero carbon targets of 2040 for our NHS Carbon Footprint and 2045 for our NHS Carbon Footprint Plus. Everyone's contribution is required in order to meet the goals set out in our Green Plan and we encourage all staff to work responsibly, minimising their contributions to the Trust's carbon emissions, waste and pollution wherever possible.

title: Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist with special interest in Glaucoma
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist with a special interest in Glaucoma to join the Ophthalmology team at Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust. The successful candidate will complement the existing glaucoma service, delivering outpatient, virtual clinic and theatre activity alongside consultant colleagues. The post holder will contribute to the provision of comprehensive elective and emergency ophthalmic care, including acute and general ophthalmology services, reciprocal leave cover and participation in the on-call rota. There will also be opportunities to contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, clinical governance, audit and research. The post is based primarily at the Queen's Medical Centre, with occasional work at the City Hospital campus. The successful candidate will join a large, supportive multidisciplinary department providing specialist and tertiary ophthalmology services to patients across Nottinghamshire and the wider East Midlands.The successful candidate will provide consultant-level care for patients with glaucoma and contribute to the wider delivery of elective and emergency ophthalmology services. The main duties will include:
  • Delivering specialist glaucoma outpatient clinics, including face-to-face and virtual review activity.
  • Undertaking glaucoma operating lists and associated pre- and post-operative care.
  • Providing general and acute ophthalmology services as required.
  • Sharing responsibility for the ongoing care of patients admitted under their care.
  • Participating in the consultant on-call rota and providing reciprocal cover for colleagues during periods of leave.
  • Supporting extended weekday, evening and weekend working where agreed through the job-planning process.
  • Contributing to clinical governance, audit, incident review, risk management, complaints, continuing professional development and evidence-based practice.
  • Participating in undergraduate and postgraduate teaching and supporting the development of resident doctors, fellows, nurses, optometrists and other healthcare professionals.
  • Working collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team to improve patient pathways, service efficiency and clinical outcomes.
  • Contributing to research and service development where appropriate.
Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust is one of the largest and busiest teaching trusts in the country, employing more than 19,000 colleagues and providing services across Queen's Medical Centre, Nottingham City Hospital and Ropewalk House. We deliver local services for Nottingham and Nottinghamshire alongside a wide range of specialist and tertiary services for patients across the East Midlands and beyond. The Ophthalmology Department is based within the purpose-built Eye and ENT Centre at Queen's Medical Centre. It is a large multidisciplinary service providing comprehensive general, specialist, elective and emergency ophthalmic care. The department includes 23 consultants and offers established specialist services across glaucoma, medical retina, vitreoretinal surgery, cornea, paediatric ophthalmology, neuro-ophthalmology, uveitis and oculoplastics. Facilities include four ophthalmic theatres, specialist diagnostic and laser equipment, a 24-hour eye casualty service and well-developed glaucoma shared-care pathways supported by specialist optometrists. As a major teaching hospital, NUH has strong links with the University of Nottingham and provides extensive opportunities for undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, clinical research, audit and professional development. The successful candidate will join a supportive consultant and multidisciplinary team committed to delivering safe, effective and innovative patient care.

title: Results Nurse
descriptionHtml:
Do you have a passion for results? Do you enjoy managing long term conditions providing excellent patient care in a non-patient facing role? Can you work as an individual and as part of a team? Then look no further.

Healthcare background ideally Nurse, Advanced Nurse Practitioner.

Confident with phone consultations with patients to discuss results and advise on lifestyle or medication changes.

Processing blood, urine and swab tests and results promptly and efficiently as they arrive electronically.

Arranging follow-up and recalls for patients if needed either on phone, text or with a member of the clinical team.

Counsel patients regarding their test results if further investigations or changes in management are needed.

Ensure ICE forms are ready for any repeat tests unless part of annual review or ad hoc diary dates.

Identify abnormal results which need GP follow up- either urgently that day by Duty Doctor if requesting clinician is not in that day, or by requesting clinician.

Complete and set up new diary dates for high-risk drugs which are being monitored.

Complete and set up diary dates for gestational diabetes, PSA monitoring and MGUS.

We are seeking Results nurse to join our fantastic team.

Appropriate training will be offered to the suitable candidate.

employer: Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: LED ST3+ in Obstetrics and Gynaecology
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen to appoint a Locally Employed Doctor (LED) - Obstetrics & Gynaecology (ST3+ equivalent) within the Maternity & Women's Services Directorate at Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust.

This post is aimed at doctors working at middle-grade level who are seeking to further develop their experience in Obstetrics & Gynaecology outside of a formal UK training programme. The role offers an excellent opportunity to working within a busy, consultant-led service, supported by senior clinicians and a well-established multidisciplinary team, within a forward-thinking and high-performing NHS organisation.

The successful candidate will work across the full spectrum of women's healthcare, contributing to the delivery of safe, effective and compassionate care in antenatal, intrapartum, postnatal and gynaecology settings, while providing senior clinical input and leadership appropriate to ST3+ level.

The post holder will work as part of the middle-grade Obstetrics & Gynaecology medical team, providing senior clinical care across inpatient, outpatient and emergency settings with and appropriate level of autonomy.

Duties include leadership of labour ward activity during shifts, management of complex obstetric and gynaecology cases, supervision and support of junior doctors, and participating in daily ward rounds, multidisciplinary handovers and safety briefings. The post holder will be expected to recognise and manage clinical deterioration, escalating appropriately to on-call consultants in line with Trust policies.

The role includes full participation in the middle-grade Obstetrics & Gynaecology on-call rota, including nights, weekends and bank holidays.

Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is a forward-thinking NHS Trust providing a full range of maternity, neonatal and women's health services to the local population. The Directorate is committed to delivering safe, compassionate and high-quality care, supported by a strong focus on multidisciplinary working, education and continuous improvement.

The successful candidate will join a supportive clinical team with access to senior supervision, structured induction and opportunities for learning and development within a consultant-led service.

employer: Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locally Employed Doctor ST3+ in Cardiology
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking to appoint 1 Cardiology Registrar. This is an excellent opportunity to gain experience working as part of a dynamic cardiology team across secondary and tertiary care. The Lancashire Cardiac Centre continues to expand with a large team of Consultants and Junior Doctors working together across sub specialities.

A provider of Tertiary Cardiac Services for the 1.6 million population of Lancashire and South Cumbria, in a newly commissioned £52 million Lancashire Cardiothoracic Hospital the Trust Executive Team and Divisional Cardiac Board are committed to expanding Cardiac Services and this appointment is seen as an integral step in this expansion.

The Cardiac Division provide a full range of Invasive and Non-Invasive Diagnostic, and Interventional Cardiology and Cardiothoracic Surgical Services, through four Catheter Laboratories and four cardiothoracic theatres with potential to expand.

Post holder will be expected to be part of the on-call rota

  • Duties and Responsibilities
  • Provision of in-patient care for the patients of all Consultants as required.
  • To provide on- call at middle grade level on a full shift rota.
  • Proficient in echocardiology
  • Support for diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in the Catheter Lab.
  • Supervision of specific exercise test sessions if required.
  • Attendance at Cardiology Clinics at the Lancashire Cardiac Centre at Victoria Hospital Blackpool. Assist in chest pain clinics
  • Dictation of discharge and clinic letters as required.
  • Occasional teaching of Nursing Staff and Junior Doctors and Medical Students

The Cardiac Unit comprises of the Cardiothoracic Unit and the Cardiology Directorate. The Division is housed in a £50 million purpose built hospital comprising of 4 catheter laboratories, 4 Cardiac and Thoracic Theatres, with potential to expand to 5, dedicated outpatient and non-invasive Cardiac Physiology investigation unit, 20 day case bed, 20 cardiac intensive care beds and 89 ward beds.

The Cardiology Directorate includes 2 wards - 37 and 39 for Cardiology patients and 4 Catheter Laboratories with day case facilities.

title: Consultant - General Medicine
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to recruit a dynamic Consultant doctor to support our General Medicine Department. East Cheshire NHS Trust has a real sense of energy and enthusiasm, and the Trust is committed to reducing the time people spend in hospital and strives to be a beacon of excellence.

The post will be based at Macclesfield District General Hospital.

Office accommodation will be provided and is usually shared with other senior clinical colleagues. Access to appropriate IT systems will be provided in the office accommodation as well as in the clinical areas.

Secretarial support will also be provided by a medical secretary, with typing of clinical correspondence supported by the clinical transcription suite.

10.5 PAs inclusive of on call.

The post holder will provide senior expertise within General Medicine. Be able to manage a full range of presentations in specific area of practice.An autonomous practice framework will be agreed along with this job description, which will outline the defined level of competency for the post holder in relation to independent and autonomous practice.

The post holder will be responsible for adhering to the generic capabilities' framework outlined nationally for Specialists. Please refer to Person Specification which details these competencies and how they should be evidenced.

In addition, the post holder will be required to undertake Hot Clinics in line with GIRFT recommendations, supporting earlier inpatient discharges and helping to prevent avoidable admissions. By providing expedited, senior-led outpatient or virtual follow-up reviews, Hot Clinic return appointments offer a safe and effective pathway for patients to be discharged sooner, contributing to reduced lengths of stay and improved patient flow.

The post holder will also be expected to deliver specialist outpatient clinics and contribute actively to the teaching and supervision of junior doctors and medical students, supporting both service development and medical education within the department.

NHS Medical and Dental salaries are set at a national level. For new starters not already working to UK Medical and Dental terms and conditions of service will be appointed to the minimum paypoint. The starting salary paypoint can only be increased when there is evidence of relevant, completed year's experience in terms of nature, type and level of role. The evidence required to increase a starting salary would be Payslips and details noted in the application form i.e. complete employment history

Please be aware that this post requires an Enhanced with Barred list Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check, the cost of which is payable by the successful candidate.

If you have lived or worked abroad for 6 months or more in the last 5 years you will need to obtain an overseas police clearance. Further information can be found on the additional information links at the bottom of the advert.

employer: Practice Plus Group - Health in Justice

employer: Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Endoscopist
descriptionHtml:
As a senior employee of the Trust the post holder will work in close co-operation with, and support, other clinical, medical, professional and managerial colleagues in providing high quality healthcare to the Trust's Patients.

To ensure the provision of a high standard clinical service.

employer: North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant in Emergency Department - HH
descriptionHtml:
At North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust, you will find excellent career opportunities to develop further your career. As a leading Consultant, you will play a major role in leading the development of a novel system of integrated emergency care at Hinchingbrooke Hospital.

The Emergency Departments at Peterborough City Hospital and Hinchingbrooke Hospital, which span two distinct acute hospital sites, are currently undergoing exciting development initiatives, including the implementation of a novel system of integrated emergency care and a system-wide approach to Frailty and Acute Medicine, which boasts one of the nation's most successful frailty services (Frailty CQUIN 2023).

We are encouraging and supporting you in developing special interests relevant to the specialty of Emergency Medicine e.g. ultrasound, paediatrics, elderly care, ambulatory care and critical care.

Our external partners will provide you with exciting development opportunities. We have established strong links with the Mid-Anglian General Practitioners Accident Scheme (MAGPAS) Helimedix and East Anglia Air Ambulance (EAA) with several Consultants and registrars working clinical shifts with them.

If you like to find more about the role and organise an informal visit, we are welcoming you to contact Dr B Natarajan- Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Clinical Lead for ED at Hinchingbrooke Hospital

The job plan is anticipated to contain 10 programmed activities per week. The Supporting Professional Activity shall be agreed at individual job planning. A minimum of 1.5 SPA is granted to start with, and additional SPA activity shall be made up by supervision of trainees, non-trainees, ACP's and Physician Associates.

You will be joining the consultant on call rota of 1:8, expected to cover for colleagues' absence from duty on the basis of mutually agreed arrangements with the Department and Employing Trust.

Your main goal will be to deliver clinical assessment, treatment and supervision to all patients' care requirements attending the Emergency Department until onward referral and discharge.

As an experienced consultant, you will provide clinical leadership and supervision for junior medical and nursing staff within the department. You will ensure adequate arrangements for hospital staff involved in the care of patients, to be able to contact them when necessary, and to observe the current local arrangements for advising details of leave.

By demonstrating your passion for providing outstanding care and clinical leadership, you will foster a positive and supportive environment that encourages the team to innovate and go beyond the call of duty, thereby enabling us to become a leading regional and national provider of emergency and acute care.

We are committed to promoting diversity and inclusion in our workforce and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, with a special focus on welcoming individuals from disabled, Black, Asian, and Minority Ethnic (BAME) communities, as well as those from our local area.

In line with our dedication to employee support, we offer a variety of benefits. For more information, please see the attached staff benefits leaflet.

We strive to create a supportive and inclusive workplace where employees feel valued and empowered to excel in their roles. Join us and become part of a team dedicated to making a positive difference in our community.

employer: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust
title: Trust Grade Registrar in Critical Care and Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
wE

We are seeking seven enthusiastic, experienced and highly motivated Trust Grade Registrars to join our Anaesthesia and Critical Care departments at London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust (LNWHT). These are exciting new posts created by the merger of our previously separate Ealing Hospital and Northwick Park/Central Middlesex rotas into a single unified, three-site rota. This change represents a significant expansion in clinical breadth for post holders, and a unique opportunity to work across one of the largest and most diverse Intensive Care and Anaesthesia departments in North West London.

The posts are primarily designed for doctors with established experience in Intensive Care Medicine who are capable of functioning as the senior resident registrar within a consultant-led critical care service. Successful applicants will participate in resident on-call rotas covering Intensive Care and Enhanced Care services across all three hospital sites. During out-of-hours periods, post holders will frequently act as the most senior resident doctor within the Critical Care service, supported at all times by an on-call Intensive Care Consultant.

Thi

The post holder will be expected to participate fully in the provision of a comprehensive Intensive Care and Anaesthetic service across all three hospital sites, accountable to the Clinical Directors?.

Critical Care Responsibilities

Participate in the resident on-call rota covering Intensive Care and Enhanced Care services across Northwick Park, Ealing and Central Middlesex Hospitals.

Function as the senior resident registrar within the Critical Care service, supported at all times by an on-call Intensive Care Consultant.

Assess, investigate and initiate management of critically ill patients presenting with respiratory, cardiovascular, neurological, renal, metabolic and infectious pathologies.

Anaesthetic Responsibilities

Provide anaesthesia and analgesia for patients undergoing elective and daytime CEPOD surgery across all Trust sites, exclusively under the direct, immediate supervision of an allocated Anaesthetic Consultant.

Post holders will not hold an anaesthetic on-call bleep. Out-of-hours commitments are entirely within Intensive Care and Enhanced Care services.

Undertake pre-operative assessments and provide post-operative care in the recovery room.

Advise surgical and pre-operative assessment teams on the preparation of patients for surgery.

London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust (LNWH) cares for the people of Brent, Ealing, Harrow and beyond.

Our team of more than 8,200 clinical and support staff serve a diverse population of almost one million people.

We run major acute services at:

  • Northwick Park Hospital: home to one of the busiest emergency departments (A&E) in the country. The hospital provides a full range of services including the country's top-rated hyper-acute stroke unit and one of only three hyper-acute rehabilitation units in the UK
  • St Mark's Hospital: an internationally renowned specialist centre for bowel disease
  • Ealing Hospital: a busy district general hospital providing a range of clinical services, as well as 24/7 emergency department and urgent care centre, and specialist care at Meadow House Hospice

We are a university teaching NHS trust, in recognition of the important role we play in training clinicians of the future and bringing the benefits of research to the public.

title: Consultant in Acute Medicine & Infectious Diseases
descriptionHtml:
Northumbria Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust's Department of Acute Medicine is looking to grow it's team and are seeking to appoint enthusiastic and committed Consultants in Acute Medicine and Infectious Diseases to join the team at Northumbria Specialist Emergency Care Hospital. Applications are welcomed on a full-time or part-time basis.

This is an exciting opportunity to work within one of the UK's leading emergency care hospitals, delivering high-quality, patient-centred care to adults presenting with a wide range of acute medical conditions. The successful candidates will play a key leadership role within a dynamic and innovative Acute Medicine and Infectious Diseases service, working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams to ensure the timely assessment, diagnosis and management of patients.

title: Transfer Doctor – Retrieve Adult Critical Care Transfer Service
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for ST5+, Specialty Doctors and Specialist Doctors in Intensive Care Medicine and / or Anaesthesia to join Retrieve, the South West Adult Critical Care Transfer Team as Transfer Doctors. The service is commissioned through Bristol NHS Foundation Trust and has two operational bases within the region.

Retrieve provides a single point of contact for all adult critical care transfer referrals 24 hours a day. All calls are managed by a Duty Consultant who triages, coordinates and can provide remote decision-support if required. Over the 24 hour period Retrieve operates a dedicated transfer team from each of its operational bases - one in Launceston, Cornwall, covering the Peninsula sub-region (Devon/Cornwall) and one in Bristol covering the Severn sub-region (Gloucestershire to Somerset).

We are looking for dynamic, and enthusiastic Specialty Doctors and Trainees to undertake adult critical care transfers working alongside Duty Consultants and Transfer Practitioners to deliver the day-to-day service. You will receive training and experience in transfer medicine with the aim of achieving autonomous practice status (with remote consultant supervision) during your time with the service. Following an orientation and induction programme in the first weeks of the role, Transfer Doctors will be initially directly supervised by Retrieve Duty Consultants. Transfer Doctors are expected to progress and undergo formal assessment following which, more distant supervision may be used, depending on the clinical case and Duty Consultant decision. The post is therefore suitable for a doctor with Intensive Care Medicine and/or Anaesthesia experience who has the appropriate skillset to assess, resuscitate and stabilise critically unwell adult patients (including deliver advanced airway management) with remote supervision.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust brings together more than 28,000 staff to deliver over 160 clinical services across thirteen hospital locations,operatingfrom three main sites at Southmead, Bristol citycentreand Weston.

With an annual turnover of £2.3 billion, we are now one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom. Our hospitals are spread across Bristol and Weston, join us and you can enjoy the very best of both worlds; city living within a stone's throw of the countryside or beside the seaside, both with easy access to all that theSouth Westhas to offer.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust values all people as individuals. As an equal opportunities employer actively working towards a diverse workforce we aim to recruit andretaina workforce whichrepresentsthe rich diversity of the local population at all levels and are committed to designing our services around the needs of individual patients and those around them. Anonymous information will be used from your applicationin order toensurewe'remeeting our pledge.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Bognor Regis (enhanced £45k RRP)
descriptionHtml:
We are pleased to offer an exciting opportunity to join Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust as a General Adult Consultant Psychiatrist within the Arun Neighbourhood Mental Health Team (NMHT), based in Bognor Regis. This is a pivotal senior medical and clinical leadership role, embedded within a dynamic multidisciplinary community team dedicated to delivering high-quality, person-centred care for adults experiencing mental health challenges.

The Arun NMHT is structured into two assessment and treatment teams--one serving Bognor Regis (this post) and the other covering Littlehampton and surrounding areas. Each team is aligned with local GP surgeries to support close collaboration with Primary Care colleagues. The Bognor Regis team benefits from the support of another Consultant Psychiatrist and a full-time Specialty Doctor.

You'll be part of a wider network of NMHTs across Coastal West Sussex, including teams in Chichester, Worthing, and Adur (Shoreham). Inpatient services are provided at Oaklands Centre in Chichester and Meadowfield Hospital in Worthing, with access to Amber Ward, a mixed PICU at Langley Green Hospital in Crawley. The area is also supported by two Crisis and Home Treatment Teams and a dedicated Enhanced Community Rehabilitation Service.

All services are consultant-led, and the successful candidate will be expected to work collaboratively with colleagues across these teams to ensure continuity of care and service excellence.

Arun NMHT is an integrated, multidisciplinary community mental health team providing specialist assessment and treatment for adults with complex and severe mental health needs. This is a key clinical leadership role within Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust, offering the opportunity to make a meaningful impact in a supportive and collaborative environment.

As Consultant Psychiatrist, your core responsibilities will include:

o Conducting specialist psychiatric assessments and delivering evidence-based treatments for patients referred to the service.

o Providing clinical supervision to junior medical staff and offering informal guidance to non-medical team members.

o Acting as the Responsible Clinician for patients subject to Community Treatment Orders, including attendance at Managers' Hearings and Mental Health Tribunals.

o Participating in Mental Health Act assessments for patients on the team's caseload.

o Liaising with inpatient Responsible Clinicians to ensure continuity of care.

o Collaborating with external services such as forensic teams, substance misuse services, and the local risk panel as required.

This role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to high-quality, person-centred care within a well-established and forward-thinking community mental health service.

Not only will you be working in a county with areas of outstanding beauty such as the south downs, and the 137 miles of coastline, along with exciting cities such as Brighton & Hove - the Trust also offers:

  • Recruitment & retention premia of £45,000; £15,000 payable upon successful recruitment and £10,000 payable at 12, 24 and 36 months thereafter. (subject to role and policy requirements; please liaise with Medical HR for more details - 0300 304 0393/ spft.medicalhr@nhs.net)
  • Relocation expenses up to £8,000 subject to role and policy requirements
  • Excellent NHS pension scheme .
  • 30 days study leave over 3 years with annual study budget.
  • Opportunities for flexible working and bespoke job planning.
  • Access to wellbeing support, staff networks, and Balint groups.
  • Monthly Medical Advisory Committees (MACs) which offer further peer support
  • Opportunities to engage in research, teaching, and quality improvement.

employer: Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board
